stories.title: Maulana questions Mohan Bhagwat’s appeal for 3 children:Points out muslims too don’t want more than 2 amid rising costs
stories.summary: In Bareilly, Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi asked which Muslim has 12 children and four wives. He added that Hindus can also have three, six, or even 12 children—there is no objection. He noted that due to rising inflation, even Muslims today prefer not to have more than two children, as educating a single child in a good school is already a challenge. This came in response to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s appeal in Lucknow asking Hindus to have three children. Maulana Razvi said that Muslims are often unfairly targeted in the name of population, which is wrong. This reflects a mindset that aims to single out Muslims. First read Bhagwat's appeal to Hindus... Now the complete matter in detail... Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Barelvi, president of the All India Muslim Jamaat, described the rising population in India as a serious problem. He said that instead of politicising this issue, all communities should collectively approach it with seriousness. The pressure of a growing population on resources is clearly visible and is a matter of concern for the future. Mohan Bhagwat’s statements on population and society Muslims living in India are also Hindus RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visited Lucknow on February 17–18. During a nearly two-and-a-half-hour meeting on Tuesday, he discussed social harmony and answered questions from various sections of society. Bhagwat expressed concern over dividing society by caste. He said that people should not get trapped in caste considerations. “Caste is something we have been trying to eliminate for decades, yet it persists,” he said. Future in danger due to declining Hindu population He urged couples getting married to have at least three children. “The purpose of marriage should be to continue creation, not merely to satisfy desires. This is the essence of duty,” he said. He added that Muslims living in India are also Indian, not migrants from Arab countries. The process of returning to Hinduism should be expedited. Those returning to the Hindu faith must be supported, while infiltrators should be detected, removed, and deported. They should not be given employment. Maulana: Having more children is not the solution Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi said that India’s population ranks second in the world. When a country or family has a high population, economic hardship follows. Regarding RSS chief Dr. Mohan Bhagwat’s statement that Hindus should have three children, he added that similar claims are made by people like Sadhvi Prachi. Such statements hold no relevance in today’s context. He said that even Muslims today do not wish to have more than two children. The cost of education, marriage, and livelihood has become high. Educating a single child in a good school itself is a challenge. Having more children is no longer practical, as meeting their basic needs is already a major struggle. Children are blessings from Allah, and every family has the right to decide according to their circumstances. However, a balanced approach to population growth is necessary in the interest of the country.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav advocates for smoking zones in prisons:Actor reveals struggle to quit cigarettes after Tihar release
stories.summary: Bollywood comedian Rajpal Yadav, released on 30-day interim bail in a cheque-bounce case, returned to his ancestral village Kundra in Shahjahanpur on Wednesday. Large crowds gathered to meet him. Speaking to the media, Yadav said, “Jail felt like a meditation camp for me. Just as every system in the country is being upgraded, prisons should also be modernised.” He suggested the introduction of smoking zones in jails to prevent others from being affected. “We are not promoting smoking, but since cigarettes are sold and consumed in the country, jails and correctional facilities should have separate areas for this. I myself am addicted and have tried many times to quit, but have not fully succeeded yet,” he added. Rajpal says - 600 crore people know me by name Claiming widespread popularity, Yadav said, “I have fans all over the world. Out of a population of 800 crore, around 600 crore people know me by name.” He described himself as a responsible actor in Indian cinema, capable of performing comedy, serious, and diverse roles. “Art is a science, and I consider myself a student of this science. For me, staples like wheat, lentils, rice, and farming have been the foundation of life. I have a deep connection with the village I am standing in. My real wealth is the hunger to live through art. Over the past 30 years, I never had to look for work because I lived my craft. All of this is the result of people’s blessings and support,” he said. Time spent in jail was like a 'Contemplation Camp' Yadav described his stay in Tihar Jail as a meditation camp. He emphasised that just as all sectors in the country are evolving, prisons should also be modernised. “The law is above everyone, and we are all subject to it. While the law delivers punishment, the conduct, behaviour, and character of inmates must also be considered. My wish is that at least 10 percent of convicts, who cannot appear in court repeatedly, should be given a new chance based on their good conduct. Thousands of such individuals can become assets to society. I am not suggesting who should be released or not, but this is a matter that deserves serious consideration,” he said. Upon reaching home, Yadav cuddled his dog. He added, “Hatred should be directed at sin, not sinners. Just as airports and railway stations have designated smoking areas, jails should also set up one or two zones per ward to protect others from second-hand smoke. I admit I am addicted to smoking and have been unable to quit despite repeated efforts.” Yadav owns a lavish home in Kundra village, Shahjahanpur. He last visited the village following the death of his father, Naurangi Lal. His elder brother Shripal and family also live in the village. Rajpal Yadav's luxurious house in the village... Reason for jail term In 2010, Yadav borrowed ₹5 crore from Murli Projects Pvt. Ltd. to make the film Ata Pata Lapatta, which flopped, leaving him in financial difficulty. He failed to repay the loan on time, and the cheques issued by him bounced, leading to a formal complaint. Despite an initial settlement, the full payment was never made, and accumulated interest increased the debt significantly. In 2018, Delhi’s Karkardooma Court found him guilty and sentenced him to six months in jail. He appealed in the High Court, receiving temporary relief several times after promising repayment. However, in early February 2026, the Delhi High Court refused to extend previous concessions, ordering him to surrender by 4 February. He complied on 5 February around 4 PM. Rajpal Yadav was released from Tihar Jail on 17 February 2026 on interim bail valid until 18 March. He had spent 12 days in jail for the ₹9 crore cheque-bounce case. Financial support during jail term Before surrendering, Yadav stated he had no money to repay the debt. After his detention, actor Sonu Sood appealed to the industry to support him, and several others, including Salman Khan, Ajay Devgn, and David Dhawan, extended financial assistance. Became Comedy King with films like Hungama, Hulchul Yadav gained fame for comedy in films like Hungama (2003), Garam Masala (2005), Chup Chup Ke (2006), Hera Pheri, and Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007), working extensively with director Priyadarshan in 8–10 films. He won the Yash Bharati Award, Uttar Pradesh’s highest civilian honour, for the 2003 film Main Madhuri Dixit Banna Chahti Hoon, recognising both comedic and serious performances. He was previously nominated for Best Comic Actor at Filmfare and IIFA but did not win. Early life and struggles After completing his training at NSD, Yadav moved to Mumbai with little support. He revealed that his first dream was simply to survive in the city. During struggles, he hosted meals for 20–22 struggling actors. Nawazuddin Siddiqui described Yadav’s home as a free community kitchen. Known as Chhotu and Buna by school friends due to his 5’1” height, Yadav started working at a village ordnance clothing factory at age 20. He married under family pressure at the same age. Personal tragedy Yadav’s first wife, Karuna, died 15 minutes after delivering their daughter Jyoti. He said, “I was supposed to meet her the next day, but carried her body on my shoulder. Enduring such pain at 20 is not easy.” He became a single father, with his mother and sister-in-law raising Jyoti. He later met his second wife, Radha, in Canada during the shoot of Hero: Love Story of a Spy and married her on 10 June 2003. Formed his political party in 2016 In 2016, Yadav launched the Sarv Sambhav Party (SSP) in Vrindavan, serving as General Secretary and star campaigner. The party’s motto was “Politics of dialogue, not controversy.” He swore an oath on religious texts and the Constitution. In the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the party fielded candidates in nearly 400 of 403 constituencies but achieved little success. Rajpal Yadav survived death 3 times In interviews, Yadav stated he survived three life-threatening incidents: nearly drowning in the Ganga, narrowly avoiding a bullock cart accident, and surviving an attack by wild dogs.

Kanpur police nab fake inspector with fake pistol:Car shows Lucknow Commissioner’s number, multiple CBI IDs seized
stories.summary: Kanpur police have arrested a man impersonating a police officer, who allegedly intimidated people using a toy pistol resembling a lighter. The accused, Sanjay Kumar from Unnao, reportedly wore a police uniform and had affixed a government vehicle number plate on his car to avoid suspicion. Police also recovered several fake ID cards of the UP Police and CBI from his possession. During interrogation, Sanjay claimed that the uniform and other equipment belonged to Durgesh, who posed as Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya’s PSO and had provided the official vehicle number plate. DCP Central Atul Srivastava stated that Sanjay Kumar was arrested for defrauding people under the guise of a police officer, promising jobs as well as transfers and postings. Police revealed that two accomplices, Durgesh and Vijay, have been identified and are under investigation. Used Income Tax Joint Commissioner's number plate Authorities recovered fake ID cards from Sanjay, some stamped with the DIG’s seal of the Police Training Centre, Unnao. Additionally, a fake lighter-type pistol and plastic cartridges were seized. His car, an i20, had a fake government plate (UP32EG2250) registered to the Lucknow Income Tax Joint Commissioner, while the vehicle’s real registration is UP35BK8203. Used to commit fraud in name of transfer-posting DCP Central Atul Srivastava further explained that police received a tip on Tuesday from Anwarganj police about a person in police uniform acting suspiciously. Officers reached the location and arrested him. During a search, the fake pistol and ID cards were recovered. Sanjay had been defrauding people by promising jobs and posting transfers, conducting fake interviews at hotels and schools. The gang reportedly includes two other men, whose details are being investigated. Fake inspector claimed - Durgesh Savita is Deputy CM's PSO Sanjay told the police that Durgesh, who poses as Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya’s PSO, owns the uniform and equipment. He claimed to have met Durgesh 7–8 months ago while commuting to Unnao, and denied committing any fraud himself. Sanjay stated that he used to work in towing vehicles but left the job around one and a half years ago. He added that Durgesh instructed him to use the fake government number plate as the vehicle’s installment was pending, while the real plate remained with Durgesh. According to police, Durgesh is currently absconding and has reportedly been terminated from his job. Authorities are continuing efforts to apprehend him and Vijay.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Rijiju alleges ‘Rahul is threat to national security’ Union Minister Kiren Rijiju alleged Rahul Gandhi poses a security risk, accusing him of links with anti-India elements and disruptive conduct in Parliament. He also criticised opposition protests against Speaker Om Birla and claimed Indian National Congress creates chaos there frequently. 2. Agra labourer waiter linked to Rohit Shetty house attack: Father says son stayed home, CCTV backs claim; village gripped by fear Five suspects were arrested for firing shots at filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s home in Mumbai, with police linking them to Lawrence Bishnoi’s gang. Investigators tracked them from Agra hideouts, alleging reconnaissance, planned attack and escape routes, while aides who sheltered them were also detained. 3. Pakistani woman lodged in Meerut's jail quarantine barrack: Son alleges Waqf property row led to FIR over two voter cards Faraz, son of jailed Pakistani national Saba Masood, claims false voter IDs were fabricated to frame her amid a dispute over alleged sale of Nadir Ali Waqf property. Police say she was arrested after verification and sent to 14-day judicial custody. 4. Biennial polls to 37 Rajya Sabha seats on Mar 16 Election Commission of India announced polls for 37 Rajya Sabha seats on 16 March across 10 states, including Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. Voting will use special pens, with nominations from 26 February and results the same evening. 5. Slogans of 'Bhagwat Go Back' raised in Lucknow University: Police forcefully shifted protesting students into jeeps and buses Protests erupted as Mohan Bhagwat arrived at Lucknow University, with protesters raising slogans and clashing with police. Several were detained and taken to Eco Garden. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief later attended events and spoke on law, society, religion, and population during his visit Wednesday. 6. BSP to go solo in 2027 UP polls says Mayawati: Rejects alliance speculations, terms them 'fake news and conspiracies' Mayawati said Bahujan Samaj Party will contest the 2027 polls in Uttar Pradesh alone, calling alliance rumours false. She accused Congress, Samajwadi Party and Bharatiya Janata Party of political motives and urged workers to stay focused. She dismissed speculation over her bungalow, citing security reasons. 7. Galgotias University flaunts Chinese robot as its own, sparks row Galgotias University was removed from expo after robot claim row; experts said its “Orion” resembled Unitree Robotics model. University admitted buying it. Rahul Gandhi criticised government, while posts on X carried notes flagging claims misleading after video went viral online, sparking fresh debate. 8. 3 girl aspirants faint during Agniveer recruitment running: Collapse after completing 4 rounds; 1000 girls joining Lucknow Cantonment At AMC Stadium in Lucknow Cantonment, three candidates fainted and several fell during a 1,600-metre run at a women’s recruitment rally. About 1,000 shortlisted participants from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand are attending the sixth phase after clearing the July 2025 CEE exam. 9. 1.86 lakh UP teachers face uncertainty over mandatory TET rule: 50k not even capable of giving exams; will Tamil Nadu model show the way? About 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh have yet to clear the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), while 50,000 lack minimum qualifications. The UP government has filed a Supreme Court review petition. Teachers’ unions plan protests if mandatory TET rules are enforced nationwide. 10. Salman's father Salim Khan suffers brain haemorrhage Veteran writer Salim Khan has been placed on ventilator at Lilavati Hospital after a minor brain haemorrhage. Doctors performed a DSA procedure and are monitoring him. Son Salman Khan, along with Javed Akhtar and Sanjay Dutt, visited as medical bulletin awaited.

stories.title: Inspector arrested while taking ₹75,000 bribe in Prayagraj:Anti-corruption team caught him at police station; money demanded to file final report
stories.summary: The Anti-Corruption Team arrested a police inspector in Prayagraj while he was allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹75,000 inside a police station. The officer had reportedly demanded the money from an accused individual in exchange for filing a final report in a criminal case. The accused informed the Anti-Corruption Unit, which subsequently laid a trap to apprehend Inspector Vinod Kumar Sonkar. As soon as the money was handed over at the police station, the team caught him red-handed. Initially, the inspector attempted to assert his authority, but when officers began escorting him away, he reportedly pleaded for leniency, saying, 'Leave me, I will be ruined. It is a staff matter. Please have mercy.' He was taken into custody and later brought to Ghurpur Police Station. The incident occurred at Bara Police Station on Tuesday afternoon. Sonkar is originally from Sarnath in Varanasi and was promoted from Sub-Inspector to Inspector in 2012. Background: Rape Case and alleged pressure The case in question involved allegations of rape and coercion to settle the matter. A complaint had been registered at Bara police station against Santosh Kumar Dubey, a resident of Lukmanpur under Suriyawan police station in Bhadohi. In November, a woman accused a man of rape on the pretext of marriage and also alleged that Santosh Kumar Dubey and two others had pressured her to compromise. Police sources state that the woman later told a magistrate she had filed the complaint due to a misunderstanding and no longer wished to pursue action. Following this statement, it was decided that a final report would be submitted in the matter. Allegation of extortion Taking advantage of the situation, the inspector allegedly demanded ₹75,000, knowing that the complainant’s revised statement had paved the way for closure of the case. Santosh Kumar Dubey claimed his name had been forcibly added during the investigation despite not being named initially. He alleged that money had previously been taken from him to remove his name from the case and that a further ₹75,000 was now being demanded. It was after this alleged demand that he approached the Anti-Corruption Bureau. Trap and arrest An initial inquiry by the Anti-Corruption Unit confirmed the inspector’s alleged modus operandi. A trap was then planned. On Wednesday at 2:40 pm, Santosh arrived at the police station with the marked currency notes. After a phone call, Inspector Sonkar summoned him to his office. As soon as the money was accepted, the Anti-Corruption Team intervened and arrested him. The operation was led by Anti-Corruption Inspector Mrityunjay Kumar Mishra. Formal legal proceedings are now underway. Previous postings and complaints Vinod Kumar Sonkar had earlier served as Station House Officer at Khuldabad police station in Prayagraj. He was later posted as SHO of Shahganj but was removed following complaints and transferred to the police line. Approximately six months ago, he was appointed in charge of Bara police station, where the alleged bribery incident occurred.

stories.title: Speaker directs officials to answer MLAs’ calls in UP Assembly:Opposition and ministers clash sharply on multiple governance issues
stories.summary: Discussion continued on Wednesday, the eighth day of the Budget Session in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly. Raising the issue of officials not answering calls from MLAs, the Speaker said such conduct was unacceptable. 'If an elected representative calls, the officer must not only answer but also show due respect,' he stated. A day earlier, Leader of the Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey had alleged that even station house officers were not taking legislators’ calls. On Wednesday, Samajwadi Party (SP) MLA Atul Pradhan raised the issue of free electricity for irrigation, claiming that five lakh farmers had been excluded over the past two years and their names not added. Energy Minister AK Sharma responded with figures, saying those excluded may not have applied. When Pradhan termed the minister’s statement ‘false’, the Speaker objected to the use of the word ‘lie’. Heated exchanges in the house SP MLA Om Prakash Singh rose to speak, prompting the Speaker to remark that he seldom stood against others but immediately opposed ministers. 'Friendships and relations should remain outside the House,' he added. Shivpal Yadav also intervened, alleging the minister spoke as though no work had been done before 2017 and accusing him of making untrue statements. In a lighter tone, the Speaker commented, ‘You should adjust a little.’ Congress MLA Aradhana Mishra raised the issue of being placed under house arrest over MGNREGA protests. The Parliamentary Affairs Minister retorted, asking why she had gone outside the House to 'invite embarrassment”. When SP MLA Anil Pradhan highlighted poor roads in his constituency, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna responded that this was not an SP government but the Yogi administration, claiming road renewal now occurs within five years instead of eight. Crime, local demands and exchanges SP MLA Hriday Narayan Patel criticised the government’s claim of reduced crime in the Budget speech, stating that numerous murders had occurred in 2025, particularly involving members of the Patel community. BJP MLA Pankaj Singh sought development works in Noida, including electricity supply to colonies near the Hindon River, an SDF unit following a software engineer’s death in Dadri, a trauma centre, and the launch of the Prime Minister’s Housing Scheme locally. During a reply by Education Minister Sandeep Singh to a question from Om Prakash Singh, MLA Ragini Sonkar expressed dissatisfaction. The Speaker remarked that Om Prakash had effectively delivered her speech. Sonkar said the Leader of the Opposition would respond, but the Speaker advised Mata Prasad Pandey to stand only if he wished. Pandey replied that he did not wish to do so.

stories.title: 9 patients’ eyes removed, 9 lose vision:Condition worsens within 24 hours after cataract surgeries in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, nine patients had to undergo eye removal after cataract surgeries, while nine others lost their eyesight. However, one patient’s vision was later restored. An eye camp was organised on February 1 at New Rajesh Hi‑Tech Hospital, where 30 patients underwent cataract operations. Within 24 hours, their condition began to deteriorate, and 18 developed eye infections. As their health worsened, they were admitted to super-speciality hospitals in New Delhi, Lucknow, and Varanasi, where treatment is ongoing. The Health Department’s culture report confirmed infection. A magisterial probe has been launched against the doctors who performed the surgeries. The ophthalmology department of the hospital has been sealed, and statements of patients have been recorded. Medical reports of the patients have also been included as evidence in the investigation. The magistrate has recorded the surgeon’s statement as well. Patients said that by the second day after surgery, they began experiencing pain and pus in their eyes. The report examines how such negligence occurred. Infection 24 hours after surgery On February 1, a total of 30 cataract surgeries were performed in the ophthalmology department of the hospital. Patients were discharged after 3–4 hours of observation. On February 2, it emerged that several had developed eye infections, and 18 returned to the hospital one by one. The surgeries were conducted under the Ayushman scheme. Doctors at the private hospital reportedly panicked as the situation worsened. The patients were referred to a Gorakhpur eye care centre, where initial examination revealed severe infection in their eyes. Treatment there also proved ineffective. Families then took the patients to hospitals in Delhi, Lucknow, and Varanasi. Within 24 hours, it was confirmed that of the 18 admitted patients, nine had lost vision and nine had to have an eye removed as the infection was spreading. Now read about the patients Patient 1. Pardeshi Lost eyesight, treatment ongoing at AIIMS Delhi A resident of Kaulha village in Belghat area, Pardeshi had also undergone surgery at the hospital. During a check-up on February 17, doctors told him his eyesight was gone and that removal of the eye would depend on reports. Patient 2. Sahwan Ali Eye had to be removed, now they won't be able to see Sahwan Ali from Gola had one eye removed at AIIMS Delhi. Family members said bleeding started from the eye the next day after surgery, after which hospital staff referred her to Delhi. She has been asked to return for review on February 23. Patient 3. Shankaravati Eye removed in Varanasi Shankarawati from Rahdauli is being treated in Varanasi, where one of her eyes was removed. Her family says she still has trouble in the other eye, with reduced vision and persistent headaches. They fear the remaining eye could also get infected and say they will pursue legal action if her vision worsens. Now CMO's Statement Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rajesh Jha said it was a serious case of negligence and an ADM-level inquiry is underway. Further action will be decided once the report arrives. The Health Department’s culture test has confirmed bacterial infection, and the magisterial inquiry report is expected soon.

stories.title: Hansi-born IAS set to wed Noida IRS officer:Himanshu Nagpal and Urja Jain engaged, father says wedding soon
stories.summary: IAS officer Himanshu Nagpal, a resident of Hansi in Haryana, is set to get married soon. He will tie the knot with IRS officer Urja Jain, who is posted in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Urja is a Joint Commissioner in the Income Tax Department and belongs to the UP cadre. Himanshu is currently serving as Municipal Commissioner in Varanasi, the parliamentary constituency of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The engagement ceremony took place at Himanshu Nagpal’s home in Hansi, attended by both families. Himanshu’s father, Pankaj Nagpal, a journalist by profession, said he is personally overseeing the wedding arrangements. He added that the wedding date will be finalised soon. Urja is originally from Aurangabad in Maharashtra and completed her studies in Mumbai. Himanshu secured All India Rank 26 in the 2019 civil services exam, while Urja secured Rank 519 in 2022. They knew each other earlier Pankaj Nagpal said the two officers already knew each other. During training, Urja would often seek academic guidance from his son. Later, Himanshu told him he liked Urja. After that, talks were held with her family, who agreed to the match. The alliance was finalised when both families met in Hansi on Mahashivratri. Himanshu Nagpal studied in Hansi Himanshu topped Class 12 from Shri Kali Devi Vidya Mandir in Hansi. He later pursued B.Com from Hansraj College, Delhi University. He also secured ninth rank nationwide in the CA Level-II exam. He had decided during school itself that he wanted to become an IAS officer and began preparing for UPSC right after finishing school. He took coaching in Delhi and often skipped festivals like Diwali and Holi to focus on studies. Urja Jain studied from Mumbai, father was former Mayor Urja Jain is an Indian Revenue Service officer who cleared the UPSC exam with Rank 519. She had decided in Class 10 that she wanted to join civil services. She completed Class 12 from Nath Valley School and graduated in Economics from Sophia College for Women, Mumbai. She belongs to a prominent family in Aurangabad. Her father, Vikas Jain, is a former mayor, and her mother, Alpa Jain, has served as a councillor. Urja began preparing for the civil services in Delhi in 2018 and succeeded on her third attempt after two unsuccessful tries.

stories.title: 'Groping, pulling drawstring is attempted rape', says SC:Reinterprets Allahabad HC’s remark, restores attempt-to-rape charge
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India has overturned an order of the Allahabad High Court which held that breaking a girl’s pyjama string and grabbing her breasts was not sufficient to constitute an offence of attempt to rape. The apex court made it clear that such acts do amount to attempt to rape. A bench headed by CJI Suryakant delivered the verdict on Wednesday. The case relates to Kasganj district in Uttar Pradesh. In 2022, a woman had filed a complaint alleging that three youths from her village stopped her minor daughter on the pretext of dropping her home and committed sexual misconduct. The accused allegedly touched the child’s private parts and broke the string of her pyjama. Case was registered against 3 under POCSO Act Based on the victim's mother's complaint, a case was registered against all three accused under the POCSO Act. The special POCSO court in Kasganj issued summons to the accused in 2023. After this, the accused challenged the case in the High Court. In March 17, 2025, the Allahabad High Court ruled that these acts did not fall under rape or attempt to rape, and directed that the charge of ‘attempt to rape’ be dropped. The ruling triggered widespread criticism. Taking suo motu cognisance, the Supreme Court stayed the High Court order on March 25, 2025, and has now set it aside completely. Three youths molested a girl in 2021 A woman from Kasganj filed a complaint on January 12, 2022, alleging that on November 10, 2021, she was returning home with her 14-year-old daughter after visiting a relative in Patiyali. On the way, three village youths — Pawan, Akash and Ashok — approached them. Pawan offered to drop the girl home on his motorcycle. Trusting him, the mother allowed her daughter to go along. However, on the way, Pawan and Akash allegedly touched the girl’s private parts. Akash tried to drag her under a culvert and broke the string of her pyjama. Mother had filed rape case Hearing the girl’s screams, Satish and Bhure, who were passing by on a tractor, rushed to the spot. The accused allegedly threatened them with a country-made pistol and fled. Based on the mother’s complaint, Pawan and Akash were booked under IPC sections 376, 354, 354B and Section 18 of the POCSO Act, while Ashok was booked under IPC sections 504 and 506. Challenging the summons, the accused moved the High Court by filing a criminal revision petition, which was admitted by a single bench of Justice Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra. High Court said - Breaking pajama string is not attempt to rape On March 17, 2025, the High Court observed that grabbing a girl’s private parts, breaking her pyjama string and forcibly trying to pull her under a culvert did not amount to rape or attempt to rape. The court altered the charges against two accused, dropping IPC Section 376 and Section 18 of the POCSO Act, and directed that they be tried under IPC Section 354(B) and Sections 9/10 of the POCSO Act. It also ordered the trial court to issue fresh summons. Supreme Court took suo moto cognizance and stayed the decision The High Court’s ruling drew criticism from legal experts, politicians and civil society. The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance and stayed the order on March 25, 2025. A bench comprising then CJI B.R. Gavai and Justice A.G. Masih observed that some of the High Court’s remarks reflected an “insensitive and inhuman approach”. Notices were issued to the Centre, the Uttar Pradesh government and other parties. Supreme Court had said - Do not use language that intimidates the victim During the hearing on December 8, 2025, the court made strong remarks, stating that such observations can have a chilling effect on victims and may even pressure them to withdraw complaints. The court said it could issue detailed guidelines for High Courts and cautioned that courts, especially High Courts, must avoid such unfortunate remarks while writing judgments or during hearings.

stories.title: Bhagwat clarifies RSS does not control BJP amid protests:Comments on US tariffs, highlights foreign pressure through force.
stories.summary: As soon as RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat arrived at Lucknow University on Wednesday morning, chaos erupted. Students associated with NSUI, Samajwadi Student Sabha, and Bhim Army started raising slogans of 'Go Back Mohan Bhagwat'. When police tried to stop the students, pushing and pulling began. Seeing the situation deteriorate, police forcefully packed the protesting students into jeeps and buses. Many students who lay down were carried away. All students were sent to the Eco Garden. After this, Mohan Bhagwat's program began. NSUI activist Shubham Yadav said- People associated with RSS are being given permission to conduct programs in the university, while opposition student organizations don't even get halls. The Supreme Court has stayed the UGC dispute. Despite this, no statement has come from the RSS chief. Bhagwat is on a 2-day visit to Lucknow. After participating in a seminar at Lucknow University today, he will attend a program at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. On Tuesday, Bhagwat attended a social harmony meeting organized at Saraswati Shishu Mandir in Nirala Nagar. He answered questions from people of different groups on topics related to social harmony. On UGC guidelines, Bhagwat said - Everyone should follow the law. If the law is wrong, there is also a way to change it. The law should not become a cause of dispute between castes. PHOTOS of student protests- What the protesting students said... Police on alert mode even before the protest The police had gone into alert mode even before the students' demonstration. On suspicion of participating in the protest, police reached Samajwadi Student Sabha member Taukeel Ghazi's hostel room at 5 AM. He was placed under house arrest. Several other members of the Samajwadi Student Sabha were taken into custody. They were taken to the Hasanganj police station. Read what the Sangh chief said yesterday, here are his key points... 1- Mughals and British could not erase Hindu religion and culture The RSS chief said that some people sitting in countries like America and China are planning against our goodwill. We need to be careful about this. We must eliminate distrust towards each other. We must participate in each other's sorrows and pains. Speaking on casteism, Mohan Bhagwat said that Mughals ruled for 500 years and the British for 200 years, but the Hindu religion and culture is so strong that they could not erase it. When no one could harm the Hindu religion in so many years, what can anyone do now? The caste inequality that is spreading in society needs to be eliminated. This is not the job of any government or organization, rather every section and individual in society must work together to accomplish this. 2- Mohan Bhagwat says - Indian Muslims are also Hindu, need to bring them back home The RSS chief said - Muslims living in India are also Hindus, they haven't come from Arabia. The work of homecoming should be accelerated. We will also have to take care of those who return to Hinduism. On increasing infiltration, the RSS chief said infiltrators need to be detected, deleted, and deported. They are not to be given employment. On the declining population rate of Hindus, he said Hindus should have at least 3 children. Currently, the population rate is 2.1. This should be at least 3. A society where the average number of children is less than three will become extinct in the future. Now tell all the children who are getting married to have at least three children. 3- Mother power is the foundation of family, women are not weak Mohan Bhagwat said, mother power is the foundation of home and family. In our tradition, men had the right to earn, but mothers decided how to spend. After marriage, maternal power comes to another house and makes everyone their own. We should not consider women as weak; she is the destroyer of demons. The concept we have of women and nature is powerful. Women should receive self-protection training. In the West, women's status is that of a wife, while here they are considered mothers. Their beauty is not seen; their nurturing nature is seen. 4- Muslims also want to join RSS A question was asked in the meeting about why RSS created a Muslim forum? Mohan Bhagwat said that Muslims also want to join the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Their people have created the forum. India will guide the world in the near future. India alone has solutions to many problems of the world.

stories.title: 'BSP to fight 2027 UP polls alone', says Mayawati:Rejects alliance speculations, terms them 'fake news and conspiracies'
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) National President Mayawati reiterated on Wednesday that her party will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently, dismissing speculations about any alliance. Speaking to the media at her Lucknow residence, she described such reports as “fake news” and “BSP-opposing conspiracies,” stressing that the party aims to secure a full majority on its own. Rumours of alliances are misleading Mayawati addressed recent discussions suggesting that BSP might form alliances in the upcoming elections. “Amidst selfish leaders’ chatter, some media reports claim BSP will contest the next UP assembly election as part of an alliance. This is entirely misleading and fabricated,” she said, calling the news “completely false, baseless, and concocted.” She also criticised the media for amplifying such rumours, warning them not to “play like a flying kite, ridiculing themselves in the process.” She highlighted that BSP’s decision to contest alone has already been publicly declared multiple times, including during a grand rally in Lucknow on 9 October 2025, on Kanshi Ram’s death anniversary. Criticism of other parties Targeting the Congress, Samajwadi Party, and BJP, Mayawati said, “These parties have a narrow outlook and are anti-Babasaheb Ambedkar. Their idea of an alliance with Ambedkarite BSP is purely for electoral gains and votes. There’s no benefit for BSP in that.” She urged party workers to remain focused on the 2027 mission independently, stating, “Ignoring baseless and fabricated claims, BSP will walk steadfastly like the elephant and aims to form a full majority government, just like in 2007.” Clarification on Delhi residence Addressing rumors about her newly allotted Type-8 bungalow in Delhi, Mayawati said it was provided for security reasons. “The current BJP government, too, had allotted several bungalows, but they were not taken due to security concerns. I have been allotted the correct Type-8 bungalow and have accepted it,” she explained. She referred to the 2 June 1995 Lucknow State Guest House incident, stating that since then she has been under special high-level security, which has now been further enhanced. “It is inappropriate to indulge in narrow and malicious politics over this,” she added. Call to BSP workers ahead of elections Mayawati warned that as the elections approach, opposition parties would increase their attempts to undermine BSP through various tactics. She urged her supporters to place “firm trust in the party and its iron leadership,” and to continue working with full dedication to strengthen the Ambedkarite movement based on self-respect and dignity.

stories.title: Snakes adorn 200‑year‑old Shivling in Kanpur:Ancient belief says It changes colour thrice daily
stories.summary: The Shivling at Nandeshwar Temple in Kanpur was decorated with snakes. First, the Shivling was adorned with flowers and bel leaves. After this, it was decorated with 10 snakes. Then thousands of devotees who came from far and wide performed worship of Mahadev. The special thing is that a snake charmer catches the snakes several days before this. On the day of decoration, he brings the snakes to the temple. After the worship, the snakes are released back into the forest. This tradition has been continuously followed for 27 years. This decoration is done every year on the third day of Mahashivratri. See pictures... Shivling changes colour three times a day This temple located in Hathigaon is about 200 years old. Narendra Singh, associated with the temple committee, says that the Shiv temple which has an Ardhanarishwar Shivling changes color three times a day. In the morning its color appears brown, and becomes shiny in the afternoon. At sunset its glow becomes lighter. Devotees consider this a divine miracle. Before Mahashivratri, snake charmers bring snakes from the forests. After special worship and rituals, these snakes are used to decorate Lord Shiva's Ardhanarishwar form. Snake charmers bring snakes from the jungle Rampal Nath, a snake charmer from Kannauj, says that during the decoration, the Shivling is adorned with bel leaves and flowers. The snakes are allowed to move freely near the Shiva family. There is a huge crowd of devotees to witness this amazing and thrilling sight. After the worship is completed, all the snakes are safely released back into the jungle. This also reflects the feeling of respect towards nature and living beings. Farmer had cut off and offered his tongue' Temple committee vice president Haripal Yadav said - On the third day of Mahashivratri, there is a prevalent belief about a farmer named Lala from Hathigaon. It is said that farmer Lala cut off his tongue and offered it to the Shivling. Devotees believe that since then, the tradition of decorating the self-manifested Shivling with live snakes began. Since then, people believe that Lord Shiva's worship is done through snakes, scorpions and other creatures that are considered inseparable parts of Lord Bholenath. Devotee Akanksha Gupta said- This ancient Shiva temple becomes a center of faith on Mahashivratri. Devotees coming from far and wide pray with true hearts. Upon fulfillment of their wishes, they offer Kanwar and perform circumambulation on foot. We have been seeing this tradition since childhood.

stories.summary: Several girls fell while running in the women's Agniveer recruitment rally. 3 of them fainted. They were taken to the hospital by ambulance. The girls had to complete a 1600-meter run in 8 minutes. The recruitment rally is being held at the AMC Stadium of the AMC Center and College in Lucknow Cantonment. 1000 candidates from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand are participating amid tight security. Only those candidates are taking part in this rally who passed the online CEE examination in July 2025. Reporting from 4 AM Candidates were asked to report at 4 AM as per the instructions given in their admit cards. A large number of candidates arrived before the scheduled time. They reported at 4 AM. The process of document verification and physical fitness test began. Physical fitness test started after document verification After height measurement, physical standards check, and document verification, other physical tests, including running, are being conducted. Army officials clarified that the selection process is completely fair and transparent. Candidates will be selected only on the basis of merit. Candidates must bring all original documents as per the instructions given in the rally notification and admit card. Opportunity given to those who passed online CEE Only those candidates are participating in this recruitment rally who passed the online Common Entrance Exam (CEE) held in July 2025. Selected candidates were issued separate admit cards at their registered email. This rally is the sixth phase of the recruitment series being organized in Uttar Pradesh. About 1,000 shortlisted female candidates from all districts of both states are participating in it.

stories.title: Weather turns unstable across Western UP:Rain in Noida and Bulandshahr, thunderstorms likely in 18 districts
stories.summary: Weather conditions have changed abruptly across western Uttar Pradesh. Heavy rainfall was recorded in Noida and Bulandshahr, while cloud cover persisted over Meerut. Strong winds swept through Sambhal, Ghaziabad and Amroha. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain and hail alert for 18 and 19 February. According to the department, thunderstorms and showers may affect 13 districts of western UP on Wednesday, with light drizzle possible in five districts of Bundelkhand. Winds of 30–40 kmph are expected, along with the possibility of lightning and hail in isolated areas. Temperature and crop concerns On Tuesday, Banda was the hottest district at 31.6°C, followed by Hamirpur at 31.2°C and Prayagraj at 31°C. The lowest temperature, 15.4°C, was recorded in Etawah. If rainfall is accompanied by strong winds, standing wheat and mustard crops could lodge, weakening grains and reducing yields. Farmers have been advised to remain alert and avoid storing harvested crops in open areas. Temperature and crop concerns On Tuesday, Banda was the hottest district at 31.6°C, followed by Hamirpur at 31.2°C and Prayagraj at 31°C. The lowest temperature, 15.4°C, was recorded in Etawah. If rainfall is accompanied by strong winds, standing wheat and mustard crops could lodge, weakening grains and reducing yields. Farmers have been advised to remain alert and avoid storing harvested crops in open areas. Rain likely in several districts Cloud cover and light showers are forecast in 19 western UP districts, including Noida, Ghaziabad, Aligarh, Hathras, Agra, Mathura, Firozabad, Baghpat, Hapur, Mainpuri, Etawah, Kasganj, Etah, Auraiya, Jalaun, Jhansi and Lalitpur. Meanwhile, rain and hail were reported in Jaipur and other parts of Rajasthan due to a western disturbance. In Uttarakhand, rain and snowfall are likely in Uttarkashi, Rudraprayag, Chamoli, Bageshwar and Pithoragarh, particularly above 3,300 metres. Now read when intense heat will start and how high the temperature will reach 1- Heat wave begins from first week of March BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava says - weather will start changing completely from the first week of March, and the heat wave will begin. Temperature will rise rapidly during both day and night. By the last week of March, the maximum temperature in many districts of UP could reach 35 to 38 degrees Celsius. 2- Temperature will reach 42 to 45 degrees in May-June Manoj Srivastava says - In April, the temperature is likely to remain around 40 degrees Celsius. In May-June, the maximum temperature in many districts could reach 42 to 45 degrees. This means that not only during the day, but even at night, there will be less relief from heat, and humidity will persist. However, this will largely depend on the El Niño conditions. If El Niño conditions persist or strengthen, the heat situation could become even more severe. 3- Heat wave will last longer Maximum and minimum temperatures will remain above normal during March to May across the country, including UP. Only in March, both maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain above normal throughout the country. Additionally, the number of heat wave days will also be higher than normal. Heat wave days will remain normal only in northeastern India and peninsular states like Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh. 4- Crops will be damaged due to heat BHU's Agriculture Department Professor PK Singh says - March month could prove challenging for farmers. The rise in temperature will affect the Rabi crop. Especially wheat. Due to heat, grains will not develop fully. This will result in lower yield. According to PK Singh, hot winds can also damage crops like mustard, chickpea, and peas. Rising temperatures cause the soil in fields to dry quickly. This increases irrigation costs. Crops face stress. 5- Early rise in temperature, conditions will worsen further According to Dhruvasen Singh, Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Lucknow University, temperatures have increased earlier than usual in 2026. Heat wave events may occur more frequently and for longer durations. Conditions could become more severe in urban areas due to the urban heat island effect. All these factors combined are continuously pushing temperatures upward.

stories.title: Gold prices rise, buyers opt for lighter jewelry:Traders expect business to pick up from April
stories.summary: The fluctuations in gold and silver prices are now directly visible in the jewelry market. Record-high prices have not only changed customer budgets but also preferences. Where there used to be demand for heavy and traditional jewelry, customers are now preferring lightweight designs and low-weight jewelry. Experts believe that gold is still considered safe for investment. However, one-time investment at current high levels could prove risky. This raises the question of whether the jewelry market's vibrancy remains the same amid rising inflation and expensive gold? How much has sales changed compared to last year? Are customers forced to buy less gold after price increases? Read in this news... Is jewelry market's festive season vibrancy the same as before? India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) North India head and UP state president Anurag Rastogi said, “This time gold prices are at record high. For this reason, customers are avoiding buying heavy and large jewelry.” According to him, there has been a 25 to 28 percent decline in gold demand. Currently only 5 to 10 percent purchasing is being seen in the market. He said that even though the season is ongoing, only people with genuine needs are coming to the market. For the past 15-20 days, the market remained almost completely stagnant. Similarly, due to price fluctuations in silver, fear and uncertainty persist among people. Mostly bullion traders were seen in the market. There were very few buyers of gold and silver, and only those people were active who came just for buying and selling. Anurag Rastogi says that there are no signs of any major downturn in gold and silver in the coming time. The same trend is likely to continue in the market ahead. Who are Bullion traders? Bullion traders are people or businesses who trade and invest in gold and silver as raw metals rather than in the form of jewelry. Are gold prices going to increase? According to Vinod Maheshwari, State Coordinator of All India Jewellery and Gold Smith Federation, there are several reasons behind market fluctuations. Among these, political conditions, especially global developments related to Russia, are also a major factor. Their effect is clearly visible on the bullion market. Their estimate regarding silver is that its price will remain within the range of three lakh rupees. Currently in the market, customers are doing more bookings rather than immediate purchases. As for gold prices, they said that a slight upward trend may be seen in the coming time. A surge of about 15 percent is being anticipated. Are people buying or coming to sell old jewelry? According to Anurag Rastogi, since gold prices reached the level of 40-50 thousand rupees per 10 grams, the way of doing business in the market has changed. Now about 80 percent of trades are such where people are getting new jewelry made by exchanging old jewelry instead of making new purchases. In simple terms, due to inflation, people are avoiding buying new gold directly. They are getting their old gold redesigned. This has significantly affected common customers. Additionally, most people are now buying lower carat gold. Especially urban customers, who used to buy heavy jewelry before, now prefer lightweight and 9 to 14 carat jewelry. So that needs can be met within budget. Customers who previously bought 92% pure (22 carat) gold are now buying 18 carat gold. What kind of jewelry are customers buying more now? According to Sanjay Agarwal, Director of Parampara Gems Jewellers in Gorakhpur, the demand for lightweight jewelry has increased rapidly in the market. Customers now prefer lightweight jewelry that looks heavy. When customers come now, they demand flashy and attractive designs in less weight. According to Dheeraj Barnwal, Director of Barnwal Jewellers in Gorakhpur, sales in the jewelry market have fallen significantly. Currently, it remains at around only 25 percent. He said that most customers are currently preferring light jewelry only. New purchases are low, while the number of people getting old jewelry recycled has increased. Only those people who have weddings are coming to the market more. Many customers are making do by wearing their old jewelry. Are people shifting towards silver? Anurag Rastogi says - When silver prices suddenly increased, people invested money in silver by selling their shares in the stock market and even their land and fields. However, when the market suddenly came down, they got scared. Common investors, who were previously selling their gold or other savings to invest in silver, are now in a fearful environment. Due to sharp fluctuations in silver prices and uncertainty, investors are worried about losses. Therefore, people are currently afraid to turn towards silver. According to Manish Kumar Verma, President of Lucknow Metropolitan Sarafa Association, people are currently shopping due to the wedding season. In between, when silver prices rose sharply, customers were unable to make purchases. However, now the demand for silver has increased due to weddings. Particularly, people are now preferring silver with 95 purity. According to them, when gold and silver prices increased, fewer sellers came forward. People expected prices to rise further. Currently, there is higher demand for 18 carat gold in the market. In Lucknow, there is also demand for 9 carat jewelry. They say that people view 9 carat jewelry as use-and-throw. While this is acceptable abroad, in India jewelry is considered an investment. For this reason, customers here generally prefer 18 to 22 carat gold. Youth trend shifting from physical to digital gold Anurag Rastogi says - Youngsters only come to the market to check gold prices. People are now giving more attention to digital gold than physical gold. The new generation is rapidly moving towards digital gold and sovereign gold bonds to avoid the heavy making charges, secure storage hassles and complications involved in buying physical gold. Another advantage is that as soon as prices drop, it shows on digital platforms. Traffic increases there. People are now buying gold digitally from 1 rupee to 1 lakh. Because it has neither storage concerns nor high costs. Manish Kumar Verma, President of Lucknow Metropolitan Jewellers Association, also says that investors still trust physical gold-silver more. Digital is fine for a time. However, people consider physical gold-silver as a lifetime investment. Traders' hopes remain high for jewelry market Gorakhpur-based Parampara Gems Jewellers' Director Sanjay Agarwal says - jewelry demand is expected to increase during the wedding season from April to June. This could bring back vibrancy to the market. Customers are now preferring lightweight and lower carat (14-18 carat) jewelry instead of heavy pieces. Additionally, the trend of recycling and exchanging old jewelry is also expected to continue. Regarding silver, Lucknow jewelers believe that despite high prices, demand will remain steady due to weddings and religious needs. However, purchases will be made thoughtfully. Traders are confident that while weight may be lower, buying will continue. The jewelry market will get good support during the wedding season. Gold could reach Rs 1.68 lakh per 10 grams by 2030 According to Vighnharta Gold Chairman Mahendra Lunia, gold prices could reach Rs 1.68 lakh per 10 grams by 2030. The factors behind the surge in gold prices include geopolitical tensions and global economic recession. Keep these 2 things in mind while buying gold 1. Buy only certified gold: Only buy certified gold with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) hallmark. Under the new rule, gold cannot be sold without six-digit alphanumeric hallmarking from April 1st. Just like Aadhar card has a 12-digit code, gold will have a 6-digit hallmark code. This is called Hallmark Unique Identification Number or HUID. This number can be alphanumeric, something like AZ4524. Through hallmarking, it has become possible to determine how many carats a gold item is. 2. Cross-check prices: Cross-check the correct weight of gold and its price on the day of purchase from multiple sources (like India Bullion and Jewellers Association website). Gold prices vary based on 24 carat, 22 carat and 18 carat. 24 carat gold is considered the purest, but jewelry cannot be made from it because it is too soft. Generally, 22 carat or lower carat gold is used for jewelry making.

stories.title: Agra labourer waiter linked to Rohit Shetty house attack:Father says son stayed home, CCTV backs claim; village gripped by fear
stories.summary: Shots were fired 5 times at Rohit Shetty's house in Juhu, Mumbai. After the attack on January 31, five suspects were arrested from Agra, 1230 km away, at 12:30 midnight on February 15. According to police, these boys were connected to the Shubham Lonkar gang, who worked for Lawrence Bishnoi. Additionally, one suspect each was caught from Noida and Jhajjar. They were taken to Mumbai by plane. After this incident, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Bijauli in the Bah area of Agra. The boys from this area were said to be part of the gang that fired shots at the film director's house. It was revealed that those who fired at Rohit Shetty's house were hotel waiters, laborers, and vegetable vendors by profession. Read the report... People fear another raid Since the night of February 15, fewer people are venturing out in village Bijauli, located 80 km away from Agra headquarters. After walking through the streets here, it felt like they were haunted by the fear of another raid. No one was ready to talk much. We knocked on some doors, and some people asked for identification without opening the door, then refused to talk. While some people did talk, they didn't appear on camera. Mumbai Crime Branch and UP STF had arrested Deepak Sharma, Vishnu Kushwaha, Sunny Thakur, Ritik Yadav, and Sonu from this village. All their houses are within 100 meters of each other in the village, and after talking to the villagers, it also became clear that their families' financial condition is not very good. Vishnu's father said - 2 sons were dragged from home The team first searched for the accused's houses. At Vishnu Kushwaha's house, we met his father, Suraj Pal. He was found sitting outside the house. We asked - what happened? Suraj said - Police teams had come to the village. At midnight, they started banging on our house doors. Some policemen entered inside the house, dragged Vishnu and his younger brother out of the house. However, the younger brother was later released. When we asked, they told us that your son fired shots at Rohit Shetty's house. We were shocked. He works in the gym, was seen here on January 31 in CCTV We asked - Where was your son on the night of January 31? He said - They are framing my son. He was at home. We asked - Who is framing him? He says - Pradeep Sharma alias Golu Pandit from the village got my son drunk and took his mobile phone. He made calls to someone. My son is innocent; he worked at the gym. When we are asked for proof, we will provide the gym's CCTV footage. Vishnu's sister Vinita says - My brother hasn't done anything. The police haven't found the real culprits, so they have framed my brother. We have proof that he was here in the village on the night of the incident. Sonu's father said - He was in Delhi a month ago Sonu is also named among those who fired at Rohit Shetty's house. His father, Vinod, says - I run a vegetable cart. My son said he will stay with relatives who live in Mumbai. He will find some work there. Then he went to Mumbai. I spoke to my son 1 month ago. Then he told me that he came to Delhi for work with Sunny Thakur from the village. Haven't talked to him since then. The police came directly to the village and said that Sonu was involved in the Mumbai attack. Sunny Thakur's grandmother said - family lives in Delhi After understanding what Sonu's father said, we reached Sunny Thakur's house. There we met an elderly woman. She was his grandmother. She told us that our entire family lives in Delhi, and they rarely come to the village. Sunny's father sells vegetables and fruits. Sunny also helps him. I don't know who was caught from where. Deepak's mother said - Haven't spoken to son for 3 months Now we reached the house of Deepak Sharma, the main accused in the firing. Here we met his mother, Ramwati. She says - Haven't spoken to my son for 3 months. He works as a waiter in a hotel in Delhi. Hasn't come home for a long time. I don't know what he has done. Yes, when the police came to the village, I learned that he was arrested from Jhajjar. I worry about my son, but I am poor; what can I do? Know about Mumbai Crime Branch Investigation Shooters roamed around the house from January 15 to 20 Mumbai Crime Branch has taken all 11 arrested accused to Mumbai by air, with their faces covered. They are being questioned separately. Investigators found that between 15 and 20 January, on Shubham Lonkar’s instructions, Sonu and Sunny Thakur carried out reconnaissance of Rohit Shetty’s building, Shetty Tower, using a scooter brought from Pune. The scooter was parked at a railway station for 11 days to avoid suspicion. The attack was planned on 20 January for the night of 31 January. That night, the accused reached Juhu by taxi, retrieved the scooter, and after dropping off one associate, Deepak and Sonu went near the building. Deepak then moved ahead on foot and opened fire with a semi-automatic pistol. How the shooters fled after firing After firing the shots, all three accused initially left together. They abandoned the scooter near the Juhu bus stop. Then they asked an auto driver to take them to Kalyan, but the driver refused. Later, another auto driver agreed to drop them at Thane station. From Thane station, they took another auto to Kalyan station. There, they met the fourth accused. After this, all four caught an express train and reached Bhopal. From Bhopal, they changed trains and reached Agra. After hiding in the village for a few days in Agra, Deepak and Sonu stayed at Vishal's house in Noida. Then, Ritik gave them shelter in Haryana. According to a senior official, Vishal, Ritik, and Jatin have been arrested for allegedly helping the accused. They are accused of providing shelter, money, and other resources during the escape. Used private transport 4 times, public transport 2 times The Crime Branch probe found that the accused used private vehicles 4 times and public transport twice while travelling to and escaping from Mumbai, mapping their route through extensive CCTV analysis. On 31 January, around 12:45 AM, 5 rounds were fired at filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residential building in Juhu, with one bullet hitting the gym glass on the first floor. A social media post, reportedly linked to the Lawrence gang, claimed responsibility for the attack and issued threats to Rohit Shetty and the film industry, warning of further violence if their demands were ignored. Were getting every police update from social media During interrogation, the accused revealed that their aim was to spread terror. This task was given to us by Vishnu Kushwaha from the village, who has connections with Golu Pandit, linked to Shubham Lonkar's gang that demanded a ₹5 crore ransom in Sriganganagar, Rajasthan. Golu is also from their village, Bijauli. The accused have admitted that after seeing the glorification of criminals on the gang's social media accounts, they too became part of this conspiracy, wanting to 'make a name'. They saw how Golu's lifestyle in the village had changed over the past 2 years.

stories.title: 1.86 lakh UP teachers face uncertainty over mandatory TET rule:50k not even capable of giving exams; will Tamil Nadu model show the way?
stories.summary: A recent Haryana government order has raised concerns for 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh who have not yet passed the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). Haryana has directed teachers to clear HTET by March 2027 or face termination. The situation in UP is more complicated. Around 50,000 teachers do not even meet the minimum qualifications to appear for TET. The state government has filed a review petition against the Supreme Court order, which is still pending. The court has given teachers time until September 2027 to pass TET. Teachers’ organisations argue that under the RTE Act, 2009, TET became mandatory only from July 2011 and should not apply to those appointed earlier. If the UP government's review petition is dismissed, what options will the state government be left with? Why are teachers' unions protesting? Read this report... How the TET matter got complicated? The Right to Free and Compulsory Child Education Act (RTE), passed in 2009 and implemented in 2010, guarantees free education for children aged 6–14 in Classes 1 to 8. In 2011, the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) was made a mandatory qualification for teacher recruitment at primary and secondary levels. On 1 September 2025, a Supreme Court bench ruled that teachers with more than five years of service remaining must pass TET within two years, by September 2027. Those with less than five years left were exempt but must clear TET for promotions. The court also questioned the 2014 Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust ruling that exempted minority institutions from the RTE Act and referred the matter to a constitutional bench, which is yet to be formed. Hearing to be held on UP government's review petition Since the Supreme Court's order, 21 lakh teachers across the country are protesting. This includes 1.86 lakh teachers from UP. Many teachers have been teaching for 20 to 25 years. They say how logical it is to take an exam again after so many years of service. Teachers' unions claim that 2 teachers have died due to this stress. Due to the teachers' movement, the UP government has filed a review petition before the Supreme Court's double bench of Justice Deepankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih. This is yet to be heard. 50 thousand teachers in the state cannot even sit for TET In the state, there are 1.86 lakh teachers in primary and secondary schools who have not passed TET. Among these, about 50 thousand teachers are not even eligible for TET. There is a reason for this. The minimum educational qualification for TET is graduation along with B.Ed, D.El.Ed. According to Dr. Prabhakant Mishra, District President of Junior High School Teachers Association Lucknow, until 1998, the minimum qualification for teacher recruitment in primary and secondary schools was only Intermediate and BTC. At that time, BTC provision was available only after passing Intermediate. About 15-20 thousand teachers are working in the state with this minimum qualification. Additionally, there are more than 15 thousand teachers who are employed as dependents of deceased employees. After 5 years of service, they get trained at a grade as per government order. Many of them are neither graduates nor have done BTC. The third category includes people working as teachers with a B.P.Ed qualification. In the state, B.P.Ed holders were appointed as physical education teachers in primary and secondary schools in 1999 and 2004. The number of such teachers is also around 20 thousand. Inter College teachers will also come under purview UP Primary Teachers Association president Dinesh Sharma says the RTE Act also applies to Classes 6–8 in inter-colleges, bringing about 20,000 teachers under the Supreme Court’s order. Teachers in recognised and private colleges teaching these classes will also need to qualify TET. Questions remain over the status of Shiksha Mitras, who teach Classes 1-8. He added that teacher recruitment has followed NCET guidelines since 1993, while promotions are based on seniority under the 1981 service rules. Earlier, TET was mandatory only for untrained teachers recruited after 2001, but it is now required for all teachers. What is UP and Center's stance on TET? Teachers are politically significant, and the UP government is currently taking a lenient approach on the TET issue. In the state assembly, Education Minister Sandeep Singh said the Supreme Court’s TET ruling applies nationwide, but UP has filed a review petition and no decision has been made yet. At the Centre, Minister of State Jayant Chaudhary told Parliament that the Supreme Court order remains in force for now. However, teachers’ leader Dinesh Chandra Sharma said Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan indicated that TET rules under the RTE Act should not apply to teachers appointed before July 2011. What options does UP government have to provide relief to teachers? Shiv Shankar Singh, General Secretary of the National Educational Federation, says - Our fight is directly about getting relief for teachers recruited before July 27, 2011. The UP government has filed a review petition based on the demands of teachers' unions. If this review petition is accepted, the Supreme Court will stay the mandatory TET requirement for all teachers. Even if the Supreme Court rejects the review petition, the state government has options to provide relief to teachers. Shivshankhar Singh says - Education comes under the concurrent list. This means both the central and state governments can make rules on it. The Teachers' Union will meet Chief Minister Yogi and inform him that he can give an exemption to teachers in TET like Tamil Nadu. In Tamil Nadu, around 4 lakh government and private teachers may be affected by the TET rule. The state has filed a review petition against the Supreme Court decision and issued an ordinance to conduct six TNTET exams in two years, while also lowering the qualifying marks. Meanwhile, teachers are upset with Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary’s statement that TET is mandatory for all. In response, teacher organisations are planning protests, including a social media campaign from 22 February, black-band teaching from 23–25 February, demonstrations on 26 February, and a nationwide rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan in March. UP TET exam likely in first week of July CBSE recently conducted CTET (Central Teacher Eligibility Test) in two shifts on February 7 and 8 across 138 districts nationwide. According to the UP Junior High School Teachers Association, about 50 thousand teachers from the state took this exam. The UP Teacher Eligibility Test is also proposed in the first week of July 2026. A large number of teachers are also preparing for the UP TET exam.

stories.title: Manikarnika makeover flags preservation concerns:Holkar Trust seeks protection of 18th century structures linked to great reformer Ahilyabai
stories.summary: The ongoing controversy surrounding demolition activities at Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi has triggered widespread concern among historians, heritage conservationists and members of the Holkar family. This is the family that brought renewed focus on the historic contributions of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar and her visionary reforms in Kashi, including the creation of the women-exclusive Jnana Ghat in the 18th century. Historians say the developments have exposed serious gaps in the documentation and preservation of structures associated with one of India’s most respected rulers, whose works played a crucial role in shaping the religious and cultural infrastructure of Varanasi. Holkar state’s enduring presence in Kashi Historical records indicate that the Holkar princely state maintained a dedicated administrative office in Kashi for decades to supervise restoration and construction works carried out under Devi Ahilyabai Holkar’s patronage. According to Khasgi Trust records, her works extended beyond temple restoration to include the construction of ghats along the Ganga, dharamshalas for pilgrims, residential complexes, gardens and the establishment of Brahmpuri for scholars and priests. Historian Zafar Ansari said the current dispute reflects a long-standing neglect of Holkar-era heritage documentation. Personal tragedy that shaped a spiritual ruler Devi Ahilyabai Holkar’s life was marked by profound personal loss. Her husband Khanderao Holkar died in 1754, followed by the death of her father-in-law Malhar Rao Holkar in 1766. The same year, she lost her only son Malerao Holkar to illness, and later her daughter Muktabai also passed away. Records and books suggest that these tragedies led her to consider renouncing power and shifting to Kashi. However, she was persuaded to continue ruling in the interest of her subjects. Instead of stepping away from governance, she dedicated the Holkar throne to Lord Shiva and ruled as a custodian, with official orders issued in the name of Huzoor Shri Shiv Shankar, symbolising that the entire state belonged to the deity. Jnana Ghat: a landmark social reform Among her most progressive contributions was the creation of a dedicated bathing ghat for women at Manikarnika, historically known as Jnana Ghat. Constructed between 1777 and 1785 using her personal funds, the ghat reportedly cost Rs 50,000 and was designed with a 60–65 feet sloping descent into the Ganga. Historians describe the structure as a rare example of gender-sensitive infrastructure during that period, when women often struggled to maintain privacy while bathing at public ghats. The conservationist emphasised that the significance of Jnana Ghat goes beyond architecture. The construction of a separate ghat for women was a remarkable social reform. Ahilyabai Holkar understood issues of dignity and safety at a time when such concerns were rarely addressed by rulers. he said. Adjacent to the ghat, she also constructed a massive gateway known as the Gate of Indore State, symbolising the Holkar administration’s presence in Kashi. Creation of Gupt Kashi in Maheshwar Her devotion to Kashi extended to Maheshwar, where she established a Kashi Vishwanath temple on the banks of the Narmada in 1786, often referred to as Gupt Kashi. The temple, known for its intricate stone carvings of Hindu deities, was constructed over a period of nearly five years. She also invited scholars, Sanskrit experts and priests from across India and established administrative systems for their settlement and sustenance. Concerns over heritage preservation Ansari warned that the recent developments at Manikarnika highlight deeper systemic challenges in heritage protection. Without strong archival systems and verified documentation, historical sites become susceptible to accidental damage or removal. The Manikarnika episode should serve as a wake-up call for authorities to develop comprehensive heritage mapping. he said. He further added, Ahilyabai Holkar’s works are not limited to religious architecture. They represent a governance model that combined spirituality, social welfare and urban planning. Losing such heritage structures would mean erasing vital chapters of Indian history. Holkar Trust seeks restoration Reacting to the controversy, Prince Yeshwantrao Holkar, President of the Khasgi Trust, expressed concern over the reported demolition and called for immediate intervention. Legacy of welfare and devotion Devi Ahilyabai Holkar continues to be remembered as a ruler who blended administrative foresight with spiritual devotion and public welfare. Historians note that institutions and public works established under her rule, including healthcare and pilgrimage infrastructure, reflected her commitment to social service. Ansari reiterated that safeguarding her legacy requires urgent and coordinated efforts. As the controversy unfolds, heritage experts and members of the Holkar family are demanding stronger conservation mechanisms to ensure that historical structures linked to Ahilyabai Holkar are preserved for future generations. How Manikarnika Ghat will look after renovation A 25-meter high chimney will also be installed at this crematorium so that the ashes from the pyre rise into the air and don't enter homes. The renovation will include sacred water tanks for bathing the dead bodies, waste trolleys, and tonsure areas. The covered cremation area will have five berths, service area, waste collection system, stairs, waiting area, ground floor registration room, 18 platforms for open cremation, wood storage area, community waiting room, and construction of two community toilets. The entire construction work here will be done using stones from Chunar and Jaipur.
