stories.title: Pakistani woman lodged in Meerut's jail quarantine barrack:Son alleges Waqf property row led to FIR over two voter cards
stories.summary: ‘False voter cards were allegedly created to implicate my mother. The entire matter is linked to our opposition to the sale of valuable Nadir Ali Waqf property.’ This was stated by Faraz, son of Pakistani national Saba Masood, who is currently lodged in Meerut jail. Faraz, a lawyer by profession, alleged that the FIR was filed as part of an ongoing property dispute. He said that the complainant, Rukhsana, is a tenant in their property and that a court case against her is already pending. According to him, the FIR was registered in connection with this dispute. Saba Masood alias Nazia, who lives in Meerut, is accused of obtaining two voter ID cards in 2003 under different names. Saba had come to India 37 years ago after marrying Farhat Masood, a resident of the Nadir Ali building. Following the FIR, a Meerut court remanded her to 14 days in judicial custody. She is currently being kept separately from other inmates in the quarantine barrack of the jail. To understand the case, the Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to her son Faraz, who explained the family’s connection to the Nadir Ali Waqf property. Family name linked to great-grandfather Nadir Ali Faraz said their great-grandfather’s name was Mohammad Ishaq, whose second brother was Nadir Ali. In this sense, Nadir Ali was also their great-grandfather. Over time, the family became known by the name Nadir Ali, and their ancestral identity continued through this lineage. He said the strongest proof of this connection is the family’s ancestral property. In 1941, all the property was declared as Waqf Alal Aulad, and a registered Waqfnama exists to confirm this. What is Waqf Alal Aulad Faraz explained that under Waqf Alal Aulad, the ownership of the property is dedicated to God, while its benefits are passed down to family members across generations. However, the property cannot be sold or transferred. He alleged that the dispute began after their family opposed attempts to sell the Waqf property. He claimed that Waqf property cannot legally be transferred, and its maintenance is the responsibility of the Mutawalli and the Waqf Board. According to him, some individuals, allegedly in collusion with the Mutawalli, have sold several properties associated with their family or the Waqf. The family has demanded an investigation into these alleged transactions. Claim: These properties were sold Filed report on protest Faraz explains - When we protested against the sale of Nadir Mahal, tensions increased with Rukhsana's family. The first case was filed against our father Farhat Masood and younger brother Rahil on April 15, 2025. They were accused of selling goods by using their great-grandfather's seal. They had to spend one and a half months behind bars, but after that they got a stay from the High Court. That stay is still in effect currently. Aunt arranged marriage from Pakistan Nadir Ali Building resident Farhat Masood, son of late Masood Ahmad's aunt (maternal) lives in Lahore, Pakistan. Farhat went to Pakistan for the first time in 1986. Here Farhat met Hanif Khan's daughter Saba from Lahore and the aunt proceeded with the marriage proposal. In 1988, Farhat and Saba got married in Pakistan. Even after the marriage, Saba stayed in Pakistan for two and a half years. After this, in 1991, Farhat brought his wife Saba to India through the long-term visa process. Gave birth to first child in Meerut One year after marriage in 1991, Saba gave birth to her first child. He was named Faraz, since Pakistan was Saba's maternal home, she used to travel to and from Pakistan even after marriage. In 1993, Farhat and Saba had another child. This time it was a girl, who was named Aiman. The special thing was that Saba's delivery took place in Pakistan. Two months after delivery, Farhat came back to India with his wife Saba, son Faraz and Aiman who was born in Pakistan. Got Aiman's passport made after coming to India When Aiman was brought from Pakistan to India, she was two months old. She came to India on a long-term visa with special permission. After coming here, father Farhat applied for her passport. Since Farhat's citizenship was Indian, based on that his daughter Anam's passport was also prepared in 1994. Now with the help of this passport, Anam also started traveling to and from Pakistan. In 1998, Farhat had a third child, who was named Rahil. SP said - FIR filed after verification in investigation SP City Ayush Vikram Singh said, "Delhi Gate Police and Intelligence Department team found Nazia and investigated her other identification documents. After finding the allegations to be true, Nazia was arrested late at night. The woman was presented in court on Tuesday, from where she was sent to jail. She has been kept in a separate barrack in jail."

stories.title: UP receives ₹1 lakh cr investment:Yogi says, 'There is a 360-degree shift in investors' perception'
stories.summary: During the Investor Road Show in Singapore, CM Yogi Adityanath said, UP received investments worth ₹1 lakh crore in 24 hours. While MOUs worth ₹60,000 crore were signed. The CM attributed this to the changing image of the state and growing confidence in investment. CM Yogi said that there has been a 360-degree change in investors' perception about Uttar Pradesh compared to before. Today, every investment coming to UP is secure and connected with rapidly growing opportunities. I spoke with Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister, Home Minister, and Energy Minister. Met with CEOs of major world-class fintech and investment companies like Temasek, GIC, UBS, SETS, Blackstone, and others. Industry leaders showed interest in investing in the state during these meetings. CM Yogi will depart for the Japan tour today from Singapore. Read the key points of CM Yogi's address... Will make Jewar Airport an MRO hub Referring to Singapore's aviation model, the CM said that Singapore is a major center for aircraft Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) worldwide. He said that there are plans to develop similar facilities in India, and Jewar International Airport will be developed as an MRO hub. Focus on skill development CM Yogi visited Singapore's ITE (Institute of Technical Education) Center. He said that their skilling model is world-class. Similar modern skill development centers will be established in Uttar Pradesh. UP moving towards $1 trillion economy goal CM said - all these agreements made in Singapore will prove to be a "milestone" in making Uttar Pradesh a 1 trillion dollar economy. India becoming the 'Dream Destination' for investment In the last 10-11 years, India has developed rapidly under Narendra Modi's leadership. It is soon going to become the world's third-largest economy. India has now become a "dream destination" for global investment, and Uttar Pradesh is becoming the growth engine of this development. Focus on 'Security, Skill and Scale' model His government has prepared a strong ecosystem of security, skill, and scale for investment in the state. Claimed that investment in UP is not only secure but also offers the most potential in the world. On the second day of his Singapore visit, CM Yogi presented a major roadmap for investment and development. Looking at the substantial investment proposals and interest from global companies, the government considers this a big step towards Uttar Pradesh's economic transformation. UP has the industrial base Yogi said - The base that any industry needs to establish itself, that MSME base is already present with the Uttar Pradesh government. 96 lakh MSME units are already operating in different sectors within UP, which is working to advance more than 3 crore people with employment and job opportunities. UP is moving forward with full strength. Singapore is the biggest investor Between India and Singapore, our focus has been on digital public infrastructure, fintech, smart nation, semiconductors, and green shipping corridor. Singapore has the highest foreign direct investment (FDI) in India across all these sectors. Singapore invests the most in India. UP is now the land of performance In these circumstances, UP is presenting itself as a dream destination within India. Because Uttar Pradesh in today's era is not just a Land of Potential, but has successfully presented itself as a Land of Performance in front of all of you. GDP tripled in 9 years In Uttar Pradesh, GDP has increased from ₹13 lakh crores to ₹36 lakh crores in 9 years. This kind of growth might not have been seen anywhere else in the world where a state has successfully tripled its economy in 9 years. Established identity as dream destination Per capita income has also tripled. Such growth might not have been seen before. Uttar Pradesh now contributes 9.5 percent to India's economy. Therefore, Uttar Pradesh has established its identity as a dream destination for investment in India. We have made many efforts in this direction. UP is the growth engine of Economy Uttar Pradesh holds the first position in de-regulation ranking within India. Through decriminalization, we have eliminated 99 percent of criminal provisions from 13 acts of the state. For the past 5 years, Uttar Pradesh has been moving forward as a revenue surplus state, fulfilling its role as a growth engine of India's economy.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Rahul Gandhi attacks govt over US trade deal; Shankaracharya seeks High Court relief amid arrest threat more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Rahul Gandhi attacks govt over US trade deal The Congress is organising a massive ‘Kisan Mahachaupal’ at Jawahar Chowk in Bhopal on Tuesday to protest the India–United States trade deal, with party leaders alleging that the agreement is harming farmers’ interests. 2. MBBS dispute turns deadly; son kills father in Lucknow A 21-year-old man in Lucknow allegedly shot dead his father after being pressured to pursue MBBS, police said. He dismembered the body, hid it in a blue drum and later filed a missing complaint. The accused confessed during interrogation; search operations continue. 3. Shankaracharya seeks High Court relief amid arrest threat: Alleges conspiracy by IPS Ajay Pal in Prayagraj After a POCSO FIR, Prayagraj police intensified the probe and camped in Kashi to question Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. Police inspected his monastery and gathered details. Avimukteshwaranand denied any link to the children and has sought relief from the High Court, saying he has not received any notice yet. 4. Cabinet approves renaming of Kerala to Keralam The Modi Cabinet has approved the proposal for alteration of name of State of ‘Kerala’ as ‘Keralam’. Kerala is due to go to the polls before May to elect 140 members to its Legislative Assembly. The Election Commission has yet to announce the schedule. 5. Suspended PCS officer floats Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha in UP Ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls, suspended PCS officer Alankar Agnihotri launched Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha in Uttar Pradesh. Unveiling the party’s flag and symbol in Vrindavan, he pitched a Hindutva plank, signalling a bid to tap into the BJP’s traditional vote base. 6. Meerut house fire kills 6 of cloth merchant’s family Six members of a cloth merchant’s family, including five children and twin infants, died in a house fire in Meerut’s Lisadi Gate. The victims were trapped for nearly 30 minutes. The merchant was at a mosque when the blaze broke out; investigation is underway. 7. Canada might revoke Mumbai terror attack mastermind's citizenship Ahead of Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s official visit to India between February 26 and March 7, Canada has moved to revoke the citizenship of Tahawwur Hussain Rana, a key accused in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks. 8. Bhagwat pushes unity outreach amid caste tensions, UGC row Amid the UGC controversy and caste tensions, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat intensified outreach in Uttar Pradesh, holding unity meetings across key cities. Analysts see the push for social harmony as an effort to bridge caste divides and safeguard organizational influence ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. 9. Students detained during protest over namaz dispute at Lucknow University Tension continued at Lucknow University for the third day as police detained students protesting against namaz being offered on campus. The protest, linked to the Lal Baradari dispute, escalated after students gathered despite restrictions, alleging selective action and demanding equal enforcement of campus rules. 10. India to face Pakistan in Women's T20 WC campaign opener The Women's T20 World Cup 2026 schedule has been announced by the International Cricket Council (ICC) on 24 February. The tournament, which will be hosted by England, will start on 12 June and come to an end on 5 July.

stories.title: E-rickshaw agency owner shot dead outside Greater Noida home:3 attackers fire in front of wife, 2 arrested
stories.summary: A 30-year-old e-rickshaw agency operator was shot dead in broad daylight in Greater Noida. 3 attackers chased him in the street near his house. Then they shot him 3 times in front of his wife outside the house gate. When his wife ran to save him, one attacker pointed a pistol at her, too. They then made several knife attacks on his neck. When neighborhood people ran towards them, the attackers fled. Family members took the injured man to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The live murder scene was captured on CCTV. The incident occurred in the Ecotech-1 police station area. Police have arrested 2 accused, and are conducting raids to search for the third one. The e-rickshaw agency operator had been released on bail just 4 months ago in a murder case. Agency owner was returning home with shampoo Nitin, who lived in village Luksar, ran an e-rickshaw agency. On Tuesday morning, he went to the shop to buy shampoo. Around 11 o'clock, he was returning home with the shampoo. On the way, 3 attackers who were lying in wait caught him from behind. When Nitin tried to run away, the attackers chased him. Nitin was caught in front of his house and thrown onto the road. Then 3 shots were fired one after another. As soon as the bullets hit, Nitin fell on the road covered in blood. Meanwhile, hearing the sound of gunshots, his wife Shweta came out of the house. When she tried to save her husband, one of the attackers pointed a gun at her. Shot him in front of the house, wife kept screaming After shooting, the attackers made several knife attacks on Nitin's neck. Meanwhile, seeing the neighbors coming, all 3 attackers fled. A relative of Nitin said that he has 2 children. Nitin was murdered by Sachin, Jeete, and his friend, who are residents of the village. Police have arrested 2 attackers. It is reported that in 2024, contractor Vinay was murdered. Nitin was accused in this case. Nitin had gone to jail on murder charges After this, Nitin had surrendered in a Delhi court. From there, Nitin was sent to jail. He had come out of jail on bail just a few days ago. When Nitin was in jail (6 months ago), his father, Phire Nagar, was murdered. His body was found in the fields of Ghanghaula. Sachin was suspected of the murder as well. However, at that time, Nitin was in jail. Due to this reason, no complaint was filed. Police had also not taken any action. Meanwhile, Additional DCP Sudhir Kumar said that two accused have been taken into custody in connection with Nitin's murder. In the 2.30-minute CCTV footage that has emerged, Nitin is seen coming towards his house. As soon as he enters the street leading to his house, three attackers emerge from a shop located at the corner of the street. During this, one attacker puts a pistol to Nitin's head. At that moment, Nitin turns around and starts running after seeing the accused. During this, a child collides with him. Because of this, Nitin stumbles after running just a few steps and falls in front of his house. By then, all 3 attackers catch up to him. After this, they start firing bullets at him rapidly. Hearing the sound of firing, Nitin's wife, Shweta, comes out and starts screaming. When she runs to save Nitin, an attacker points a pistol at her, too. After this, she stands at the gate in fear. stories.title: Speeding car driven by doctor hits trader:Victim dies; vehicle rolls back 30 feet after hitting dumper
stories.summary: A speeding car driven by a doctor struck a furniture trader in Basti town, fatally injuring him. Vehicle, reportedly travelling at around 100 km/h, hit the businessman with such force that he was thrown nearly 10 feet into the air, crashed into a parked dumper, and then fell onto the highway. The car also rammed into the dumper. The impact was so severe that the car rolled back about 30 feet before coming to a stop. The businessman sustained critical injuries and was rushed to the hospital by family members, where doctors declared him dead. The driver, a doctor, was also seriously injured. An angry crowd caught the driver and handed him over to the police. The collision left the car badly damaged, with its front portion completely crushed. The accident occurred around 8 pm on Monday near the Chhavani police station area in Harraiya tehsil. A video of the incident has surfaced today. See the images of the accident... Car hit while talking on mobile Abdul Qadir (45), a resident of Shankarpur village, was a furniture businessman. He has a furniture shop called 'Safiq Ara Machine' along the highway. His house is also behind the shop. Abdul had been in this business for the past 15 years. On Monday, he was going to cross the highway to go to the mosque for prayers. After closing the shop, he was standing by the highway talking to someone on mobile. During this time at 8 PM, an out-of-control Maruti Ciaz car came and hit him hard. Multiple bones broken, head injured The collision was so severe that Abdul was thrown about 10 feet in the air and collided with a dumper passing through the service lane. The car also hit the dumper. Abdul was badly injured in the accident. Several bones in his body were broken, and his head was split. Upon receiving information, family members reached the spot and took him to Ayodhya Medical College in the car, where he died during treatment. After this, the family members returned home with the body and filed a complaint about the accident with the police. Car driver doctor was intoxicated Local people caught the car driver at the accident site. During questioning, he was identified as Dr. Ashutosh Sharma from Kelly Hospital. It is alleged that he was heavily drunk. After the accident, Ashutosh informed CMO Rajeev Nigam of Basti District Hospital about the incident. Dr. Atul Singh, superintendent of Vikramjot CHC, said that on the night of the accident, the CMO called and said that Dr. Ashutosh's car had met with an accident, asking to get him out of there. By the time he reached the spot, the police had already taken Ashutosh away.

stories.title: Uproar continues for 3rd day at Lucknow University:Students detained before Hanuman Chalisa recital; protest linked to namaz, disputed Lal Baradari site
stories.summary: Tension continued at Lucknow University for the third consecutive day on Tuesday, as police detained several students who had gathered to recite the Hanuman Chalisa in protest against namaz being offered on campus. Police reached the spot soon after students assembled and took them into custody. Officers escorted the students into police vehicles. Some students protested and climbed onto the vehicles while opposing the action. Students questioned the police move, stating that no action was taken when namaz was offered and an iftar gathering was held earlier on campus. They said they were being detained for planning to recite the Hanuman Chalisa. The students had also released a poster before the planned recital mentioning “purification” of the campus. See 3 pictures... Dispute linked to Lal Baradari building The dispute is linked to the Lal Baradari building inside the university campus. Some students claim there is a mosque inside the structure, while others say there is also a small temple. The building is in a damaged condition, and the university administration has started renovation work. On Sunday, when excavation began, students affiliated with the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) reached the site and protested. They said Lal Baradari is a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), and construction work cannot be carried out without permission. Confrontation between student groups On Sunday, Muslim students offered namaz and held iftar at the site. On Monday, another group of students gathered at the same place and raised religious slogans. Muslim students had reached the spot to oppose the construction work, and another group raised slogans in response, leading to tension between the two sides. Students protest detention Videos showed students protesting while being taken into custody. Some students climbed onto police vehicles during the detention. One student said when namaz and iftar were held earlier, no action was taken, but students planning to recite the Hanuman Chalisa were detained. Police have increased deployment on campus to maintain order.

stories.title: Woman cuts her stomach during labor pain:Experts stress ignoring severe labour torment can have deadly consequences
stories.summary: On 19 February in the Bondi area of Bahraich, a pregnant woman named Nankai attempted to cut open her stomach with a blade after being unable to bear the intensity of labour. Neighbours acted swiftly, rushing her to Fakhpur CHC by ambulance. There, doctors managed a normal delivery, and she gave birth to a daughter. However, her condition remains critical. This shocking act raises troubling questions: why would a woman take such a dangerous step? Can unbearable labour agony drive someone to such extremes? Does severe pain have the potential to disturb mental balance? Experts weigh in on these concerns in this report. A similar case from 2025 In March 2025, another disturbing incident emerged from Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh. A young man named Rajababu, suffering from chronic stomach pain, attempted self-surgery after failing to find relief through medical treatment. He gathered surgical equipment from the market and followed instructions from YouTube videos. Within hours of the procedure, his condition deteriorated. He confided in his nephew, who rushed him to hospital. Doctors were stunned by his actions, highlighting the dangers of desperation and misinformation when dealing with severe pain. What is labor pain and how intense is it? Labor pain is the pain that begins with the contraction of the uterus (womb) before delivery. It helps the baby move downward for birth. This pain is completely different and much more intense than normal stomach pain. Doctors say that labor pain is considered the most intense pain in the body. Its intensity can vary from woman to woman. However, in many cases, this pain can also affect a woman's mental balance. In one study, labor pain was rated around 7.2/10 on the pain intensity scale. This puts it close to or above pains like bone fractures or kidney stones. However, it is not the same for everyone. Why did woman take such a dangerous step? Nankai told in the hospital that there was a baby in her stomach, that's why I was having severe pain. To get rid of the pain, I cut my stomach with a knife. Due to the pain, Nankai lost consciousness. Dr. Sudhir Gupta, gynecologist at Gorakhpur District Hospital, says - The pain during labor pain sometimes reaches an unbearable level. This pain is not normal stomach pain, but is continuous and extremely intense. This can break a woman's endurance capacity. According to Dr. Gupta, when the pain is very severe and the woman does not get immediate medical help, she may think in panic and mental pressure that somehow she will get relief from the pain. The woman must have taken such a step in this misunderstanding and mental imbalance. In medical science, this is considered an Extreme Pain-Induced Crisis, where a person is not in a position to make normal decisions. Can mental balance be disturbed in case of severe pain? According to Dr. Amit Shahi, psychiatrist at Gorakhpur District Hospital, a person's mental balance can be temporarily disturbed in situations of severe and unbearable pain. Extreme pain and stress can create conditions of fear, anxiety and confusion. During such times, a person cannot make right-wrong decisions. They may lose control over themselves momentarily. This condition is considered a Psychiatric Emergency in medical terms, not a deliberate action. What is this pain like? Dr. Sudhir says, “This pain occurs due to continuous and intense contractions of the uterus, which is completely different and much more severe than normal pain. This pain is counted among the most intense pains in the world. Although a woman's body is hormonally and biologically prepared to endure this pain, it is still not easy.” How dangerous is stabbing yourself in stomach? According to experts, the way the woman stabbed herself in the stomach was an extremely dangerous and life-threatening situation. Such wounds to the stomach can cause severe blood loss within minutes. Internal organs can be seriously damaged. This type of injury can lead to serious problems like intestinal protrusion, spread of infection, shock, and damage to the uterus. In the case of pregnant women, this risk increases further, as it becomes a direct threat to the life of both the mother and the unborn child.

stories.title: Son kills father, hides body in blue drum in Lucknow:Dad wanted him to be doctor; caught while disposing of body
stories.summary: Lucknow’s Vardhman Pathology lab owner Manavendra Singh was shot dead by his 21-year-old only son Akshat. After the murder, the accused cut the body with a saw and stuffed the pieces into a blue drum. He severed the head, kept it in a car and dumped it 21 kilometres away from the house. Akshat carried out the crime in front of his sister and threatened to kill her if she told anyone about it. After disposing of the head, the accused returned home and cleaned the car. Three days later, on Monday, he went to the police station and lodged a missing complaint. During questioning, police noticed he appeared nervous. On suspicion, he was interrogated strictly and eventually confessed to the crime. Police took him to the spot and recovered the body parts, but the head is yet to be found. During interrogation, the accused told police that his father wanted him to clear NEET and pursue MBBS. He was firm that he should not be forced into a medical career. He had suggested that instead of running a pathology lab, they should open a lawn or restaurant, which he believed would be a better business. The argument over this issue escalated on February 20, and in a fit of rage, he shot his father with his licensed rifle. The incident took place in Sector-L under Ashiyana police station limits. The deceased, Manavendra Singh, was associated not only with a pathology lab business but also with the liquor trade. See 3 pictures related to the incident- Accused is B.Com student, mother has passed away Manvendra Singh was originally from Jalaun district. His father Surendra Pal Singh is retired from Uttar Pradesh Police. Many years ago, Manvendra built a house in Ashiana Sector-L and started living there. His wife passed away nine years ago. Since then, he had been taking care of his son Akshat and daughter Kriti (17) by himself. The accused Akshat is a B.Com student. Kriti is an 11th grade student at APS. Manvendra's younger brother SS Rajawat is in Uttar Pradesh Police. He is currently posted at the Secretariat. The father, son and daughter lived on the top floor of the three-story house. The accused's uncle and aunt lived on the second floor. The parking and guest room are on the lowest floor. Threatened sister - Will kill you According to the accused son, he shot his father with a licensed rifle at 4:30 AM on February 20. His sister was also present at that time. When the sister tried to scream, he threatened her and said If you tell anyone about the incident, I will kill you. After this, he made a plan to dispose of the body. He brought the father's body from the third floor to the ground floor and kept it in an empty room. Then he bought a saw from the market and cut the body into several pieces. He put the head and some pieces in the car and dumped them in Sadrauna village. The remaining parts were packed in polythene and filled in a blue drum. Reached police station 3 days after incident, police became suspicious of his behavior According to police, three days after the incident, the accused son reached Ashiana police station on Monday and filed a missing person report. He told police that his father had left on February 20 at 6 AM saying he was going to Delhi and said he would return by afternoon of February 21, but hasn't returned yet. All three of his mobile numbers were continuously switched off. When police started searching for Manvendra and interrogated the son, his behavior seemed suspicious. Upon strict questioning, he first said that his father had committed suicide. When pressured further, he confessed to the murder. Rifle was hidden under the mattress After killing his father, Akshat hid the rifle under the mattress. Police arrived at the house with him. When the body was recovered, only half of it was found, the remaining parts were missing. During interrogation, he revealed that he had disposed of the body parts in Sadrauna area of Kakori. Police remained at the house for about eight hours conducting investigation. Late at night, the body was sent for post-mortem. Neighbors said, ‘He was reserved, had run away from home four years ago’ Manvendra Singh's friend and neighbor Dharmendra Singh said that Akshat didn't interact much with anyone in the neighborhood. If he ever encountered someone, he would just say hello. He had no friends in the neighborhood. Four years ago, Akshat ran away from home. During that time, he left a six-page letter. In it, he wrote that he didn't want to do MBBS and should not be forced into it. He had also advised to close the pathology lab and open a lawn or restaurant. Later, on his father's persuasion, he returned in just one day. Manvendra Singh was completely different in nature from his son. He used to talk to everyone in the neighborhood and was a person who kept everyone united. He celebrated every festival with enthusiasm and kept organizing some event or the other. He also organized Ramlila in the park, where Akshat played the role of Meghnad. During that time, he used to mingle with everyone. 'Manvendra not seen after February 19' Dharmendra Singh said that his last meeting with Manvendra was on February 19. He had returned from a feast. When he was not seen by anyone from the next day, the son was asked. He said that father had gone to Delhi. There were often disputes between father and son, so people thought he might have left in anger. But after two days passed, when information was sought again, still no clear answer was received. When asked again after this, the son said that father had gone missing and he was searching for him in nearby areas.

stories.title: Shankaracharya seeks High Court relief amid arrest threat:Alleges conspiracy by IPS Ajay Pal in Prayagraj; whole system is against
stories.summary: After an FIR was registered against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, Prayagraj police have intensified their investigation. A police team has set up camp in Kashi and may visit his monastery today to record his statement. Officials said further action, including arrest, may be considered based on the questioning. The team reached Bhelupur police station on Monday night to gather information about the Shankaracharya. Police inspected the monastery and collected details about his close associates. The Bhelupur police inspector shared inputs related to the case. Meanwhile in his reply, Avimukteshwaranand said, "We haven't received any notice yet. When they (Police) come, we'll talk to them. Police haven't contacted us yet, nor have they been informed, nor have they been served any notice... The most important issue is, what connection do we have with those children? Children who never came to our attention, who never enrolled in our institution, you can conduct thousands of medical tests on them. It's up to you to prove their connection to us. "We mentioned that our lawyers are working on going to court against the FIR... In a case like POCSO, the police should immediately act. They should believe what the child says, and after believing it, they should immediately get a medical examination. Action should be taken immediately. So the question is, why didn't the police register it?..." he added. ‘People are being tempted against me’ Swami Avimukteshwaranand alleged that attempts were being made to frame him. He said a family from Shahjahanpur told him that a person named Ashutosh Maharaj had asked them to make allegations using their minor daughters’ names. He claimed the family was threatened after refusing and alleged that people were being tempted or pressured to make accusations against him. Lawyers, political leaders gather at monastery Several lawyers, including All India Bar Council Co-Chairman Srinath Tripathi, have gathered at the monastery and expressed willingness to represent him. Political leaders have also been visiting the ashram. Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai has written to the Prime Minister demanding an impartial investigation. He said the POCSO case appeared politically motivated and linked it to the Shankaracharya’s criticism of the state government over alleged mismanagement during the Kumbh Mela. A woman who came to seek blessings at the monastery became emotional and started crying over the allegations. Swami Avimukteshwaranand consoled her and said people should react only after the truth is established. Police inspect Magh Mela camp site in Prayagraj On Sunday, police visited the Magh Mela area in Prayagraj along with complainant Ashutosh Maharaj. They inspected the site where the Shankaracharya’s camp had been set up and prepared a map of the surrounding area, including entry and exit routes. Ashutosh Maharaj had filed a complaint on January 24, alleging sexual exploitation of children during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. On February 8, he approached the Special POCSO Court in Prayagraj, alleging police inaction. Two children were produced in court on February 13, and their statements were recorded on camera on February 21. On the same day, the court directed police to register an FIR at Jhunsi police station. Swami Avimukteshwaranand, his disciple Mukundanand, and two to three unidentified persons have been named as accused. SP, Congress leaders express support for Shankaracharya Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticised the case, calling it unfortunate and alleging it was a false case against a religious leader. SP MP Virendra Singh also met the Shankaracharya and said leaders connected with the monastery stood in his support. Congress MP Imran Masood questioned the allegations and said the matter required careful scrutiny, adding that such action against a Shankaracharya had raised concerns among followers. Police said the investigation is ongoing and further steps will be taken based on evidence and statements.

stories.title: 5 killed, 45 injured in Lucknow double-decker bus crash:28 injured admitted to SGPGI trauma centre; driver, cleaner fled after crash
stories.summary: Five people were killed and 45 injured after a double-decker bus overturned on the Purvanchal Expressway in Lucknow, police said. The injured included seven children, 12 men and nine women. Of them, 28 were admitted to the Apex Trauma Center at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGI) for treatment. Photos and videos of the accident surfaced on Monday, showing the scale of the damage and rescue efforts. Rescue operation and aftermath Police said the accident caused panic among passengers. Rescue teams used a crane to straighten the overturned bus and shift it to the toll plaza. Emergency personnel and local police carried out rescue operations and rushed the injured to nearby hospitals. Visuals from the scene showed injured passengers trapped inside the vehicle. Rescue teams had to break windows and doors to pull people out. Police later cleared the road to restore traffic movement on the expressway. Bus was travelling from Punjab to Bihar According to police, the bus was travelling from Ludhiana in Punjab to Motihari in Bihar at the time of the accident. Preliminary information suggests the bus was moving at a speed of over 80 kmph when it overturned. The driver and cleaner fled from the spot after the accident. Police have registered a case against the driver and the bus operator. The driver, identified as Sompal, is a resident of Naultha village in Panipat district of Haryana. Victims identified, probe underway Police identified some of the deceased as Birendra (30), Anjali (8), and Priyanchu (15), along with a six-year-old child and a 30-year-old man. Authorities said identification of all victims is ongoing. Passengers gave different accounts of the cause of the accident. Some alleged that the driver had consumed alcohol at a roadside eatery before the journey resumed, while others claimed he may have fallen asleep while driving. See pictures of the accident- Driver claims sudden speed breaker, eyewitness contradicts version During questioning, the bus driver told police that a speed breaker suddenly appeared on the Purvanchal Expressway, forcing him to apply brakes. He admitted to having a light drink at a roadside dhaba before resuming the journey. He claimed the bus lost control due to sudden braking and excess passengers, hit the divider, and overturned. However, officials said the driver’s statement appears false, as there is no speed breaker at the accident site. An eyewitness, Ansh Patel, gave a different account. He said the bus was swaying uncontrollably before the accident. “The bus was moving like a snake. Suddenly, it overturned. There was screaming everywhere. We ran to help the passengers,” he said. Police said the driver may have given misleading information, and his role is under investigation. Preliminary probe finds major safety violations A joint inspection by Regional Transport Office (RTO) officials revealed serious violations in the bus structure and safety systems. ARTO Administration Prabhat Pandey said the emergency exit at the rear had been blocked by installing additional seats. This prevented passengers from escaping quickly after the bus overturned. “Emergency gates must remain accessible, but in this bus, the exit was covered. The inspection report is being prepared, and action will follow,” Pandey said. Bus modified illegally, carried passengers beyond capacity According to ARTO Enforcement officer Alok Kumar Yadav, the bus had permission for 16 sleeper berths and 32 sitting seats. However, operators illegally modified the bus to create 43 sleeper berths and reduced sitting seats to nine. Officials also found that around 90 passengers were travelling in the bus, far exceeding its permitted capacity. This overcrowding increased the risk and severity of the accident. Investigators also found illegal iron structures installed on the roof, and unauthorised changes in the bus’s length and internal layout. Single driver operated long-distance route Officials said the bus was travelling around 1,360 km from Ludhiana in Punjab to Motihari in Bihar with only one driver. Rules require at least two drivers for such long-distance journeys. Transport norms also mandate rest breaks after fixed driving hours. Preliminary findings suggest these rules were not followed. Bus had 67 unpaid challans, yet continued operations Transport department records show the bus had 67 pending challans for traffic violations. Despite this, the vehicle continued to operate across multiple states without enforcement action. Officials said the bus passed through more than 50 transport jurisdiction zones, raising questions about enforcement lapses. Technical inspection to determine exact cause Officials said a detailed technical inspection of the bus will be conducted to examine brakes, tyres, wiring, and other mechanical systems. Police Commissioner Amarendra Singh Sengar and District Magistrate Vishakha G visited the accident site and reviewed rescue and investigation efforts. Authorities said further action will be taken based on the technical report and investigation findings.

stories.title: Barsana prepares natural colours for Nandgaon’s 'Huriyars':Radha’s sakhis to shower 'abeer'; know the tradition behind laddoo throwing
stories.summary: Barsana’s Shriji Temple is resonating with Holi songs as preparations intensify for the famous Lathmar Holi, scheduled on February 25. On the temple rooftop, young men from the Goswami community are preparing natural colours using Tesu flowers in large iron cauldrons, following a tradition that has continued for generations. The festival formally begins when Huriyas (men from Nandgaon) arrive at the temple to seek permission from Radha to play Holi. Devotees symbolically apply colour on Radha using a silver pichkari, marking the start of Braj’s world-famous Holi celebrations. Authorities estimate that around 15 lakh visitors will reach Mathura-Vrindavan over seven days to witness the festivities. Traditional Holi songs accompany colour preparation Preparations for Holi colours began nearly a month ago. On the temple rooftop, Goswami youth sing Braj Holi songs as they work. Large drums filled with Tesu flowers soaked in water and massive cauldrons placed on stoves form the centre of activity. The flowers are boiled and stirred continuously with wooden sticks to extract vibrant natural colours. After sufficient heating, the liquid is strained and stored for use during Holi celebrations. According to Goswami Rakesh Brajwasi, natural colours are made from Tesu flowers, sandalwood, rose petals, kewda, and traditional fragrances. Nearly 1,000 quintals of flowers are sourced from Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana each year for this purpose. “These colours are completely natural and safe. This process starts at least a month before Holi,” he said. Why Tesu flowers are used Tesu flowers, also known as Palash, are considered sacred in Braj traditions. Their natural pigment produces bright saffron and yellow shades. Temple volunteers soak and boil the flowers in large quantities, ensuring the colours remain eco-friendly. The preparation involves soaking the flowers in water, heating them in iron cauldrons, and filtering the mixture after the pigment is released. These colours are later used by devotees and temple participants during Holi. Laddoo Holi draws lakhs of devotees One day before Lathmar Holi, Barsana celebrates the unique Laddoo Holi. During this event, laddoos are thrown and distributed as prasad from the Shriji Temple. This year, around 8 to 10 lakh devotees are expected to attend the event. Preparations are underway to distribute nearly 10,000 kilograms of laddoos. Local confectioners have begun large-scale production while maintaining strict quality standards. Halwai Rambabu, one of the confectioners, said gram flour for laddoos is prepared in-house to ensure purity. “The batter is fried in ghee to make boondi, which is then soaked in sugar syrup and shaped into laddoos,” he explained. Around 18 sweet shops in Barsana are involved in preparing laddoos for the temple. “We do not see this as business. It is service to Radhaji,” he added. Mythological roots of Laddoo Holi Residents of Braj trace the origin of Laddoo Holi to the Dwapara Yuga. According to tradition, Radha’s friends went to Nandgaon to invite Krishna for Holi. When Krishna accepted the invitation, people in Barsana celebrated by throwing laddoos and colours. This symbolic celebration continues today and marks the beginning of Holi festivities in Barsana. Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan also prepares for Holi Preparations are also underway at the Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan, where colours made from Tesu flowers, sandalwood, saffron and traditional perfumes will be used. Temple priest Gopi Goswami said preparations begin weeks in advance. “Devotees from across the world come to experience this Holi. Natural colours and fragrant gulal create a unique spiritual atmosphere,” he said. At the temple, Tesu flowers are boiled in large iron vessels placed on a special furnace inside the Holi chamber. The colour festival will begin on Rangbhari Ekadashi on February 27 and continue until March 2. Temple authorities plan to use nearly 2,000 to 3,000 kilograms of gulal and about 25,000 litres of Tesu-based coloured water during the celebrations. Special offerings and rituals during Holi On Dolotsav, celebrated on March 3, special food offerings including chaat, jalebi, gujiya, thandai and sweets will be presented to the deity. Devotees will also receive coloured prasad during darshan. Due to a lunar eclipse on March 3, darshan timings have been revised. Devotees will be allowed darshan from 6:15 am to 9 am and again from 7 pm to 10 pm. Lakhs expected as Braj prepares for grand Holi celebrations With preparations in full swing in Barsana and Vrindavan, the Braj region is ready to host one of India’s most iconic Holi celebrations. From natural Tesu colours and devotional songs to laddoo offerings and traditional rituals, the festival reflects centuries-old traditions that continue to attract lakhs of devotees every year.

I-PAC to handle Akhilesh's election campaign in UP:Secret meetings in Delhi and Bengal; hired on advice of 2 CMs
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has set up his fielding to challenge CM Yogi in the 2027 assembly elections in UP. Election strategist Prashant Kishor's (PK) company, I-PAC, will develop the election campaign strategy for Akhilesh Yadav in UP. PK's team will soon take charge in Lucknow. Sources say that Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin and Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee had advised Akhilesh Yadav to hire PK's company. Akhilesh had his first meeting with PK in Delhi in December 2025, then met again when he went to Bengal recently. After this, the Samajwadi Party hired them. Sources say that Akhilesh Yadav is going to start his election campaign from Noida on March 28. He will hold a PDA partnership rally in Noida. SP is hiring multiple companies SP is hiring different companies for different tasks. Mumbai-based company Show Time Consulting has been given the task of data analysis and strategy based on it. A Karnataka-based company has already started survey work in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Do or Die Election for Akhilesh Yadav The 2027 election is do or die for Akhilesh Yadav. After success in the Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh Yadav now wants to gain power in UP at any cost. For this, he is not only hiring different agencies but also party officials are connecting with booth-level workers on the ground and taking complete reports. PK has made strategies for many political parties Prashant Kishor is known as PK in political circles. Through his company, I-PAC, he has delivered success to many major election campaigns. Created a strategy for the BJP in 2014. Secured victory for Nitish Kumar in Bihar in 2015. Delivered victory to Captain Amarinder Singh in Punjab in 2016. PK's company played an important role in the successes of Mamata Banerjee's TMC and MK Stalin's DMK. Sources say that Akhilesh and PK had a meeting in Delhi in December 2025, and then again when Akhilesh went to West Bengal in January 2026, both had a long discussion. It is believed that PK will oversee Akhilesh Yadav's entire election campaign from behind the scenes. I-PAC will focus on training workers at the booth level along with the election campaign, using app-based tools to increase voter turnout, as well as focusing on the weaknesses of opposition parties. Akhilesh seeing golden opportunity In the 2022 assembly elections, SP won 111 seats. However, it fell short against BJP's 255 seats. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP showed its strength by winning 37 seats. Now, Akhilesh wants to leave no stone unturned to return to power. He is continuously attacking the BJP government over law and order, corruption, and unemployment. Akhilesh Yadav is now not missing any opportunity to directly attack the Chief Minister as well. Who is Prashant Kishor? Prashant Kishor entered Indian politics after resigning from the United Nations in 2011. In 2014, he campaigned for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. After its success, he established I-PAC, which is now India's first professional election consultancy company. However, in recent years, PK has distanced himself from the company and is running his Jan Suraj Party in Bihar. In the 2025 Bihar elections, he decided not to contest, but instead focused on strengthening the organization. There are also some rumors that PK was sent to Bihar by Amit Shah to tarnish Tejashwi Yadav's image, but these are mere speculations. I-PAC is now in the hands of people like Prateek Jain, who are working with TMC and DMK. Prashant Kishor has worked in UP earlier Prashant Kishor has worked in UP before as well. In the 2017 assembly elections, he had devised a strategy for Congress and gave the slogan "27 years UP Behal" (27 years UP in distress). However, later an agreement was reached between SP and Congress. The UP Behal slogan had to be abandoned midway. Even after the agreement with SP, Congress could win only 7 seats. SP also faced a bad defeat, getting reduced to just 47 seats.

stories.title: 6 of cloth merchant’s family die in Meerut house fire:5 children and twin infants among dead; father was at mosque when blaze broke out
stories.summary: Six members of a cloth merchant’s family, including five children and twin infant daughters, died after a massive fire broke out in their two-storey house in Meerut’s Lisadi Gate area late Monday evening. The businessman was at a mosque offering prayers when the incident occurred. Police said the victims were trapped inside the house for nearly 30 minutes before firefighters and residents managed to bring them out. By then, the merchant’s wife and all five children had died. Victims included twin daughters aged six months The incident took place in Gali No. 1, Kidwai Nagar, near Surahi Wali Masjid. Cloth merchant Iqbal alias Asim had gone to the mosque with his brother Farukh. At home were his wife Rukhsar (30), mother Ameer Bano (55), and five children — Mahvish (12), Hammad (4), Addas (3), and twin daughters Nabia and Inayat, both six months old. According to police, the children were playing while the women were preparing food when the fire broke out. Neighbours noticed smoke and flames and raised an alarm. Residents and firefighters used ladders and entered through neighbouring rooftops to rescue those trapped inside. All seven victims were taken to Capital Hospital, where Rukhsar and the five children were declared dead. Ameer Bano and a neighbour sustained severe burns and are undergoing treatment. Narrow lanes hampered rescue operations SP City Ayush Vikram Singh said fire engines faced difficulty reaching the house due to narrow lanes. Firefighters had to access the building through adjacent rooftops. “There was a fire in the house of Iqbal Ansari in Kidwai Nagar. Police and fire brigade teams reached the spot. Firefighters entered through rooftops and rescued seven people trapped inside,” Singh said. Officials said a large quantity of cloth was stored inside the house, which may have intensified the fire. The blaze was brought under control after nearly two hours of firefighting. Cause under investigation; short circuit suspected Chief Fire Officer Surendra Singh said the cause of the fire is under investigation. Initial police findings suggest a possible short circuit, while some residents claimed the fire may have started due to a gas leak. Police said the LPG cylinder in the house did not explode, preventing further damage. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination. Family and neighbourhood in shock Iqbal, who makes clothes and sells them on order and at exhibitions, rushed home after hearing about the fire. He broke down on seeing the condition of his family, officials said. A large number of residents gathered at the hospital. District Magistrate VK Singh, SSP Avinash Pandey, DIG Kalanidhi Naithani, SP Crime Avneesh Kumar, and local MLA Ghulam Mohammad visited the hospital. Police said further investigation is underway to determine the exact cause of the fire.

stories.title: UGC row triggers concern in RSS:What Bhagwat’s 'unity' message in UP means ahead of 2027 elections
stories.summary: In the backdrop of controversy over University Grants Commission (UGC) rules and growing caste tensions, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat has intensified outreach in Uttar Pradesh, emphasising social harmony and unity. Political analysts say the campaign reflects concerns within the organisation about the widening divide between upper castes and backward-Dalit groups and its possible impact on the 2027 Assembly elections. Bhagwat’s recent tour of Gorakhpur, Lucknow and Meerut, part of the RSS’s centenary year outreach, included social harmony meetings, intellectual conferences and youth interactions. He urged followers to prioritise national and religious unity over caste identities and cautioned against divisions that could weaken social cohesion. Centenary year tours focus on social outreach As part of the RSS’s centenary year programme, Bhagwat has been visiting provinces across the country, spending two to three days in each region. His earlier visits covered Kashi, Braj and Kanpur, followed by the western Uttar Pradesh tour. During these visits, Bhagwat addressed meetings attended by representatives from different castes, social organisations and RSS affiliates. The discussions focused on removing caste discrimination and strengthening social unity. He also interacted with RSS functionaries and their families and addressed youth and intellectual gatherings, signalling an attempt to engage influential sections of society and shape public discourse. UGC issue and Bhagwat’s calibrated messaging Political observers link Bhagwat’s emphasis on unity to recent controversy surrounding UGC-related issues, which have triggered debates and disagreements across caste groups. Bhagwat’s remarks in Lucknow reflected a careful approach. At a social harmony meeting on February 17, he stressed the importance of following the law while preserving social unity. “Everyone should follow the law. If the law is wrong, there are ways to change it. Castes should not become a cause of conflict. Society progresses through harmony, not conflict,” he said. He added that discrimination stems from lack of goodwill and called for eliminating such divisions. “We are all sons of one motherland. Sanatan ideology is based on goodwill,” he said. However, at an intellectual conference at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow on February 18, Bhagwat avoided direct comment on the UGC matter, noting that the issue was before the Supreme Court. “The matter is in the Supreme Court. There is no need to worry about it now. Our society must remain united and free from divisions,” he said. Observers said this shift reflected caution after reactions emerged on social media following his earlier remarks. Message against caste-based politics At intellectual gatherings, Bhagwat also criticised caste-based political mobilisation without naming any party. He emphasised unity under a shared religious identity and argued that caste divisions weaken society. He said social harmony requires people to move beyond caste and linguistic differences and recognise shared cultural roots. He added that caste-based divisions enable political mobilisation and that weakening such divisions could change political discourse. Analysts believe these remarks were aimed at the evolving political landscape in Uttar Pradesh, where caste-based alliances played a significant role in recent elections. Analysts link outreach to electoral concerns Political analysts say Bhagwat’s outreach reflects concern over shifting caste equations, especially after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, where caste mobilisation influenced electoral outcomes in Uttar Pradesh. The Samajwadi Party’s focus on backward, Dalit and minority consolidation altered traditional voting patterns, affecting the BJP’s performance in the state. Analysts say the recent UGC-related controversy has further intensified divisions, particularly among youth from different caste groups, potentially affecting political alignments. They believe the RSS’s outreach seeks to reinforce unity and maintain its social influence across caste groups. RSS seeks to preserve organisational influence The centenary year is significant for the RSS, which aims to expand its organisational presence by establishing shakhas in every nyay panchayat by Vijayadashami. However, the organisation is also navigating challenges arising from caste-related debates and religious controversies, which could affect its social outreach. Analysts say the RSS is keen to ensure that its long-standing influence across communities is not weakened by emerging divisions. Journalists see continuity in RSS’s unity message Senior journalist Virendra Nath Bhatt said the RSS and the Modi government have sought to shift political discourse away from caste over the past decade. He noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasised broader social categories such as youth, farmers, women and the poor rather than caste identities. However, Bhatt said political developments in Uttar Pradesh and recent policy debates have brought caste back into focus, affecting traditional voter alignments. Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpayee said the RSS has historically emphasised Hindu unity as central to its ideological framework. He said the organisation views caste divisions as weakening social cohesion and cultural identity, and Bhagwat’s recent remarks reflect efforts to counter such fragmentation. Government steps seen as damage control Political analysts also point to recent policy measures by the Uttar Pradesh government as efforts to address potential social and political fallout. During the budget session, the government nearly doubled honorariums for over 1.4 lakh Shiksha Mitras and more than 24,000 instructors. It also announced interest-free loans of up to Rs 10 lakh for women and measures such as establishing a State Data Center Authority. Analysts said further announcements targeting women, farmers, youth and employees may follow. Political implications ahead of 2027 polls Observers believe the RSS’s social harmony campaign is not limited to organisational concerns but is also linked to broader political dynamics ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. They said caste tensions and education policy debates could influence electoral outcomes, making social unity a key focus area for the organisation. Bhagwat’s centenary year outreach, analysts said, signals an effort to reinforce cohesion within society and address emerging social and political challenges.

stories.title: Seema Haider gives birth to baby boy:Welcomed daughter 11 months ago with husband Sachin; brought 4 children from Pakistan
stories.summary: Seema Haider, who came to India from Pakistan, has become a mother for the sixth time. On Tuesday, she delivered a baby boy at a private hospital in Noida. 11 months ago, Seema had given birth to a daughter. She has four children from her previous marriage to her Pakistani husband, Ghulam Haider. This is her second child with her Indian husband, Sachin Meena. Following a normal delivery, both mother and baby were declared healthy. They were discharged later in the evening and returned to their home in Rabupura, Noida. Family members and neighbours congratulated the couple, and Sachin’s family distributed sweets in celebration. Doctors have advised routine precautions for the newborn and mother. Pregnancy announcement on YouTube Two months ago, Seema shared an 11-minute video on her YouTube channel announcing her pregnancy. In the video, Sachin is seen urging her to visit hospital and rest, offering to cook and bring coconut water. He mentions that she was in her seventh month and reluctant to seek medical care. Seema says in the video, 'I am pregnant. A new guest is coming to my house. I am very happy.' She expressed a craving for ghee, after which Sachin phoned a relative requesting two kilograms. stories.title: Protests in UP against ‘Yadav Ji Ki Love Story’:Police complaint filed over film; Mridul Tiwari alleges threats to sister
stories.summary: Protests have begun in Uttar Pradesh against the upcoming film Yadav Ji Ki Love Story, with members of the Yadav community filing a police complaint and demanding a ban on its release. The film is scheduled to release on February 27. On Tuesday, members of the community lodged a complaint at Dhanari police station in Sambhal against the film’s producer Sandeep Tomer, director Ankit Bhadana, and actors Pragati Tiwari and Vishal Mohan. They alleged that the film hurts the sentiments of the Yadav community and damages its image. Community members said the film portrays a love story between a girl from the Yadav community and a Muslim youth. They claimed that the title and storyline target the community and misrepresent its culture. They also appealed to cinema hall owners not to screen the film and warned of protests if it is released. Viresh Yadav, one of the complainants, said the film is spreading anger in the community and demanded an immediate ban. SP leader warns filmmakers Samajwadi Party leader Gagan Yadav also objected to the film and warned its makers. In a video message, he said the film appears to be an attempt to defame the Yadav community. “We will speak fearlessly and oppose anything that harms our community’s respect,” he said. He added that protests would continue but urged people to maintain peace and avoid violence. Actor Pragati Tiwari receives threats, says her brother Pragati Tiwari, who has acted in the film, is the sister of YouTuber and Bigg Boss 19 contestant Mridul Tiwari. Mridul alleged in a video posted on Instagram that his sister is receiving abusive messages and death threats on social media. He said his sister worked only as an actor and is not responsible for the film’s title or story. “If people want to protest, they should raise their concerns in the right place. Abusing and threatening a girl is not acceptable,” he said. He added that some social media users have posted threatening messages, including warnings of violence. He said the family respects all communities and religions. Viral clip adds to controversy Amid the protests, a short clip of Pragati Tiwari has gone viral on social media. In the clip, she is seen responding to a question about the film’s title, which has further intensified criticism. Background of those involved Mridul Tiwari, 24, is a YouTuber from Etawah in Uttar Pradesh. He runs a comedy channel called The Mridul and has millions of followers. His sister Pragati also appears in his videos and has acted in the film. Police said they have received the complaint and are examining the matter. The filmmakers have not issued a public response so far.

stories.title: RSS chief addresses Social Harmony meeting in Lucknow:Says, 'Indian muslims are also Hindus'; urges 3 children per family
stories.summary: Mohan Bhagwat, chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), said in Lucknow on Tuesday that Muslims living in India are also Hindus and 'have not come from Arabia'. He stated, ‘Muslims living in India are also Hindus, they have not come from Arabia. They also need to be converted back to Hindu, but this work will happen gradually.’ Bhagwat made these remarks during his two-day visit to Lucknow on 17 and 18 February. Expressing concern over the declining population growth rate among Hindus, Bhagwat said that there should be at least three children in every family. ‘Currently, the population rate is 2.1. It should be at least 3. Now, tell all those who are getting married to have at least three children,’ he said. Remarks on UGC guidelines Addressing concerns surrounding University Grants Commission (UGC) guidelines, Bhagwat said they are not against anyone and that everyone must be taken along. He explained that in a federal system, the government frames laws and regulations. 'One side feels it is against them, the other feels it is in their favour. If someone does not agree, they should express their views. The matter is currently pending in the Supreme Court. Whatever law the government makes, it should be followed,' he said. Using a metaphor, he added: ‘If a person has fallen into a pit, they will have to raise their hand to get out, and the person standing outside will have to bend down and extend their hand to pull them out. Only when both extend their hands will things work out.’ Concerns over caste divisions Bhagwat also expressed concern over the continued division of society along caste lines. He said society should not become entangled in the cycle of caste. 'Caste is something we have been trying to eliminate for many decades, but it just does not go away,' he remarked. Social harmony meeting in Lucknow On the first day of his visit, Bhagwat participated in a social harmony meeting held at the auditorium of Saraswati Shishu Mandir in Nirala Nagar, Lucknow. The meeting lasted approximately two and a half hours. During the session, Bhagwat responded to questions from people representing various sections of society on issues related to social harmony. It was stated during the meeting that although there are many streams associated with Sanatan Dharma in India, their fundamental basis is the same. The basic challenges faced by different opinions and sects are similar and can be resolved through coordination and coexistence. Families were also encouraged to engage with environmental issues. On the second day of his visit, 18 February, Bhagwat is scheduled to address a youth dialogue and an intellectual gathering. ‘Mughals and British could not erase Hindu culture’ Bhagwat said that despite centuries of foreign rule, Hindu religion and culture remain strong. 'Mughals ruled for 500 years and the British for 200 years and then left, but Hindu religion and culture is so strong that they could not erase it. When no one could harm Hinduism in so many years, what can anyone do now?' he said. He reiterated that Muslims living in India did not come from Arabia and need to be 'brought back home', adding that this would happen gradually. Muslims and the RSS Platform Responding to a question about why the RSS created a Muslim platform, Bhagwat said that Muslims themselves wanted to join the organisation. 'Muslims also want to join the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Their people have created the platform,' he stated. Encouraging Hindu cultural practices Awadh’s Provincial Propaganda Chief, Dr Ashok Dubey, said that families were inspired to adopt and promote certain traditions. These included signing in Hindi, wearing dhoti, consuming indigenous food, travelling within India before going abroad, planting a Tulsi sapling, hoisting a flag in front of their homes, and writing ‘Swagatam’ instead of ‘Welcome’. Bhagwat’s 3 recent notable statements- 13 December: ‘Time to live for India, not to die’ On 13 December, Bhagwat said that the country should be placed above everything. 'It is time to live for India, not to die. In our country, there should be devotion only to our own country. Language like ‘your pieces will be broken’ will not work here,' he said. He was addressing a ceremony in the Andaman Islands marking the 115th anniversary of Damodar Savarkar’s song Sagar Pran Talamala. 1 December: ‘India is getting its rightful place’ On 1 December, speaking at an event in Pune marking 100 years of the RSS, Bhagwat said that Prime Minister Modi’s words are now heard carefully on the global stage, reflecting India’s growing global stature. 'India is now getting its rightful place in the world,' he said. He also suggested that organisations should not wait for anniversaries or centenaries, but instead focus on completing their work within stipulated timelines. 18 November: ‘No need to declare India a Hindu nation’ On 18 November, at an event in Guwahati, Bhagwat said that there is no need to formally declare India a Hindu nation. 'India and Hindus are one. There is no need to declare India a Hindu nation. Our civilisation already expresses this,' he said. He added that whoever is proud of India is a Hindu, describing Hindu not merely as a religious term but as a civilisational identity connected to thousands of years of cultural tradition.

stories.title: NCC cadet accuses TTE of rape on Ahmedabad–Gorakhpur Express:Accused fled train after complaint; case transferred to Deoria
stories.summary: A young woman preparing for Army recruitment has accused a travelling ticket examiner (TTE) of raping her on board the Ahmedabad–Gorakhpur Express in Uttar Pradesh, the Government Railway Police (GRP) said on Monday. The alleged incident took place on Sunday night between Indara and Deoria stations. The accused, identified as Rahul Kumar, allegedly fled after the woman alerted the police. Victim alleges assault on pretext of arranging seat The survivor, a resident of Mau district, lives in Gorakhpur and is preparing for Army recruitment. She had travelled to Mau to appear for her NCC C-certificate examination and was returning to Gorakhpur when the incident occurred. According to the complaint, she was unable to purchase a ticket due to heavy crowd at the station and boarded the train, standing in an air-conditioned coach. During ticket checking, the TTE questioned her about her identity and travel details. She alleged that the TTE offered to arrange a seat after collecting the prescribed fine and took her to a cabin in the AC first class coach. Once inside, he allegedly closed the door and raped her. The accused also threatened her with legal action for travelling without a ticket if she disclosed the incident, she said. Accused fled after victim alerted police The woman raised an alarm and called the police emergency helpline (Dial-112) during the journey. Upon learning of the complaint, the accused got off the train at Deoria station and fled, police said. After the train reached Gorakhpur, the survivor filed a complaint at the GRP police station. The case was later transferred to Deoria, as the alleged crime occurred within its jurisdiction. Police have registered a first information report (FIR) and conducted a medical examination of the survivor. Police conduct raids to trace accused GRP Superintendent of Police Laxminivas Mishra said police teams were conducting raids to trace and arrest the accused, who is a resident of Bihar. “A case has been registered, and raids are underway. The accused will be arrested soon,” he said, adding that railway authorities have also been informed. Action violates railway procedures Railway officials said that under existing rules, passengers travelling without tickets are fined and issued valid tickets by the TTE. They are then directed to travel in the appropriate coach. Taking a passenger to a private cabin is not part of standard procedure.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day- 1. Assam Assembly polls likely in April, single-phase voting expected Assembly elections for all 126 seats in Assam are likely to be held in a single phase in April. The Election Commission is expected to announce the schedule between March 4 and 8, with polling in the first week of April. 2. Congress MP, 200 workers placed under house arrest ahead of UP Assembly protest Police detained a Congress MP and around 200 workers in Lucknow before a planned march to surround the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. The protest over MGNREGA and Shankaracharya comes during the Budget Session, with security tightened across the city. 3. Police car crashes into tree in UP, sub-inspector killed and five injured A speeding police vehicle returning from a raid in Kushinagar crashed into a tree near Gorakhpur, killing a sub-inspector. A woman SI, a senior SI and five other personnel were injured in the accident. 4. Bomb threat at Mohali hospital treating Punjab CM turns out to be hoax A threatening email claiming Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had been poisoned and warning of a blast at Fortis Hospital, Mohali triggered panic. Police later declared the bomb threat a hoax and launched a probe into the message sent in the name of a Khalistan outfit. 5. Low political claims in voter revision drive as lakhs apply independently During the Special Intensive Revision, objections were filed against nearly 1.25 lakh voters, while over 51 lakh people sought inclusion. Only around 1% of claims came from political parties, with most applications submitted directly by citizens. 6. Haryana order on TET fuels anxiety among 1.86 lakh UP teachers The Haryana government has mandated that all state teachers must clear the HTET by March 2027 or face dismissal. The directive has raised concerns among teachers in Uttar Pradesh who have yet to pass the eligibility test. 7. PM Modi, Macron inaugurate H125 helicopter assembly line Prime Minister Narendra Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron held a joint press conference in Mumbai, reaffirming their commitment to deepen India-France ties. 8. ₹8 lakh robbed near Kanpur police post, four attackers flee on bikes Four assailants assaulted a man with a pistol butt and snatched a bag containing ₹8 lakh just 200 metres from a police post. Senior police officers reached the spot and launched a search operation to trace the accused. 9. Ghaziabad sisters’ deaths reignite debate on digital addiction among teens The deaths of three minor sisters in Ghaziabad have intensified concerns over excessive exposure to foreign digital content. The tragedy has sparked a wider discussion on online culture and its impact on Gen-Z mental health. 10. Tarique Rahman take oath as Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman, chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, was sworn in as the Bangladesh's new Prime Minister. The oath ceremony marked the formal formation of the new government.

stories.title: UP govt rules out new teacher recruitment:Education Minister says, '47,000 posts are vacant, but we have enough teachers'
stories.summary: An estimated 20 to 25 lakh candidates aspiring for jobs in Uttar Pradesh’s primary schools have suffered a major setback. Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh informed the Assembly on Tuesday that the government will not undertake fresh recruitment of teachers in the Basic Education Council. The Minister provided this written response to a question raised by Samajwadi Party (SP) MLA Anil Pradhan. Pradhan had asked whether the government planned to initiate new teacher recruitment in the Basic Education Department. In his reply, the Minister stated that there are 46,944 vacant posts of assistant teachers in schools run by the Basic Education Council. However, the government will not consider creating new recruitment posts for TET-qualified candidates after 2022. He maintained that there is an adequate number of teachers and Shiksha Mitras currently working in council schools. Read the Minister's reply in writing SP raises concern over youth migration During proceedings in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly on Tuesday, Anil Pradhan strongly raised the issue of teacher recruitment in primary schools. He said that whenever he had previously raised the matter, the Minister had responded by stating that the student-teacher ratio was balanced. Pradhan pointed out that 20 to 25 lakh young people who have passed D.El.Ed are awaiting recruitment opportunities. As no recruitment is being conducted in the state, many are travelling to other states to sit recruitment examinations. He further questioned the Education Minister regarding the Supreme Court’s ruling that teachers who have not passed TET must do so. He observed that many senior teachers are currently in service and asked whether the government would seek legal advice to provide them with relief. He also enquired whether the government intended to increase the salaries of Shiksha Mitras and instructors, and whether it would initiate fresh recruitment of teachers. No recruitment for 8 years The Uttar Pradesh government last conducted a major recruitment drive for 69,000 assistant teachers in 2019. Of these, 5,886 candidates were appointed in 2022 following court orders. Since then, no new recruitment process has been announced. The 69,000 assistant teacher recruitment matter remains pending before the Supreme Court. The High Court had earlier directed that the recruitment merit list be reissued. News is being updated…….
