stories.title: Akash’s father-in-Law gains prominence in BSP:Naushad Ali given charge of 4 divisions, responsibilities of 18 in-charges altered
stories.summary: Mayawati has introduced significant changes within the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), restructuring responsibilities among national office bearers. In a notable move, Ashok Siddharth, father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, has once again been assigned a key role. Dr Ashok Siddharth has been appointed in charge of four states, Delhi, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Kerala. Simultaneously, the party has elevated its prominent Muslim face, Naushad Ali, entrusting him with responsibility for four politically significant divisions in Uttar Pradesh, Kanpur, Lucknow, Agra and Meerut. Ramji Gautam’s influence curtailed The reshuffle has reduced the prominence of Ramji Gautam, who was earlier considered the party’s number one national office bearer. That position has now effectively gone to Ashok Siddharth. Responsibilities for Delhi, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bihar have been withdrawn from Ramji Gautam. He has instead been assigned charge of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Similarly, Rajaram, who previously oversaw only Maharashtra, has now been made in charge of Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand. Former MP Girish Chandra has been given responsibility for Uttarakhand, while Sumrat Singh has been appointed in charge of Rajasthan. Changes in UP Divisions Mayawati has also altered the responsibilities of 18 divisional in-charges in Uttar Pradesh to strengthen the organisation ahead of upcoming elections. The promotion of Naushad Ali is viewed as part of a broader strategy to consolidate minority support and reinvigorate the party structure. The four divisions assigned to Naushad Ali are regarded as politically crucial for the BSP. The reallocation of roles is seen as an attempt to inject fresh momentum into the organisation and enhance its influence across regions. These changes are being interpreted as preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and other state contests. Earlier this month, Mayawati had initiated a restructuring drive down to the booth and sector level. This included a decision to provide 50 per cent representation to youth and to abolish certain key posts, such as the system of having two district in-charges. Political analyst and senior journalist Syed Qasim described the reshuffle as part of a broader strategy to energise party workers, reward loyal cadres and strengthen “Mission 2027”. The BSP is seeking to consolidate its traditional support base among Dalits, backward classes and minority communities, while simultaneously expanding its outreach to other social groups. Ashok Siddharth’s return after expulsion The development is particularly significant given that Ashok Siddharth had been expelled from the party on 12 February 2025. Mayawati had taken action against him and her close aide Nitin Singh, citing factionalism and indiscipline in organisational matters. In a post on X at the time, Mayawati stated that Dr Ashok Siddharth and Nitin Singh, who were overseeing southern states, had continued internal factionalism despite warnings and were therefore expelled with immediate effect for anti-party activities. Subsequently, on 2 March 2025, Mayawati removed her nephew Akash Anand from his position and expelled him from the party a day later. After an apology, Akash was reinstated on 13 April 2025. Ashok Siddharth, however, returned only six months later, in September 2025. He has now emerged as the most senior among the national office bearers. From govt doctor to National leader Born on 5 January 1965, Dr Ashok Siddharth is a medical professional by training. He completed a diploma in ophthalmology from Maharani Laxmibai College. During his government service, he served as Assembly, District and Divisional President in BAMCEF. In 2007, while posted at the Gursahaiganj Primary Health Centre in Kannauj, he resigned from government service to join the BSP. He was elected as an MLC in 2009 and again in 2016 on the BSP ticket. In 2016, he was nominated to the Rajya Sabha, where he served until 2022. From govt doctor to National leader Born on 5 January 1965, Dr Ashok Siddharth is a medical professional by training. He completed a diploma in ophthalmology from Maharani Laxmibai College. During his government service, he served as Assembly, District and Divisional President in BAMCEF. In 2007, while posted at the Gursahaiganj Primary Health Centre in Kannauj, he resigned from government service to join the BSP. He was elected as an MLC in 2009 and again in 2016 on the BSP ticket. In 2016, he was nominated to the Rajya Sabha, where he served until 2022. Within the party, he has held several key posts, including Kanpur-Agra Zonal Coordinator and National Secretary, and has previously overseen five states, including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. His wife, Sunita Siddharth, served as Vice-Chairperson of the UP Women’s Commission from 2007 to 2012. Dr Siddharth is regarded as a low-profile figure who works largely behind the scenes, making his reinstatement and elevation particularly noteworthy in the BSP’s evolving organisational structure.

stories.title: Principal accused of bad touch beaten up in Rampur:Parents protest at school for 2 hours; principal arrested under POCSO
stories.summary: In Rampur, people beat up a school principal accused of molesting students. He allegedly inappropriately touched students under the pretext of punishment. When students protested, he would beat and threaten them. Troubled by his actions, female students had even stopped going to school. When family members learned about the matter, they reached the school and beat up the accused principal. The incident took place at St. Francis School in Khuntakheda village of Bilaspur. The commotion at the school continued for about two hours. Upon receiving information, police arrived at the scene and rescued the principal, taking him to the police station. Police have registered a case against the accused principal and sent him to jail under the POCSO Act. Family members allege that when they reached the school to discuss the matter, the principal was intoxicated and began misbehaving with them. Now know the full matter... Parents said - St. Francis School's Principal Arisheril Joseph would lock students in a room under the pretext of punishment and sexually harass them. When female students reported this, they went to school last week to complain, and the principal had apologized. However, he continued harassing female students even after that. Many girls had stopped coming to school out of fear. On Saturday, the principal inappropriately touched some girls. The affected students went home and told everything. On Monday, a large number of parents reached the school. It is being reported that the principal started misbehaving with them. This angered the parents. They beat up the principal. The commotion continued for about two hours. Upon receiving information about the commotion, Bilaspur Station Officer Arjun Tyagi reached the spot with police force. After calming people down, the accused Principal Arisheril Joseph was removed from the school. The police also took possession of the footage from CCTV cameras installed in the school. Based on the parents' complaint, police have registered a case under POCSO Act and started investigation. Three students revealed Father's misdeeds The accused principal is from Kerala The accused missionary school principal Arisheril Joseph is originally from Kerala. He was appointed at this school in 2020. He has been living here since then. Parents allege that the principal performs his duties while intoxicated. He would roam around classes only after consuming alcohol. If he saw any innocent child misbehaving, he would take them to a room in the name of punishment and perform obscene acts. He would also beat children if they resisted. He would threaten to give severe punishment if they complained at home. ASP Anurag Singh said that parents have accused the school principal of making obscene gestures with children. Based on these allegations, the principal has been arrested.

stories.title: Brajesh Pathak on Shankaracharya row:Hair-pulling a grave crime; strict action promised
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak on Monday said strict action should be taken against those responsible for pulling a religious leader’s hair, calling the act unacceptable and inappropriate even during police action. Speaking at the Times Now Conclave, Pathak said police personnel have other means to use force if necessary, such as batons, but pulling someone’s hair should not have happened. He described the act as a serious wrongdoing and said those found guilty would face consequences. Pathak made the remarks when asked about the controversy involving Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand during Mauni Amavasya at the Magh Mela, though he did not mention the seer by name. His statement comes amid growing resentment among sections of the Brahmin community over the incident, with social media users questioning accountability and the government’s response. Maurya assures probe, but does not meet Shankaracharya Earlier, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, speaking in Prayagraj, said he bows at the feet of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand and urged him to take the ritual bath. He said if any saint or Shankaracharya was insulted, the government would investigate the matter and take appropriate action. However, Maurya did not personally meet the Shankaracharya following the incident. Yogi says not everyone can become Shankaracharya Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath addressed the controversy in the Assembly on February 13, saying not everyone can declare themselves a Shankaracharya and that no one is above the law. He said every person in India must follow the legal system and traditions. The CM said the Magh Mela controversy was unnecessarily created and emphasised that positions such as Chief Minister, Minister or Shankaracharya cannot be assumed without following established procedures. He added that Sanatan Dharma has a defined structure and sanctity attached to the Shankaracharya position. Law is equal for all, says chief minister Yogi said the same law applies equally to everyone, including himself, and no individual can claim exemption. Referring to the large turnout of about 4.5 crore devotees during Mauni Amavasya, he said arrangements were made to ensure order and safety, and rules had to be followed by all. Shankaracharya rejects political authority over religious title Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, speaking in Varanasi on February 14, said the identity of a Shankaracharya is determined by religious tradition, not by any political authority or government certification. He said neither the government nor political parties have the right to decide who holds the religious position. He also criticised political leaders, saying arrogance had affected those in power, and asserted that his appointment as Shankaracharya of Jyotish Peeth was in accordance with established religious tradition. What happened during Mauni Amavasya at Magh Mela The controversy began on January 18 during Mauni Amavasya at the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was proceeding towards the Sangam in a palanquin for the ritual bath when police stopped him and asked him to walk instead. His disciples objected, leading to a confrontation with police. Several disciples were detained, and the situation escalated into pushing and shoving. The Shankaracharya’s palanquin was moved away from the Sangam, and its canopy was damaged during the incident. The Shankaracharya was unable to take the ritual bath and staged a protest outside his camp until January 28, after which he returned to Varanasi. Pictures of clashes between Shankaracharya's disciples and police- Brahmins remain a decisive voter group in UP Brahmins, who account for around 9 to 11 per cent of Uttar Pradesh’s population, continue to play a crucial role in the state’s electoral politics. The community is considered influential in at least 31 of the state’s 75 districts, particularly in Purvanchal, central Uttar Pradesh and Bundelkhand, where their voting preference often affects election outcomes. Political observers say Brahmins function as a key swing vote due to their social influence, economic presence and vocal political participation. Their voting behaviour often influences other caste groups, making them an important factor in closely contested elections. However, their support has historically shifted between parties rather than remaining permanently loyal to any single political formation. Over 100 assembly seats have strong Brahmin influence Political assessments indicate that around 115 Assembly seats across 31 districts—including Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Jaunpur, Amethi, Ballia and Sultanpur—have a significant Brahmin voter base. In these constituencies, Brahmin voters range from 30,000 to 1.6 lakh, making them a decisive electoral bloc. Given that the average number of voters in an Assembly constituency is about 2.2 lakh, even a small shift in Brahmin voting patterns can affect results, especially in seats decided by narrow margins. Shifted from Congress to BJP after 1990 After Independence, Brahmins largely supported the Congress and played a key role in its dominance. Several prominent Brahmin leaders, including Govind Vallabh Pant, Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna and Narayan Dutt Tiwari, served as Chief Ministers. However, political developments such as the Mandal Commission and the Ram Temple movement led to disillusionment with the Congress. In the early 1990s, Brahmins shifted towards the BJP, which benefited from Hindu mobilisation around the Ram Temple movement. This support helped the BJP secure a majority in the 1991 Assembly elections. Support shifted between BSP, SP and BJP The community again changed its political alignment in 2007, when the BSP successfully attracted Brahmin voters through targeted outreach and leadership representation. This shift helped the BSP secure a full majority in the Assembly elections. In 2012, a section of Brahmin voters supported the Samajwadi Party, contributing to its electoral victory. However, from 2014 onwards, Brahmins largely consolidated behind the BJP, playing a significant role in its successive victories in Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. Recent trends show signs of shifting voter preferences Recent elections indicate early signs of changing preferences among Brahmin voters. Even a small shift in their support can influence election outcomes, especially in closely contested seats. In the 2022 Assembly elections, more than 100 constituencies were decided by margins of less than 10,000 votes. Political analysts say any sustained shift in Brahmin voting patterns could significantly impact future election results in Uttar Pradesh, given the community’s numerical strength and influence across key regions.

stories.title: Teachers must pass TET exam by 2027:To face dismissal if they fail, what lies ahead for 1.86 lakh UP teachers?
stories.summary: An order issued by the Haryana government has heightened anxiety among teachers in Uttar Pradesh who have not passed the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). On 16 February, the Haryana government directed that all state teachers must clear the Haryana Teacher Eligibility Test (HTET) by March 2027. It warned that those who fail to qualify by the deadline would be removed from service. The development has intensified concerns in Uttar Pradesh, where thousands of in-service teachers have yet to pass TET and are awaiting clarity from the state government. Issue raised in UP assembly On Tuesday, during proceedings in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, Samajwadi Party (SP) MLA Anil Pradhan from Chitrakoot questioned the government’s stance on teachers who have not cleared TET. In response, Education Minister Sandeep Singh stated that the Supreme Court’s ruling, which makes TET mandatory, applies nationwide. He added that the UP government has filed a review petition in the matter. The Supreme Court has directed that all teachers up to junior high school level nationwide must pass the Teacher Eligibility Test by September 2025. Several state governments, including Uttar Pradesh, challenged the order by filing review petitions. However, petitions from many states have already been rejected. Legal experts believe UP’s plea may also face dismissal, which would leave the state government with no option but to implement the TET requirement fully. Teachers announce protest programme In response to the Haryana government’s directive and the broader uncertainty, teachers’ organisations in UP have announced an agitation plan. Dr Prabhakant, District President of the Junior High School Teachers’ Association, Lucknow, said teachers are formulating a protest strategy. From 22 to 24 February, teachers will wear black armbands as a mark of protest. From 26 February, demonstrations will be held outside Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) offices in every district. Memoranda addressed to the Prime Minister will be submitted to each District Magistrate (DM). In the first week of March, teachers from across the country plan to gather at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi for a large protest. SC ruling and its implications The controversy stems from a Supreme Court hearing on 1 September 2025 concerning the mandatory nature of TET in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra. The bench comprised Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih. The Court ruled that teachers with more than five years of service remaining must qualify the Teachers Eligibility Test. Failure to do so would require them either to resign or opt for compulsory retirement. The Court further directed state governments to ensure compliance within two years under the Right to Education (RTE) Act. In Parliament, MPs from several parties, including the SP, protested against making TET compulsory and urged the Centre to introduce an ordinance. However, the central government declined, citing the binding nature of the Supreme Court’s order. The ruling triggered protests among teachers in Uttar Pradesh. In two tragic incidents, 52-year-old government teacher Ganeshilaal in Hamirpur and 49-year-old Manoj Kumar in Mahoba died, with their families claiming they were distressed by the order. Under mounting pressure, the UP government filed a review petition. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated that experienced teachers should not have their qualifications disregarded, noting that the government provides regular training. 1.86 lakh teachers face uncertainty The issue affects approximately 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh teaching classes one to eight who have not passed TET. Under the RTE Act (2009) and a National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) notification dated 29 July 2011, TET is mandatory for all teachers, both newly appointed and in-service, teaching Classes 1 to 8. However, 1.86 lakh teachers were appointed before 29 July 2011 and have not cleared TET. Their appointments were based on qualifications such as B.Ed, B.P.Ed and BTC. Many are Intermediate pass and dependent teachers. The crisis intensified after a Supreme Court bench comprising Justices Dipankar Datta and Manmohan reaffirmed on 1 September 2025 that all teachers up to junior high school level must pass TET within two years under the RTE framework. CTET participation and eligibility challenges The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) recently conducted the Central Teacher Eligibility Test (CTET) on 7 and 8 February in two shifts each day. According to the Uttar Pradesh Junior High School Teachers’ Association, around 50,000 teachers from the state appeared for the examination. The results are yet to be declared. The schedule for the UP Teacher Eligibility Test has not been finalised but is expected in the first week of July. Many teachers are awaiting this opportunity. However, around 80,000 teachers who are B.P.Ed and Intermediate pass face a particularly difficult situation, as TET eligibility requires a graduation degree along with D.El.Ed or B.Ed. These teachers may not even be eligible to sit the examination, deepening the uncertainty surrounding their future employment.

stories.title: SP's protest demonstration outside Jalkal office:Says, 'People of Bajardiha ward are troubled by sewer problem', officials asked for 10 days time
stories.summary: In Ward No. 27 of Varanasi's Azad Nagar (Bajardiha), local residents staged a sit-in protest at the Jalkal Department office regarding the ongoing problem of sewer blockage and waterlogging that has persisted for the past two years. Samajwadi Party (SP) workers were also among the protesters, who sat on the ground, raised slogans, and submitted a memorandum to departmental officials. Demand raised to fix sewer line It is alleged that due to blocked sewer lines, dirty water remains filled in roads and streets, which is hindering movement. The waterlogging has also increased the risk of infectious diseases in the area. Despite filing complaints multiple times, no permanent solution to the problem has been implemented, which has caused anger among the people. During the sit-in, the Jalkal General Manager, Secretary, and other senior officials were busy in a meeting with the Municipal Commissioner. Meanwhile, Rewari Talab Chowki in-charge Shivam Srivastava reached the protest site and informed senior officials about the situation over the phone. After his intervention, the department assured to immediately send employees to the spot to start cleaning work. Administration asked for 10 days time Aman Yadav said - Officials assured that the campaign will continue until satisfactory cleaning of sewers and the drainage system is completed. Also, 10 days time was requested for a permanent solution to the problem. The protest ended after the administration's assurance. Abdullah Shahid, Babu Bharti, and a large number of local citizens were present at the demonstration.

stories.title: Virat Kohli, Anushka Sharma meet Premanand Maharaj:Couple were in Ashram for 1 hour; fourth Vrindavan visit in last one year
stories.summary: Cricketer Virat Kohli arrived in Vrindavan on Tuesday with his wife Anushka Sharma. Both visited Saint Premanand at Keli Kunj Ashram. This is their fourth meeting with Premanand ji this year. During this time, both sat with folded hands in front of the saint. Both of them sat with the other devotees during their visit. They reached the Ashram at around 5:30 AM in the morning and stayed there for approximately 1 hour. Virat, Anushka reached Vrindavan on Monday evening. They stayed in a hotel, and in the morning reached the Ashram in their car. People in the know of the things said the couple reached the Ashram before time. They subsequently left for Delhi. When did Anushka-Virat meet Premanand Maharaj, and what did they talk about.... December 16, 2025: Wore the Guru Diksha kanthi (necklace) On December 16, Virat and Anushka were seen wearing Tulsi Mala Kanthi around their necks. Both have taken initiation (diksha) from Saint Premanand. In the Vaishnava tradition, the guru gives the Kanthi mala only after initiation. However, Kellykunj Ashram has not yet confirmed this. Anushka said - Maharaj ji, we are yours and you are ours. To this, Premanand ji said with a smile - We all belong to Shriji. Live with great joy. Be happy. Be dependent on God. Premanand ji said- Consider your work as service to God. Be earnest. Be humble. Life must be made progressive. Until God is found, our journey must not stop. We cross all worldly and transcendental realms. Once, also see Thakurji, to whom we truly belong. May 14, 2025: Virat-Anushka stayed in the ashram for 2 hours and 20 minutes Virat Kohli had arrived to meet Premanand Maharaj with Anushka after retiring from Test cricket. Both prostrated themselves and sought blessings. Premanand Maharaj asked Virat and Anushka - Are you happy? To this, Virat smiled and said - Yes. The Maharaj blessed both - Go, remain very joyful, keep chanting the name. To this, Anushka asked - Baba, will everything be fulfilled by chanting the name? The Maharaj said - Yes, everything will be fulfilled. Premanand Maharaj said - "Attaining opulence is not grace. It is merit. God's grace is to change the inner contemplation. This burns the impressions of your infinite births, and the next birth becomes very excellent. When God bestows grace, He grants the company of saints. When the second grace occurs, He gives adversity and then an inner path. This is not the path of peace. God gives that path and calls the soul to Himself. Without adversity, attachment to the world is not destroyed. Anushka-Virat stayed in the ashram for about 2 hours and 20 minutes. January 10, 2025: Premanand Maharaj had said - Keep practising, victory is certain Virat Kohli, along with his wife Anushka Sharma and both children, reached Premanand Maharaj's ashram. Anushka sought blessings from Premanand Maharaj for devotion. During the conversation, Virat asked, 'How to overcome failure?' Maharaj replied, 'Keep practising, victory is certain. Continue your practice consistently and with control. Just as chanting is a spiritual practice for me, cricket is a spiritual practice for Virat. Just keep taking God's name occasionally.' He said, 'Two things are required for victory: one is practice, and the other is destiny (prarabdha). If there is no destiny, only practice, then victory becomes difficult. For this, along with the knowledge of God, chanting His name is essential.' Anushka asked, 'Last time when we came, I had some questions in my mind, but I couldn't ask them. I was talking to you in my mind. Whatever questions I had in my mind, someone or the other would ask them.' Premanand Maharaj said - Shriji makes those arrangements. The biggest thing is, we are giving happiness to people through spiritual practice. And they give happiness to the whole of India in a game. If they win, firecrackers are set off all over India. Joy is celebrated across India. Is this not their spiritual practice? This is also their spiritual practice. The whole of India is connected with them. If they win, every child becomes happy, so this is also a spiritual practice. Virat asked - How should we conduct ourselves in failure? Maharaj said - At that time, we must have patience while contemplating God. This is very difficult. If someone can patiently smile and get through failure, it is a very big deal. Failure will not last forever. If there is day, night will come; if there is night, day will come. We should patiently remember God. But this is very difficult, because the respect one gets in success is not received in failure.

stories.title: Police Scorpio crashes into tree, inspector dies:5 police personnel injured, were returning to Gorakhpur after raid
stories.summary: A Gorakhpur police team's speeding Scorpio crashed into a tree. A sub-inspector died in the accident. A female sub-inspector and a senior SI, along with five policemen, were injured. The police team was returning after conducting a raid in Kushinagar. Initial investigation revealed that the driver dozed off on the highway, causing the Scorpio to climb onto the divider and then collide with a tree. Hearing the screams, nearby people arrived and helped transport everyone from the vehicle to the hospital. Pictures have emerged after the accident. In these, policemen can be seen writhing in pain on the road. The collision was so severe that the front portion of the Scorpio was badly damaged. The accident occurred on Tuesday at 6:30 AM in the Katarari area of the Shyamdeurwa police station limits. See the pictures related to the accident- The team was returning after conducting a raid According to police, the Ramgarhtal police station team had gone to the Khadda area of Kushinagar to conduct a raid in a fraud case. The team included SSI Ramesh Chandra Kushwaha, Inspector Santosh Kumar, Inspector Geeta, the driver, and 6 policemen. After the raid, the team was returning to Gorakhpur. During this time, the Scorpio suddenly went out of control and overturned in Maharajganj. All policemen were injured in the accident. Immediately after the accident, people from nearby arrived and pulled the injured policemen out of the vehicle. Police were informed. The injured were brought to Gorakhpur for treatment. Inspector Santosh Kumar, posted at Ramgarhtal police station, died during treatment at BRD Medical College. Senior SI and female sub-inspector in critical condition In the accident, SSI Ramesh Chandra Kushwaha, Sub-Inspector Geeta, and driver, along with 5 policemen, are injured. The condition of the SSI and female sub-inspector is reported to be serious, while the driver is out of danger. 2 policemen have minor injuries. Upon receiving information about the accident, police officers reached the medical college and inquired about the condition of the injured. SI was a resident of Bihar's Siwan Inspector Santosh Kumar, who lost his life in the accident, was originally from Sahasrawan village in Siwan district of Bihar. He was currently posted at Ramgarhtal police station in Gorakhpur. Upon receiving information about the incident, his family members have left from the village for Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Agra records hottest day in 23 Years at 32.2°C:Rain expected in Uttar Pradesh soon; likely to damage crops
stories.summary: The cold is gradually subsiding in UP. Cold is felt only in the morning and night. Strong sunlight is coming out during the day. However, the weather is going to deteriorate again in the state. The Meteorological Department has issued a 2-day rain alert in the state. Not only this, the temperature is expected to drop due to snowfall in the mountains. Meanwhile, Agra has broken the 23-year summer record in the state. The temperature here has reached 32.2 degrees Celsius. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said - In Agra, the temperature had gone up to 32.1C in 2003. Lucknow Weather Center scientist Atul Singh said- Western disturbance is becoming active again. This may cause rain in some parts of the state on February 18 and 19. Winds will also blow at a speed of 30 to 40 kilometers per hour. Rain will damage crops If it rains with strong winds, wheat and mustard crops may fall. This will weaken the grains and affect the yield. Therefore, the meteorological department has asked farmers to stay alert and advised against keeping harvested crops in open spaces. How has the weather been so far Noida-based Skymet Weather expert Mahesh Palawat says - UP experienced less cold this time compared to 2 years. The average maximum and minimum temperatures in December-January remained above normal. A 36 percent decrease was seen between January 1 and February 11. Extreme cold was not observed this time. Due to La Nina not being active, it couldn't get very cold. Mohammad Danish, scientist at Lucknow Meteorological Center, also says that this time the activity of western disturbances was less during the winter season in the state. This resulted in below-normal rainfall during the cold season. BHU weather scientist Professor Manoj Srivastava says - Now the cold is in its final phase. Temperature will gradually increase in the coming days. Spring season is currently ongoing. There won't be major changes in weather for next 2-3 weeks. During this time, mornings and nights will remain slightly cold, while afternoon sun will feel somewhat intense. According to weather expert Mahesh Palawat, light drizzle may be seen in many districts of UP around February 18. This includes areas like Hathras, Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Banda, Lalitpur and Jhansi. Now read when intense heat will occur and how high temperatures will reach 1- Heat wave begins from first week of March BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava says - weather will start changing completely from the first week of March and the heat wave period will begin. Temperature will rise rapidly during both day and night. By the last week of March, maximum temperatures in many districts of UP could reach 35 to 38 degrees Celsius. 2- Temperature will reach 42 to 45 degrees in May-June Manoj Srivastava says - In April, the temperature is likely to remain around 40 degrees Celsius. In May-June, the maximum temperature in many districts could reach 42 to 45 degrees. This means that not only during the day, but even at night there will be less relief from heat and humidity will persist. However, this will largely depend on the El Nio conditions. If El Nio conditions persist or strengthen, the heat situation could become even more severe. 3- Heat wave will last longer Maximum and minimum temperatures will remain above normal during March to May across the country including UP. Only in March, both maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain above normal throughout the country. Additionally, the number of heat wave days will also be higher than normal. Heat wave days will remain normal only in northeastern India and peninsular states like Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. 4- Crops will be damaged due to heat BHU's Agriculture Department Professor PK Singh says - March month could prove challenging for farmers. The rise in temperature will affect the Rabi crop. Especially wheat. Due to heat, the grains will not develop fully. This will result in lower yield. According to PK Singh, hot winds can also damage crops like mustard, chickpea and peas. Due to rising temperatures, the soil in fields dries up quickly. This increases irrigation costs. Crops face stress. 5- Early onset of heat, conditions will worsen further According to Dhruvsen Singh, Head of Department of Geology at Lucknow University, the heat has increased earlier than usual in 2026. Heat wave events may occur more frequently and for longer durations. Conditions could become more severe in urban areas due to the urban heat island effect. All these factors combined are continuously pushing temperatures upward. 125-year record broken in February 2025 After 1901, it was the first time in February 2025 when the average minimum temperature remained above 15 degrees Celsius. The year 1901 is when temperature records began to be maintained across the world including India. On the other hand, January 2025 was the third warmest month since 1901. According to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), 2024 was the hottest year on record. The Earth's average temperature increased by 1.55 degrees Celsius that year. Severe Heat Will Also Impact Worldwide According to a report by Environment and Climate Data UK, 2026 could be among the 4 hottest years ever recorded globally. It is estimated that the world's average temperature could be 1.4 to 1.5 degrees Celsius higher compared to historical times. This clearly indicates that the pace of climate change has still not slowed down. Experts say that the continuous increase in greenhouse gases and natural causes like El Nino are raising Earth's temperature. This is directly affecting people's health, agriculture and daily life. Now learn about La Nina and El Nino La Nina: La Nina is a climate pattern that affects weather worldwide. In this pattern, ocean water becomes colder than normal. When this water rises as vapor, clouds form. It rains in many places. Whether India will receive less or more rain, experience cold or heat largely depends on La Nina. In 2025, before winter began, the Meteorological Department had predicted that La Nina could become active. This was expected to bring more cold weather to North India. However, La Nina conditions did not develop in the Pacific Ocean. Therefore, there was no significant increase in cold weather. At the start of the winter season, the US weather agency NOAA had also said that there was about a 60 percent chance that La Nina would be active during winter. Its effects were expected to be visible until March, but this did not happen. El Nino- Whether it's El Nino or La Nina, both these geographical phenomena occur in the world's largest ocean, the Pacific Ocean. Whenever El Nino occurs, the monsoon in India weakens. This causes drought in many states of the country. However, meteorologists have currently only expressed concerns about El Nino. They say that if such conditions develop, the country could experience severe heat.

stories.title: ₹8 lakh robbed near Kanpur police post:Four attackers on two bikes hit man with pistol butt; escape with bag containing cash
stories.summary: A robbery of ₹8 lakhs occurred in broad daylight just 200 meters away from a police post in Kanpur. 4 criminals on two motorcycles hit the young man on the head with a pistol butt and fled after snatching his bag. Upon receiving information about the incident, DCP and ADCP arrived at the scene with the police force. The incident took place near Shatabdi Udyan turn close to Shyamnagar police post. A video of the robbery has also surfaced. It shows some bikers assaulting a young man on the roadside. As soon as people started gathering, the criminals on bikes fled from the scene. Mohammad Wasid, a resident of Yashoda Nagar in Thana Naubasta area, said - I had sold village land. On Monday, after withdrawing about ₹8 lakh rupees from a bank in Civil Lines, I was returning on a bike. My friend Arsad was also with me. Between around 6 and 6:30 PM, we were heading towards the bypass from Shatabdi Udyan, about 200 meters from the Shyamnagar police post. We stopped near a tree to urinate. Just then, 4 criminals came on two bikes from behind. As soon as we resisted, they attacked our heads with the butt of a pistol. Police took the young man to the police post Mohammad Wasid was just providing information about the robbery incident when police personnel took him inside. When the victim came out with his family, he refused to say anything. While family members also started denying the robbery incident. Eyewitnesses said - 6 criminals came on 3 bikes. They first beat both youths with helmets. After that, they took out a pistol. After this, people could not gather the courage to save the youths. DCP East Satyajeet Gupta said- The victim is denying the incident of robbery. Meanwhile, no complaint has been filed by the victim and family members. After this, the injured person's family members took him away with them.

stories.title: Congress MP, 200 workers under house arrest in UP:Assembly protest announced, Ajay Rai says, 'Barricades will be broken today'
stories.summary: The UP Congress has announced a plan to surround the state assembly in Lucknow over the issues of MGNREGA and Shankaracharya. Workers from across the state are reaching the city. The budget session is currently underway in the assembly, prompting the police to go on high alert. The Congress office has been turned into a garrison. PAC personnel have arrived in two trucks, and forces from four police stations have been deployed. More than 200 workers, including Barabanki MP Tanuj Puniya, were placed under house arrest while heading to Lucknow. The police stopped them and sent them back. However, Pratapgarh Congress district president Dr. Neeraj Tripathi managed to bypass the police and is on his way to Lucknow. State Congress President Ajay Rai said the protest would raise several issues, including alleged plans to weaken MGNREGA, an insult to women, disrespect towards Shankaracharya and Mata Ahilyabai Holkar, and the destruction of traditional markets such as dal mandis. In Raebareli, Congress National Secretary Sushil Pasi was placed under house arrest by the police. This led to a heated argument. He told the inspector, “You brought forces into my house. The children are scared. Are you bullying in the name of the BJP?” To be updated….

stories.title: Ghaziabad sisters’ deaths spark digital addiction debate:Excessive foreign digital content exposure takes toll on teenagers’ mental health
stories.summary: The deaths of 3 minor sisters in Ghaziabad have sparked serious concerns about online culture and digital addiction among children. The incident is being seen not only as a tragedy but also as a social warning about the growing influence of foreign digital content on Gen-Z. In early February, sisters Nishika (16), Prachi (14), and Pakhi (12) allegedly jumped from the ninth floor after their father tried to restrict their exposure to Korean web series, films, music, and games. Investigators found they were deeply immersed in Korean culture and identified themselves with it. Their suicide note stated that “Korean was our life” and expressed distress over marriage, saying they could not imagine marrying an Indian man. The note also mentioned their liking for content from Korea, Thailand, the US, Japan, and China, along with several games and cartoons, reinforcing their emotional attachment to this digital world. What exactly is the Korean love game? First, it is important to understand that Korean game is not an official or popular mainstream game category. In this case, the game being referred to is being called 'Korean Love Game' or 'Korean Lover Game' in different reports. According to Noida's cyber expert Dr. Rakshit Tandon, this is not a game, but Korean web series, K-pop dramas, movies, and music available on online platforms. What are Korean Dramas? Korean dramas are TV and web series made in South Korea. These are typically presented with complete stories in limited episodes. These dramas present subjects like romance, family, thriller, and fantasy in an emotional style. Are Korean web series or dramas banned in India? No, Korean web series or drama shows are not banned at the national level by the government in India. These shows are legally available on OTT platforms in India. People do watch them. Is Korean culture popular among Gen-Z? 16-year-old Raj (changed name) from Etah district is a fan of Korean culture. His hairstyle and dress are quite similar to those of Korean youth. Raj says that Korean boys and girls have very glowy skin. They look quite good. Raj says that among boys, watching BTS shows, following them on social media, and knowing every update is common. Meanwhile, Korean girl group Blackpink is also very popular among Gen-Z. Raj admits that he often watches BTS live or old shows until 3-4 AM. However, he doesn't find anything wrong with it. He says that they are truly dashing. Every fan wants to be like them. In college, teenagers generally prefer discussing Thai dramas, K-dramas (Korean dramas), and C-dramas (Chinese dramas) more than Bollywood or Hollywood, and enjoy learning new things about them. Raj's friend Mahima (changed name) says that she is completely dedicated to the BTS Army. From her t-shirts and bags to her bed sheets, everything has printed photos of the BTS group members. Her parents also know that she likes Korean bands. They don't say anything about her preferences. Why do youngsters connect with Korean dramas? According to cyber expert Dr. Rakshit, the glamour, emotional stories, and perfect lifestyle shown in Korean dramas quickly attract youth. In these stories, youngsters start relating themselves to the actors/actresses' emotions, loneliness, struggles, and relationships. K-pop singers' songs there are written especially keeping youth in mind. These songs contain positive messages like maintaining strong friendships, supporting each other, and fulfilling one's dreams. These deeply influence young people. Are Korean web series dangerous for children? Cyber experts say that the danger is not Korean content, but excessive and unguided content consumption. Parents hand their phones to children during their busy time. They don't pay attention to what the child is watching and doing. The child starts getting disconnected from real life, and that's alarming. But parents don't pay attention to this. Dr. Amit Shahi, psychiatrist at Gorakhpur District Hospital, says - In the digital age, web series and online games are no longer just entertainment. They have started influencing children's thinking, behavior, and decisions. This effect is particularly profound on teenage children. The teenage brain is still developing. They quickly believe what they see. It becomes difficult to differentiate between fiction and reality. How do web series and games affect children's minds? Experts say that children quickly believe the violent, emotional, or fantasy content shown in web series and games. The distinction between fiction and reality starts to blur. The algorithm of online platforms also plays an important role in this. Once a particular type of content is watched, related web series, reels, and games are repeatedly shown. This gradually makes the child sink deeper into that digital world. The tasks, levels, and reward systems present in online games create mental pressure on children. The desire to win and progress often turns into addiction. This directly affects children's sleep, studies, and family relationships. Using a mobile for long periods leads to symptoms like irritability, loneliness, anger, and sudden behavioral changes. Do online games really target children? Cyber expert Dr. Rakshit Tandon explains - A case like Blue Whale game has come up before. In which tasks were given for about 50 days. In the end, incidents of taking steps like self-harm had come to light. However, it is not necessary to have complete similarity in every case. But the pattern of task-based control and mental pressure may appear similar in many cases. Dr. Tandon also clarifies that not every Korean or online game is dangerous. Many legitimate and safe games are played worldwide. The real danger comes from unauthorized, suspicious, and emotionally manipulative apps and online challenges. These target the mental vulnerabilities of children and teenagers. In addition, cases of targeting children have also emerged through some chat groups and private messaging platforms present on social media, where attempts are made to gradually put them under mental pressure. According to Dr. Rakshit Tandon, even 10-11-year-old children today are playing online games made for 17-18-year-old youth. Parents need to pay attention to this. Parental control is necessary. How did Korean culture start in the country? The growing trend towards Korean culture is not sudden; it's the result of a gradually built cultural acceptance. This is called Hallyu or the Korean Wave. In India, it is believed to have started in 2000 from the northeastern states, especially Manipur. People there first began watching Korean content. After this, the COVID lockdown helped spread this trend across the country. Young people confined to homes made Korean dramas and music their source of entertainment on Netflix and other OTT platforms. From here, the popularity of Korean content grew rapidly.

stories.title: Massive voter participation in SIR as parties lag behind:Only 1% claims filed by political groups; lakhs of voters file form-6 independently
stories.summary: Under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) program, objections for removing names of about 125,000 voters have been received by the Election Commission of India. Meanwhile, 5.1 million people have applied to add their names. The Samajwadi Party has been continuously accusing the BJP and Election Commission of conspiring to remove names on a large scale. In this context, it is reasonable to ask how many applications BJP has submitted for adding and removing names? How many applications have SP and other political parties made? How much substance is there in SP's allegations? What does the Commission have to say? Read this special report... The Election Commission has extended the time for claims and objections by one month. Previously this was until February 6, which has been extended to March 6. According to Commission data, most applications received so far have been submitted by common voters themselves to the BLO (Booth Level Officer). Whether it's Form-6 for adding names or Form-7 for removing names, political parties' participation has remained less than one percent. So far, a total of 51 lakh 43 thousand 362 people have submitted Form 6 to the Commission. Of these, the number of Form-6 submitted by political parties is only 40,284. In this too, SP and BJP together have submitted the maximum 36,950 forms. Similarly, objections have been received regarding one lakh 18 thousand 688 voters. This includes only 1790 objections from political parties. BJP has filed the maximum 1729 objections. SP filed objections against 47 voters. The deadline for claims and objections is March 6. Hearings will be completed by March 27 and final publication of voter list will be on April 10. Applications increased after extending time period Election Commission data shows that after extending the deadline for claims and objections by one month, the number of applications increased rapidly. On February 6, Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa had informed in a press conference that in 30 days from January 6 to February 4, about 37 lakh 80 thousand people had filled Form-6 to add their names. While more than 82 thousand people had submitted Form-7 to remove their names. During this period, an average of 1 lakh 26 thousand Form-6 and about 2756 Form-7 were being filled daily. But when the last date for applications was extended by one month on February 6, the pace increased further. SP's allegation - BJP getting names removed The Samajwadi Party alleges that BJP and the Commission together want to remove people's votes on a large scale. Form-7 is being filled fraudulently for this. SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav has alleged that BJP workers are filling Form-7 on a large scale by forging voters' signatures to remove people's names fraudulently. These forms are filled using computers. On February 16, Akhilesh Yadav also said that attempts are being made to remove names of SP workers and legislators' families through Form-7. He has demanded an investigation into the forms that were filled anonymously. Names should be made public of those whose names were submitted for removal through Form-7 and those who filed objections for name removal. Akhilesh Yadav has said that party legislators will meet the Chief Electoral Officer. They will complain about irregularities happening in SIR. They will raise questions with the Commission regarding their concerns. After this, the matter will also be raised in the Assembly. Commission rejects allegations of political interference Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa says - Form-7 is filled to remove someone's name or object to someone's claim. While filling Form-7, the objector needs to provide their name, voter ID card number, the name of the person against whom the objection is being made, and the reason for objection. Form-7 is not accepted in large numbers (in bulk). Booth level agents of political parties can submit maximum 10 Form-7s in one day. They also need to provide an undertaking. Upon receiving Form-7, the ERO sends notices to both the objector and the person against whom the objection has been made. After receiving the notice, a hearing takes place. Evidence is presented during this. Then the ERO makes a decision according to the rules.

stories.title: Stone pelting hits Vande Bharat carrying RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat:Window breaks, police suspect cricket ball or mischief
stories.summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat’s train was hit by stones near Hardoi while he was travelling to Meerut. The incident damaged the window pane of one coach, but Bhagwat was safe and no injuries were reported. According to officials, the incident took place when the train was passing through the Hardoi area. A window glass of one bogey shattered after being struck by a stone. The Government Railway Police (GRP) has launched an investigation to identify those responsible. Bhagwat reaches Meerut safely, stays at Madhavkunj Mohan Bhagwat reached Meerut railway station at around 9 PM amid tight security arrangements. He got down safely and proceeded to Madhavkunj in Shatabdinagar, where he will stay during his visit. Security was heightened at the station and along his route to ensure his safety. RSS members and local organisers were present to receive him. GRP suspects cricket ball or mischief behind incident The GRP in Hardoi is examining two possible reasons behind the stone pelting. Officials said the damage may have been caused accidentally if children playing cricket near the railway track hit the train with a ball. Another possibility being considered is that some mischievous children deliberately threw stones at the moving train. Police are collecting information and verifying facts to determine the exact cause. No arrests have been made so far. Bhagwat to attend two-day dialogue programme Mohan Bhagwat is in Meerut to participate in a two-day dialogue programme scheduled on February 20 and 21. During the visit, he will interact with intellectuals from 28 districts of Meerut and the Braj region. Sources said Bhagwat may also hold discussions with athletes and listen to their social experiences. The programme is part of the RSS’s outreach efforts to engage with different sections of society. Police said further action will be taken after the investigation establishes whether the incident was accidental or intentional. Mohan Bhagwat to stay at Madhav Kunj for three days in Meerut RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will stay at Madhav Kunj in Shatabdi Nagar for three days during his visit to Meerut.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav's first dance after release from jail:Joins niece's wedding festivities in Shahjahanpur, freed 2 days ago
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav was seen dancing for the first time after his release from jail. He had arrived at his home in Shahjahanpur to attend his niece’s wedding, where he enjoyed dancing with the women of his family. A video of Rajpal’s dance has also emerged. Actor Rajpal’s elder brother, Shripal Yadav’s daughter, is getting married today, Thursday. The wedding procession is coming from Noida. On Wednesday, a music programme was organised at their ancestral home in Kundra village. Rajpal Yadav had been released from Tihar Jail just two days prior. Rajpal spent 11 days in jail Rajpal Yadav had spent 11 days in Tihar Jail in connection with a cheque bounce case. After his release, he returned home in Kundra on Wednesday, where fans, villagers, and family welcomed him. After attending his niece’s music programme, he left for Noida. Preparations for his niece’s wedding had been underway in the family for quite some time. The wedding is on Thursday, with ceremonies beginning on Wednesday evening. Since Rajpal returned home, a festive mood has prevailed in the family. On Wednesday evening, Rajpal Yadav danced enthusiastically with his family. In the video that surfaced, women and children of the family were seen forming a circle around him as they danced. Just two days earlier, a somber mood had prevailed in the village because Rajpal was in jail, but now the entire village is celebrating. Why was Rajpal Yadav in jail? In 2010, Rajpal Yadav had taken a loan of ₹5 crore from a private company, Murli Projects Private Limited, to produce the film Ata Pata Lappataa. The film flopped, and Rajpal faced financial difficulties. He could not repay the loan on time. The cheques Rajpal issued to the company bounced, prompting a complaint against him. Despite an agreement between both parties, the full payment was not made, and interest accumulated over time, increasing the total debt. In 2018, the Karkardooma Court in Delhi found Rajpal Yadav guilty and sentenced him to six months in jail. He appealed to the High Court, where he received relief multiple times due to assurances of repayment and agreement compliance. However, at the beginning of February, the Delhi High Court refused to extend previously granted concessions and deadlines. The court ordered him to surrender by 4 February, after which he surrendered around 4 PM on 5 February. Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav was granted interim bail from Tihar Jail from 17 February 2026 to 18 March. He had spent 12 days in jail over a ₹9 crore cheque bounce case. Before surrender, said: ‘I Have No Money’ Before surrendering, Rajpal stated he did not have the funds to repay the loan. When he went to jail, actor Sonu Sood appealed to the industry to help him. Following this, several people came forward to support Rajpal Yadav. Salman Khan, Ajay Devgn, and David Dhawan were among those who provided financial assistance. Rajpal Yadav was released on interim bail on 17 February 2026 until 18 March, after serving 12 days in jail. Became comedy king with films like Hungama, Hulchul Rajpal gained recognition in comedy through films like Hungama (2003), Garam Masala (2005), Chup Chup Ke (2006), Hera Pheri, and Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007). He collaborated with director Priyadarshan on nearly 8–10 films. Rajpal has won Best Versatile Actor Award Rajpal has received the Yash Bharti Award, the highest honour of Uttar Pradesh, for the 2003 film Main Madhuri Dixit Banana Chahti Hoon. This award recognised his performances in both comic and serious roles. Previously, the award had been given to Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan. Rajpal was also nominated for Best Comic Actor at Filmfare and IIFA but did not win. ‘First dream in Mumbai was just to survive’ After completing his studies at NSD, Rajpal came to Mumbai. Initially, he had no support. In an interview, he said his first dream was simply to survive in Mumbai. After some struggle, he began getting work. During those days, Rajpal fed 20–22 struggling actors at his home. Nawazuddin Siddiqui said in an interview, “Rajpal’s home was like a langar – free food and lodging.” School friends called him Chotu and Batla Rajpal Yadav is approximately 5 feet 1 inch tall. At school, due to his short height, friends called him Chhotu and Batla. At the age of 20, he got a job at the village ordnance clothing factory. In an interview, he said his marriage was arranged by his family around that time, while he had just begun his career and was living in the village. Wife passed away 15 minutes after daughter's birth In an interview, Rajpal said he was 20 years old when his first marriage, to Karuna, was arranged by his family. A year later, his daughter Jyoti was born, but his wife died 15 minutes after delivery. He said, “I was going to meet her the next day, but I had to carry her dead body on my shoulder. It is not easy to endure such pain at the age of 20.” After this, he became a single father, with Jyoti being cared for by his mother and sister-in-law. Rajpal met his second wife, Radha, in Canada while shooting Hero: Love Story of a Spy with Sunny Deol and Preity Zinta. Through a mutual friend, they connected and married on 10 June 2003. Formed his political party in 2016 In 2016, Rajpal Yadav launched a new political party, the Sarv Sambhav Party (SSP), in Vrindavan. He served as General Secretary and star campaigner but did not contest elections himself. The party’s motto was “Politics of Dialogue, Not Controversy.” Rajpal swore on the Gita, Quran, Bible, Guru Granth Sahib, Ramayana, and Constitution to work with honesty. For the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the party announced it would contest approximately 390–400 of the 403 seats. The headquarters was in Lucknow. His two brothers, Shripal Singh Yadav (Bislapur) and Rajesh Singh Yadav (Tilhar), contested from the party, but it did not achieve significant success. Rajpal Yadav survived death 3 times In an interview, Rajpal said he survived three life-threatening incidents. Once, while bathing in the Ganga, he went into deep water and lost consciousness. On another occasion, he narrowly escaped being run over by a bullock cart, and on a third, he survived a wild dog attack.

stories.title: 900 fake degrees seized from 14 universities in Kanpur:MSc math teacher ran syndicate, sold BTech degrees for 1.50 Lakhs
stories.summary: Kanpur police have uncovered a syndicate involved in manufacturing and selling fake degrees. The gang’s ringleader is an MSc-qualified mathematics teacher. Authorities recovered 900 forged degrees and other documents from 14 universities, including Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University (CSJMU). The highest number of fake degrees—357—belonged to CSJMU. The syndicate operated across nine states, providing fake degrees ranging from high school certificates to BTech, BPharma, and LLB without any examinations. Now know the complete case... Gang's mastermind is math teacher Shailendra Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal revealed on Thursday that the gang’s activities had been under investigation for some time. Following intelligence reports, Kidwai Nagar police raided Shail Group of Education near Gaushala Chauraha and arrested four young men with fake degrees. The accused identified themselves as Shailendra Kumar (Raebareli/Unchahar, residing in Saket Nagar), Nagendra Mani Tripathi (Kaushambi), Jogendra (Ghaziabad), and Ashwani Kumar (Shuklaganj). The ringleader Shailendra, MSc in Mathematics, taught children at Shail Group of Education. Nagendra holds an MCA, Jogendra completed high school, and Ashwani has passed 12th grade. Shailendra began teaching in 2003 and later started filling private forms for high school and intermediate students, eventually branching into creating fake degrees. The gang had contacts with staff from 14 universities across Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and other states. University clerks and employees also involved in the gang During interrogation, the accused admitted providing fake degrees for high school, intermediate, undergraduate, law, and pharmacy courses without exams. They also created fake mark sheets under the guise of private university enrollment. Police revealed that many university clerks and staff were part of the syndicate, supplying original certificates and mark sheets to the gang on demand. Rates for fake degrees ranged from ₹50,000 for high school/intermediate certificates, ₹1.5 lakh for BTech, ₹50,000–75,000 for graduation, ₹2.5 lakh for BPharma/DPharma, and ₹1.5 lakh for LLB. Police also identified 10 Kanpur-based lawyers who obtained fake LLB degrees from the gang. Some staff uploaded forged mark sheets online to make them appear genuine. Authorities seized post-dated cheques worth ₹50–60 lakh, as well as SBI and ICICI bank accounts linked to the syndicate, now under investigation. Fake UP Board mark sheets were also recovered. Shailendra built property worth crores using fake degrees Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal stated that Shailendra accumulated crores from these operations. He established Shail Group of Education with ₹40 lakh, purchased a ₹50 lakh apartment in Saket Nagar, a ₹30 lakh flat in Panki, a ₹75 lakh plot in Ramaipur, two plots in Bidhnau worth ₹50 lakh each, and a ₹20 lakh Seltos car. The youth found dead in Harbansh Mohal hotel was also connected to the gang Authorities noted that Anand Srivastava, 45, found dead in room 105 of Hotel Swami in Harbans Mohal on 19 February 2025, was connected to the gang. Anand, an educational counselor, provided mark sheets and degrees from Shree Krishna University to the syndicate. A suicide note indicated distress over causing trouble to others. Police revealed that several lawyers had obtained fake LLB degrees from the syndicate, facilitated by clerks from universities. These included: Naushad, Sujan, Sandeep Mishra, Randhir Singh, Md. Qasim Rizvi, Ratna Shukla, Vijay Yadav, Vishal Pal, Faizan Javed, and Shamsad from Babu Purwa. Police searching for these absconding accused Commissioner Raghubir Lal confirmed that Mayank Bhardwaj (Chhatarpur), Manish alias Ravi (Hyderabad), Vineet (Ghaziabad), Shekhu (Bhopal), and Shubham Dubey remain at large. Authorities seized forged mark sheets, degrees, grade sheets, provisional certificates, migration booklets, and a fake deputy registrar seal of CSJMU. The accused admitted issuing nearly 80 fake migration certificates.

stories.title: Yogi to visit Singapore and Japan from February 22:Investment push on agenda; to visit Hanuman temple near Tokyo
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will visit Singapore and Japan starting February 22. This will be his first visit to both countries as Chief Minister. According to the Chief Minister’s Office, he will stay in Singapore on February 23 and 24, and in Japan on February 25 and 26. The main purpose of the visit is to attract investment to Uttar Pradesh, strengthen industrial cooperation, and encourage foreign companies to invest in the state. The Chief Minister is expected to meet business leaders, investors, and officials during the tour. Will wear traditional saffron attire during the visit Yogi Adityanath will travel abroad in his traditional saffron kurta and chola. He is usually seen in this attire at government programmes in India and at international events. Political observers say saffron clothing reflects his personal and religious identity, as he is a monk of the Nath sect. Supporters view his attire as a representation of India’s cultural identity on the global stage. Some opposition leaders, however, see it as symbolic politics. It is uncommon, though not unprecedented, for constitutional authorities to travel abroad in traditional religious attire. Will visit Hanuman temple in Japan During his Japan visit, Yogi Adityanath is also expected to visit a Hanuman temple located about 40–50 kilometres from Tokyo. The visit is being seen as part of cultural and religious outreach. Officials say it reflects the cultural links between India and Japan. May wear formal shoes during foreign tour There is also discussion about his footwear. Yogi Adityanath usually wears sandals in public life, regardless of the season. However, he may wear formal shoes during this visit due to international protocol and weather conditions. Has visited several countries after becoming Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath made his first foreign visit as Chief Minister to Myanmar in August 2017, where he attended an international conference. He later visited Nepal, Mauritius, and Russia as part of official programmes. He has continued to wear saffron attire throughout his public life, including during official visits in India and abroad.

stories.title: UP's IAS Aditi marries without band or procession:Garland exchange marks union, love began during training
stories.summary: In a world full of ostentation, two young 2023-batch IAS officers have set a new example of simplicity. Aditi Varshney from Bareilly and Madhav Bhardwaj exchanged garlands and committed to each other for life. At the Alwar Collectorate in Rajasthan, the chamber was turned into a mandap. The wedding was simple, without any band, priest, or baraat. On Wednesday, the couple arrived with only their family members. The officers completed a court marriage, promising to stay together for life. IAS Madhav Bhardwaj serves as SDM in Alwar, while Aditi is SDM in Jamnagar, Gujarat. On Wednesday, they officially became life partners. Now read in detail... IAS bride and groom exchanged garlands The couple registered their marriage in front of Alwar District Collector Dr. Artika Shukla. Inside the chamber, the bride and groom exchanged garlands. Within minutes of the news spreading, nearby staff and officials arrived to witness the moment. Love story began during training Aditi and Madhav first met during training at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA). Sharing similar outlooks and a belief in living a simple life in public service, their friendship eventually blossomed into love. The couple had decided to avoid extravagance in the wedding to set an example of simplicity for the younger generation of officers and youth. Now know both of their success stories... IAS Aditi achieved success in her first attempt Currently, Aditi is posted as Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) in Jamnagar, Gujarat cadre. Her father Dinesh Varshney said that a traditional ceremony will also be organized soon in Bareilly. Father is a businessman, mother is a homemaker: She is from Biharipur in Bareilly. Her early education was also at Bishop Conrad School in Bareilly. She is the eldest among three siblings. Her father is a local cloth merchant and mother is a homemaker. Left Post Graduation for Preparation: Aditi completed her BA Honours degree from Jesus and Mary College, Delhi University. After this, she had enrolled in post graduation. However, she left her studies midway to prepare for UPSC. She cleared the UPSC Civil Services Exam in her first attempt. She secured All India 57th rank. Achieved Success Without Coaching: Aditi had mentioned in many of her interviews that she did not take any coaching for GS (General Studies). However, she joined test series for Sociology preparation. Sociology was her optional subject in UPSC Mains exam. When the UPSC result came out, she couldn't believe her success at first. Therefore, she downloaded the result PDF file again. Fulfilled mother's incomplete dream: Aditi's journey to become an IAS officer was born from her mother's unfulfilled dream. Her mother Indu Varshney, who played the role of a homemaker, also had the desire to become an IAS officer. This dream was realized by her daughter. IAS Madhav left corporate job Thought of becoming an engineer in childhood: Madhav Bhardwaj's journey from Mussoorie, Uttarakhand has been quite inspiring. In childhood, Madhav Bhardwaj dreamed of becoming an engineer instead of an IAS. After 12th, he took admission in BTech Computer Science at MNNIT, Prayagraj. Started preparation during Covid period: After obtaining BTech degree, he did MBA from IIM Ahmedabad. After this, he got a job as Product Manager at multinational company Microsoft. In 2020, the coronavirus pandemic gripped the world. Due to this, he got work from home for a long time. Missed by 3 marks in first attempt: During this time, Madhav thought of becoming an IAS. He devoted himself completely to UPSC civil services exam preparation. In his very first attempt, he missed final selection by just three marks. Got rank 536 in second attempt: Madhav cleared the Prelims, Mains and Interview rounds in his second attempt. He secured rank 536 in UPSC Civil Services Examination 2022. Currently, Madhav is serving as SDM in Alwar, Rajasthan.

stories.title: Brother commits suicide after sister breaks his toy:11-year-old found hanging in Raebareli; father says he always slept with the toy
stories.summary: In Kasarawa village, Raebareli, 11-year-old Mayank ended his life by hanging himself after a fight with his sister over a toy. During an argument, his sister, Muskaan, threw the toy on the ground in anger, breaking it. Upset by this, Mayank went to another room and hanged himself with a rope. Even after two hours, Mayank did not come out. When the family searched for him, they found his body hanging. On receiving the news, a crowd of villagers gathered. Police reached the scene, took possession of the body, and sent it for postmortem. Now the complete incident in detail... The family lives in Kasarawa village. Father Santosh earns through hard labour to support his family. Along with Sushila, they had four children: Mohini (17), Mohit (15), Muskaan (14), and Mayank (11), the youngest. Muskaan studied in Class 8 at the village primary school, while Mayank was in Class 7. Sister said - I got into a fight with Mayank Muskaan said that she and Mayank had a quarrel in the morning. Their father had asked for a bucket, but Mayank was busy playing. They fought, and Mayank complained to their mother. The mother scolded and punished both children. Later, Muskaan said she burnt two of Mayank’s plastic tractors in anger before going to school. At that time, the parents and other children were busy with construction work outside. Did not anticipate brother's anger Muskaan said she did not expect her brother to be so upset. Mayank skipped school that morning, and when the mother realized he was missing, she went to search for him. Inside the house, she found him hanging from a bamboo rod placed over sacks of paddy in his room. Seeing this, she screamed. The family immediately removed Mayank from the rope and rushed him to Bachhrawan Health Centre, but doctors declared him dead. Father said - Son used to sleep keeping the tractor nearby Santosh, Mayank’s father, said that Mayank always kept his tractor toy next to him while sleeping. He added that he was building a house about 50 meters away along with the rest of the family. When Mayank was not visible, they went looking for him. Mayank had a deep affection for his plastic tractor. The siblings had been playing together when the dispute arose. Muskaan broke both tractors in anger. Mayank loved his toy so much that he would sleep with it by his side and play with it first thing in the morning.

stories.title: Unable to bear labour pain, woman cuts abdomen with knife:Taken to hospital, baby girl delivered safely
stories.summary: A pregnant woman in Bahraich was unable to endure labour pain and injured her abdomen with a blade. She then began screaming in distress, prompting neighbours to rush to the spot. They found her in a critical condition and immediately arranged an ambulance. She was taken to Fakharpur Community Health Centre, where doctors conducted a normal delivery and she gave birth to a baby girl. However, due to her serious condition, she was referred to the district hospital and later sent to Lucknow for advanced treatment. The case falls under the Baundi police station area. Now read the full matter Police reached the hospital and recorded the woman’s statement. She said she acted in an attempt to get relief from the intense pain. The 35-year-old woman, identified as Nankai, lives in Nandwal village. Her husband died six months ago after an illness, and she has been living alone since. Around 1:30 pm on Thursday, she suddenly went into labour and began crying out in pain and distress. When she felt unable to cope, she picked up a kitchen knife and injured herself. Hearing her cries, nearby residents rushed to her house and arranged immediate medical help. Deep wound on stomach Neighbours said she had sustained a serious wound and could not deliver at home. She was rushed to the health centre, where doctors acted quickly and safely delivered the baby. After she was referred to Lucknow, her mother Neeta stayed at the hospital to care for the newborn. Nankai said - The pain was very severe, that's why I stabbed myself At the hospital, she told officials that the pain had become extremely severe and she acted in desperation to try to stop it. Shortly after giving her statement, she lost consciousness. Doctors said her condition remained critical after delivery, so she was referred onward for specialised treatment. Sent to Lucknow with mother According to district hospital staff, she was brought to the emergency ward at 3:20 pm. When her condition did not improve after initial treatment, she was referred to Lucknow’s trauma centre. Her mother accompanied her in the ambulance. Hospital official N.N. Tripathi said she had suffered a deep abdominal injury and was referred in serious condition for further care.
