stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:'AI will not take away jobs,' says Mukesh Ambani; UP deputy CMs hold talks with RSS chief after Yogi’s meeting more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. 'AI will not take away jobs,' says Mukesh Ambani The fourth day of the 'India AI Impact Summit 2026' is underway today at Bharat Mandapam in Delhi. Mukesh Ambani said the best of AI is yet to come. He adds India will emerge as one of the greatest AI powers in the 21st century. Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the summit. 2. After Yogi, UP Dy CMs meet RSS chief: Mohan Bhagwat holds talks with Brajesh Pathak Keshav Maurya after Batuk Puja After CM Yogi, both Deputy CMs Keshav Maurya and Brajesh Pathak met with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat. On Thursday morning, both Deputy CMs arrived separately at Saraswati Vidya Mandir in Nirala Nagar. 3. UP speeds up digital census preparations: 6 lakh staff to collect data through 33 key questions; survey to be conducted in 2 phases Census preparations in UP for 2027 have intensified. For the first time, the census will be conducted entirely through digital means, where 33 important questions will be asked door-to-door. These questions will form the foundation for determining budgets for roads, water, housing, schools, hospitals and government schemes in the coming years. The census will be conducted in 2 phases. 4. SC slams freebies, says, ‘Give jobs, not handouts’ Supreme Court on Thursday criticised the Tamil Nadu government over the “freebie culture.” The court said it is time to reconsider such policies, as they impact the country’s economic growth. The court further said that helping the poor is understandable, but providing free facilities to everyone without distinction is not appropriate. 5. Cab driver rapes student in Lucknow: Marries victim after pregnancy; runs away after birth of daughter Priya (name changed), a young woman from Varanasi, came to Lucknow with the dream of preparing for the NEET exam. She rented a small room in Chinhat, while her coaching classes were in Gomtinagar. During her daily commute, she befriended a cab driver named Aditya. What began as casual conversations soon turned into companionship. Aditya started accompanying her everywhere, gradually earning her trust. One day, he invited her to his room. There, he allegedly drugged and sexually assaulted her. 6. Bee attack during cricket match, kills umpire in Unnao: 8 players injured, admitted to hospital; video goes viral In Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, a swarm of bees attacked players during a local cricket match. As the bees swarmed, the umpire tried to escape but fell, sustaining more than 50 stings as the bees continued attacking him for about 10 minutes. After the incident, the umpire and 8 players were injured and taken to a private nursing home in Kanpur. 7. ‘US could strike Iran at any time,' says report Tensions between the US and Iran have escalated rapidly, and the situation has now reached a point where a major military confrontation could occur in the coming days or weeks. According to a report by the US news agency Axios, if the US takes military action, it will not be a small or symbolic strike, but a large-scale operation lasting several weeks. 8. Fake inspector’s father is a real cop: Conducting school admission test in Lucknow; found using CM advisor’s letterhead Kanpur police caught a fake inspector. He was accused of conducting recruitment exams at a private school in Lucknow under the guise of a police uniform. He was extorting money from new candidates by luring them with police department jobs. Kanpur police is investigating how many children have been cheated so far. Only 3 boys have come forward till now. 9. Ayodhya GST Deputy Commissioner’s disability certificate fake: CMO says on hidden camera it is forged, warns action; officer feared inquiry Doctors have questioned the authenticity of Ayodhya GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh’s disability certificate, calling it fake. Experts said the disease mentioned cannot occur at his age, and the hospital lacked testing equipment. Missing required authorisations raised further doubts. The controversy intensified after Singh resigned from service and withdrew his resignation days later. 10. Youth force for Imran’s release Tensions are escalating in Pakistan over demands for the release of former Prime Minister Imran Khan. Thousands of supporters of Imran’s party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), have taken control of the strategically important Attock Bridge in Khyber province on Wednesday.

stories.title: BLO teacher commits suicide in Amethi:Family claims repeated calls over Aadhaar feeding caused severe mental stress
stories.summary: A 46-year-old government teacher died by suicide in Amethi. His body was found hanging from a noose inside his room. His son has alleged that a block-level employee had telephoned and pressured his father over official work, asking him to urgently complete Aadhaar data feeding. He claims that the mounting stress led his father to take his own life. Ram Prakash Verma had been on duty in Pratapgarh for the UP Board examinations. He was also handling SIR-related responsibilities. After completing his examination duty on Wednesday, he travelled approximately 30 kilometres to his village, arriving late in the evening. After dining with his family, he went to sleep at his house located near the market. At around 11 pm on Wednesday night, his father made a phone call, but it went unanswered. Concerned, the family asked a neighbour to check on him. When the neighbour reached the house, the teacher was found hanging from a noose. The police were informed immediately. He was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The incident falls under the City Kotwali police station area. Background and family details Ram Prakash Verma was a resident of Badhaipur village in the Sangrampur police station area. While his parents lived in the village, he resided in a two-storey house built in Phulbari Bazaar. His family comprises his wife, daughter Vandana (17), and sons Alok (14) and Aman Deep (12). Both sons are students at Shiv Pratap Inter College. Owing to school holidays during the board examinations, the family had come to the village. For the past eight years, Ram Prakash had been serving as an assistant teacher at Gauhani Primary School in Pratapgarh district. The distance between his home and the school was about 30 kilometres, which he commuted daily. According to his son Alok Verma, his father also served as the Booth Level Officer (BLO) for Gauhani village. At present, he had been assigned duty for the board examinations at Gauhani Inter College. Son alleges work pressure led to tragedy Alok Verma stated that his father had been under mental strain due to continuously increasing work pressure. 'On Wednesday, after finishing his board examination duty, he returned to the village. During this time, the BRC called and instructed him to complete Aadhaar feeding under SIR at the earliest. He was warned of action if he failed to do so,' Alok said. He added that his father had shared this information with both him and his grandfather. After having dinner with the family, he left for the house in the market area. ‘At around 11 pm, grandfather called to check whether he had reached home, but the call was not answered. Despite repeated attempts, there was no response. We then asked a neighbour to check. When he arrived, the gate was closed. He looked inside and saw father’s body hanging from a noose in the hall. After that, the police were informed,’ Alok said. The family has maintained that sustained work-related stress was the primary cause behind the tragic incident.

stories.title: Madani hits back at Bhagwat's 'ghar wapsi' statements:Adds sharp jibe; says those targeting Muslims were themselves destroyed
stories.summary: An uproar has erupted over RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s statement about “ghar wapsi” of Muslims. Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind national president Arshad Madani questioned whether 200 million Muslims would be turned into Hindus and whether 60 million Christians would also be made to undergo “ghar wapsi”. He said such remarks would push the country towards disaster. Madani released a video on X and said people who were not even born 70 years ago are now talking about “ghar wapsi” of 200 million Muslims. He added it seems as if only they had drunk their mother’s milk. A voice that leads the country towards destruction and hostility cannot be called a voice of loyalty, he said. He alleged that an atmosphere of hatred is being created in the country. Speaking in the name of “ghar wapsi” about converting 200 million Muslims and 60 million Christians is not only impractical but also against the Constitution and social harmony, he added. Key points from Madani's statement 1- Islam will remain alive till the Day of Judgment: Muslims will remain firm on their religion and will not accept religious conversion under any pressure. Muslims are alive and will remain alive in their faith. Those who tried to eliminate Muslims were eliminated themselves, but Islam is alive and will remain alive till the Day of Judgment. 2- Harmony possible only through Constitution: Peace, brotherhood and mutual harmony in the country is only possible under the shadow of a secular constitution. Violence in the name of any religion cannot be accepted. All religions preach humanity, love and tolerance. 3- Mob lynching and religious violence increased: Incidents of mob lynching and religious violence are increasing in the country. Innocent people are being killed in the name of cows, churches are being set on fire and the government remains silent. 4- Both Will Bleed: Why do people who raise their voice on issues like triple talaq remain silent on other alleged atrocities? According to them, if hate politics continues, both the majority and minorities will bleed in the coming times and violence could spread in the streets and alleys. 5- Country's Real Strength, We Stand With It: The real strength of the country is its constitution. Some organizations and political forces are trying to weaken the country's secular framework. We don't have the power of authority, but we stand with the constitution. 6- Elders Made Sacrifices for Freedom: Jamiat was against hate politics before and will continue to be. Our elders made sacrifices for freedom, endured insults, but never left the path of love and brotherhood. The country runs on love, not hate. Minister Rajbhar says - Why don't Maulana talk about education Rajbhar said clerics making such statements should instead speak about education, health, employment and participation of their community. He alleged they teach the language of hatred. BJP MLA says - Maulana is ISI Agent BJP legislator Nand Kishor Gurjar said he believes the Jamiat leader provides legal help to terrorists and called him an ISI agent, claiming he may have to go to Pakistan someday. Now read RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's statement... RSS chief Bhagwat had said Tuesday in Lucknow that Muslims living in India are also Hindus and have not come from Arabia. He said efforts for “ghar wapsi” should be intensified and those who return to Hinduism should be cared for. On infiltration, he said infiltrators must be detected, deleted and deported and should not be given jobs. On declining Hindu population growth, he said Hindus should have at least three children. The current rate is 2.1 and should be at least three, he said, adding that societies with fewer than three children on average eventually disappear. Newly married couples should be told to have at least three children. He also said the purpose of marriage should be continuation of creation, not fulfilment of desire, as that brings a sense of duty. Mughals and British could not erase Hindu religion and culture On casteism, Bhagwat said 500 years of Mughal rule and 200 years of British rule could not destroy Hindu religion and culture, which shows its strength. Society must remove caste inequality collectively, not just through government or organisations. People should work for education and progress within their communities and maintain harmony with neighbours.

stories.title: Rajpal Yadav seeks smoking room in jail:Actor calls Tihar a meditation camp, visits village after interim bail
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav, who is currently out on 30-day interim bail in a cheque bounce case, visited his ancestral village Kundra in Uttar Pradesh’s Shahjahanpur district on Wednesday after being released from Tihar Jail. Speaking to reporters, Rajpal Yadav said his time in jail gave him a chance to reflect and stay calm. He described the jail experience as similar to a meditation camp. He also suggested that prison facilities should be modernised. “Just as every system in the country is being upgraded, jails should also be modernised,” he said. The actor further said separate smoking zones should be created inside jails to protect the health of other inmates. “This will ensure that others do not get affected by smoke or develop any disease,” he added. Rajpal Yadav was granted interim bail for 30 days in connection with a cheque bounce case. After his release, he travelled to his native village, where he met family members and locals. A video of his journey from the cheque bounce case to his arrest, jail stay, and release has also surfaced.

stories.title: Shankaracharya targets CM Yogi:Questions his religious conduct; gives saints 10-day ultimatum to declare stand
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimuktheshwaranand Saraswati criticised Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath during a press conference in Varanasi on Thursday. He said Deputy Chief Ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya were trying to control the situation, but some religious heads remained firm in their position. He questioned the Chief Minister’s remarks about “Kalnemi”, saying the term was not clearly explained. He asked whether such people were genuine followers of Sanatan Dharma or deceptive in their conduct. Avimuktheshwaranand gave the saint community 10 days to declare their stand. He said those who support the Chief Minister despite abandoning religious principles would face similar opposition. He also questioned whether a renunciate could hold a salaried government position after taking vows of renunciation. Questions Deputy CM’s religious gesture and government action Reacting to Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak’s worship of 101 Batuks, the Shankaracharya said the gesture showed personal sentiment but raised questions about government responsibility. He said if the matter was not political, the Batuk allegedly mistreated earlier should have been honoured. He also criticised remarks suggesting religious leaders lacked authority to act, saying such statements showed the government was unwilling or unable to take action. Calls for gathering of saints in Lucknow on March 11 Avimuktheshwaranand said saints, mahants, scholars and followers should gather in Lucknow on March 11 to present their views publicly. He claimed recent steps for cow protection were insufficient, including making a film tax-free and issuing administrative instructions on cow shelters. He also alleged that incorrect statements were made in the Assembly regarding the issue. Clash during Magh Mela triggered controversy The dispute escalated after a confrontation between police and the Shankaracharya’s followers during Mauni Amavasya at Prayagraj Magh Mela on January 18. Police stopped his palanquin and asked him to walk to the Sangam. His disciples objected, leading to a scuffle. Police detained several followers and allegedly used force. The Shankaracharya protested and remained at his camp until January 28 before returning to Varanasi. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya later said any insult to religious leaders would be investigated. CM Yogi says law applies equally to everyone Speaking in the Assembly on February 13, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said no one is above the law. He said the same legal system applies to every citizen, including religious leaders and public officials. He added that the Magh Mela was conducted under strict arrangements for millions of devotees and rules had to be followed equally by all. stories.title: SP MLA warns Brahmins will remove govt:Questions Deputy CM’s shikha ritual; Speaker lashes out at minister
stories.summary: The ninth day of the UP Assembly budget session continued on Thursday, with spirited debates, occasional light moments, and exchanges between ministers and opposition members. SP MLA Atul Pradhan took a dig at Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak’s batuk pooja, commenting on the Brahmin community’s revered status and joking about the ritual of untying the “shikha.” Pradhan added that, similar to Chanakya’s vow in legend, Brahmins would remove the Deputy CM from power if necessary. Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi’s reply sparked a reaction from Shivpal Singh, who asked, “Did you bring the budget from your home? This is the people’s money, not for self-praise.” Earlier, Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana reprimanded ministers Dinesh Pratap Singh and Narendra Kashyap for overstepping their allotted time while detailing development works in his constituency. SP lawmakers raise multiple issues SP legislators pressed several points, including AI robots linked to Noida’s Galgotia University, corruption in Varanasi’s market road payments, and inadequate fertilizer distribution. Rajendra Chaudhary highlighted farmers’ struggles, stating that despite long queues, fertilizers were unavailable while rations of lesser quantity were supplied. Ministers’ defences and achievements AK Sharma, Urban Development Minister, defended government expenditure, highlighted stray dog control initiatives, and insisted UP electricity rates have not increased for six years. Dharamveer Prajapati emphasised improvements in education, healthcare, and infrastructure, noting the expansion of medical college seats and smart transformer installations. Surya Pratap Shahi claimed irrigation projects have reached the last canals, and farmers’ incomes have more than doubled since the SP government. Suresh Khanna, Finance Minister, presented the CAG report showing rising revenue and lower expenditure, describing UP as a “surplus revenue state.” Walkouts and heated exchanges Several SP lawmakers staged walkouts in protest over farmers’ issues. Members repeatedly questioned ministers on budget allocations, project completions, and policy impacts. Speaker Mahana maintained control, requesting decorum and reminding ministers and legislators to respect allotted time. Amidst the session, lawmakers exchanged anecdotes and jabs. SP MLA Samarpal Singh narrated a story involving a BJP MLA at a roadside eatery. Speaker Mahana and ministers also teased legislators for prolonged speeches or vague questioning, adding light moments to the otherwise heated session. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya reiterated the government’s commitment to inclusive development, highlighting budget presentations as a vehicle for departmental progress and public welfare.

stories.title: UP speeds up digital census preparations:6 lakh staff to collect data through 33 key questions; survey to be conducted in 2 phases
stories.summary: Census preparations in UP for 2027 have intensified. For the first time, the census will be conducted entirely through digital means, where 33 important questions will be asked door-to-door. These questions will form the foundation for determining budgets for roads, water, housing, schools, hospitals and government schemes in the coming years. The census will be conducted in 2 phases. The census in the state is scheduled for May-June 2026, for which around 6 lakh personnel will be deployed, but with every census, some important questions also arise. For example, why don't people provide accurate information? Does registering mobile numbers in the census pose a risk of tax or any kind of investigation? What losses could common people and their areas face by hiding information, and what direct benefits will they get from providing accurate information? What are those 33 questions that will be asked from every household this time? Read in this report... Why don't people provide accurate information in the census? Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says that most people fear that providing accurate information might cause them harm. They feel that giving complete information to the government could deprive them of certain benefits they are currently receiving. For example, ration cards provide grain based on fixed units, but many people avoid stating the correct number of all family members. They fear their benefits might get reduced. For this reason, some people also try to show themselves as absent during the census so that they cannot be counted. However, this time in the census process, it has been provided that enumerators will reach out again to families found absent in the first round, so that no house or person is left out of the count. Consequences of not providing correct information in Census Not registering name or correct information in the census may cause difficulties for individuals or families in accessing government benefits in the future. If someone's name is not included in the census record, the administration may assume that person does not reside at that location. In such situations, records will be matched based on the previous 2011 census data. The verification of people who received free rations and other relief benefits during the COVID period can also be done through census data. If any person or family is found absent in the current census, their cases may be reviewed again. Government schemes and benefits such as ration, housing, pension or other assistance are often determined based on census data. In such cases, people who do not provide correct information or exclude themselves from the count may be deprived of government benefits in the future. Is there risk of tax or any kind of investigation from registering mobile number? Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says, no. There is no risk of tax or any kind of investigation from registering your mobile number in the census. Master trainers of these districts are being trained in the first phase A four-day special residential training of 285 master trainers from 27 districts is being conducted from February 17 to February 20 at the State Health and Family Welfare Institute, Lucknow under the supervision of Director Sheetal Verma. These master trainers will further train other staff in their respective districts. In the second phase, training of master trainers from the remaining districts will be conducted between February 24 to 27. Which 27 districts are included? The 27 districts whose master trainers are being trained in the first phase include Agra, Aligarh, Amroha, Baghpat, Ghaziabad, Ballia, Bijnor, Bulandshahr, Chandauli, Deoria, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Ghazipur, Hapur, Hathras, Jhansi, Lalitpur, Mathura, Mau, Meerut, Moradabad, Muzaffarnagar, Rampur, Saharanpur, Sambhal, Shamli, Sonbhadra and Varanasi. The objective of the training is to complete the census work accurately, timely and systematically, so that the Census-2027 process can be conducted smoothly. Know why census is important? Census is the most important source of information about the country. Through this, it is known where people live in the country, how they live and what facilities they need. Based on these figures, the government makes policies, starts schemes and also checks whether the existing schemes are working properly or not. Census data is used to determine representation in Parliament, State Assemblies and local bodies, as well as in the delimitation of electoral constituencies. Not just the government, but business and industry also decide where to invest and how to expand their services based on these figures. Additionally, the Finance Commission also determines grants to states keeping census data in mind. Census will be conducted in two phases The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) announced on January 8 that the first phase of Census 2027 will be conducted between April 1 and September 30. Every state and union territory will complete this work within 30 days in their respective regions. The government also said that people will be given the option of self-enumeration 15 days before the house listing begins. Actually, the census was supposed to be conducted in 2021, but it was postponed due to the coronavirus pandemic, which will now be completed in 2027. In the first phase, house listings and house data will be collected. In the second phase, the population count will be conducted. Census will be completely digital The government announced that this time the census will be completely digital. About 30 lakh employees will collect information through mobile apps. Through mobile apps, portal and real-time data transfer, the census will be largely paperless. These apps will work on both Android and iOS. Caste-related data will also be collected digitally. For the first time since independence, caste counting will be included in the census. Previously, caste-based census was conducted until 1931 during British rule. This decision was taken by the Cabinet Committee chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in April. According to the last census of 2011, India's population was about 121 crore, of which approximately 51.5% were males and 48.5% were females. Last census was conducted in 2011 Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal says that the last complete census in the country was conducted in 2011, and even today many schemes of central and state governments are running based on these figures. Due to the Corona pandemic, the 2021 census could not be conducted, due to which policies and budgets are still being determined based on old data. The 2011 census was door-to-door and paper-based. Census workers would go door-to-door filling paper forms, which took considerable time to prepare the data. This census collected not only population data, but also statistics related to housing, water, toilets, electricity, education, employment and family structure. Based on these, the requirements for roads, schools, hospitals and housing schemes were determined. Even today, many schemes like ration cards, PM Housing Scheme, Ujjwala, Swachh Bharat Mission, MGNREGA are based on 2011 figures. Data related to female literacy, gender ratio, urbanization and migration are also taken from this census. What will happen if these 33 questions are not answered? These questions asked during the census are for people. It is people's duty to answer these questions so that the government gets the correct picture. So that the shortcomings in future plans can be addressed. The ones that people are facing. It has nothing to do with citizenship. But not only should one actively participate in the census but also provide accurate information.

stories.title: After Yogi, UP Dy CMs meet RSS chief:Mohan Bhagwat holds talks with Brajesh Pathak Keshav Maurya after Batuk Puja
stories.summary: After CM Yogi, both Deputy CMs Keshav Maurya and Brajesh Pathak met with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) Chief Mohan Bhagwat. On Thursday morning, both Deputy CMs arrived separately at Saraswati Vidya Mandir in Nirala Nagar. Each had about 20-minute meetings with Mohan Bhagwat. These meetings are considered important from the perspective of coordination between government-organization and RSS. In the morning, Deputy CM Keshav Maurya arrived first to meet Bhagwat. Various political issues were discussed with Bhagwat. Shortly after, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak arrived. Several important issues were discussed with him as well. Notably, on Thursday morning, Brajesh Pathak first performed Batuk Puja at his residence. After this, he arrived to meet Bhagwat. The RSS chief is currently on a UP tour. After Gorakhpur, he arrived in Lucknow on Tuesday. Today he will leave for Meerut. During his two-day stay in Lucknow, the RSS chief focused particularly on organizational expansion and social harmony. He addressed programs organized at Lucknow University and Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. Earlier, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and CM Yogi met in Ayodhya on November 25, 2025. It was during the Dharma Dhwaja ceremony at Ram Temple. The meeting between the two lasted for about half an hour. When did Bhagwat-Yogi meet before this Read what the RSS chief said yesterday- 1- 'RSS is not BJP's remote control' RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said on Wednesday that RSS is not BJP's remote control. RSS volunteers go to BJP. They have progressed there too. But it is wrong to say that RSS controls BJP. However, those who oppose BJP are the ones who oppose RSS. Mohan Bhagwat said about American tariffs - this is their old method. They want to make others bow down through weapons and economic power. But India is so strong that it has not bowed before them. Our public is ready. Therefore, this will have no effect on India. 2- 'We are all one, untouchability must end' Bhagwat said, 'The UGC related matter is currently in Supreme Court. Whatever decision the court gives, further steps will be taken accordingly. If a law is wrong, there is also a way to change it. We are all sons and daughters of Mother India. Color, appearance or caste may be different, but the sense of belonging should remain. This feeling alone can end evils like untouchability.' 3- 'Hindu society is divided' He said, 'The system of caste should no longer exist. Earlier it was based on work, but times have changed now. The walls of caste are slowly breaking down. Hindu society has strength, but it is divided and trapped in self-interest. If society unites, it can move the country forward.' There is no opposition to new things, but imitating westernization is not right. Be modern, but don't forget your roots and culture. Joint families have now decreased, but the feeling of relationships should remain. Family should sit together at least once a week. Children get values from both home and school.'

stories.title: Cab driver rapes student in Lucknow:Marries victim after pregnancy; runs away after birth of daughter
stories.summary: Priya (name changed), a young woman from Varanasi, came to Lucknow with the dream of preparing for the NEET exam. She rented a small room in Chinhat, while her coaching classes were in Gomtinagar. During her daily commute, she befriended a cab driver named Aditya. What began as casual conversations soon turned into companionship. Aditya started accompanying her everywhere, gradually earning her trust. One day, he invited her to his room. There, he allegedly drugged and sexually assaulted her. When Priya discovered she was pregnant, Aditya proposed marriage. In the presence of two friends, they were married at Chandrika Devi temple. Afterward, the couple began living together as husband and wife. Their daughter was born, but soon after, Aditya abandoned them. He left home one day under the pretext of buying medicine and never returned. Priya’s attempts to reach him through his friends failed—her calls were blocked. When she finally managed to speak to him, his response was devastating: he refused to accept her and cruelly told her to “go and die somewhere with your daughter.” Now, Priya is struggling to survive. With no money left even to buy milk for her child, she has been wandering from place to place for over a month, seeking justice. Tearfully recounting her ordeal at the Assistant Police Commissioner’s office in Vibhuti Khand, she explained how Aditya trapped her in a web of false love, exploited her, and abandoned her when she needed him most. What's the case? Melupur Varanasi resident Priya came to Lucknow in December 2022. She was preparing for NEET while staying in a rented room in the Naubasta Chinhat area. The coaching was in Gomtinagar area. She used to go to coaching by cab. In July 2023, she booked a cab. Aditya Yadav from Barabanki came with the cab. Aditya enticed her with his words and offered to pick and drop her daily. Due to having to book a cab daily, the girl found his proposal reasonable and agreed. After this, Aditya started dropping the girl from home to coaching. During this time, they talked and became friends. Priya expressed her desire to learn driving. On this, Aditya taught her driving for free. While teaching driving, Aditya would often talk about love and romance. But Priya kept ignoring it. Victim's story Got married in temple after trapping in love Priya said that Aditya kept expressing his love continuously. "When I asked him to meet my family, he said he would arrange it soon. After gaining trust, he increased closeness. After this, he started accompanying me everywhere. One day he took me to his room on some pretext. He mixed intoxicants in tea and made me drink it. I became unconscious. He had physical relations while I was intoxicated. When I regained consciousness, I couldn't understand anything. After a month, I found out I was pregnant. On this, Aditya proposed marriage, which I accepted. Then we got married in Chandrika Devi temple. Continued meeting for a month after pregnancy Priya said - For a month after the incident, Aditya kept bringing and taking her by cab. When he found out about my pregnancy, he planned for family. Said we will raise this child. Trusting him, I agreed. For the first five months, stayed at home in Barabanki. Then the belly started growing due to pregnancy. After this, had to stop coming and going home. Thought would fix everything later by telling the family. During this time, asked Aditya many times to take her to his home, but he kept avoiding. However, Aditya stayed with her and continued the treatment. On February 2, she gave birth to a daughter in a private hospital. After this, Aditya got her discharged from the hospital and took her to a room. He rented a room on the third floor in Naubasta. He stayed there for three days. Then he left home saying he was going to get medicine, but never returned. Refused to accept the child and me Tried to contact him on mobile, but it was switched off. When contact was made after several attempts, he refused to accept us. When asked to return for the sake of the child, he said you are not my wife. Go die with your daughter. Then he switched off his mobile. After this, a complaint has been filed with the police. Priya said, 'My mother doesn't know anything' Priya said, "There is only mother in the family. She doesn't know about this. I am very broken after this betrayal. Now there isn't even a grain of rice at home to eat. I can't even buy necessary items for the baby. I don't have money left even to feed milk." Police not taking action Priya filed written complaints with Chinhat police station and ACP Vibhuti Khand. No hearing was held on either. Following this, Priya met Joint CP Bablu Kumar on February 18 and complained. She demanded action in the matter. He assured appropriate action in the case. SHO Chinhat Dinesh Chandra Mishra said that according to the victim student, her husband has been missing since the birth of their daughter. Her family members were also giving threats. He said that a case has been registered based on the student's complaint. Whatever evidence comes forward in the investigation will be added to the inquiry and legal action will be taken.

stories.title: Ayodhya GST Dy Commissioner’s disability certificate forged:CMO admits on hidden camera, warns of action
stories.summary: This certificate is completely fake because this disease (macular degeneration) cannot occur at this age (31 years) - Dr. Vakil Ali, In-charge CMO, District Hospital, Mau (regarding Prashant Singh's disability certificate) There was no machine for testing macular degeneration disease in Mau District Hospital then, nor is there now - Dr. LS Chaubey, Eye Surgeon, District Hospital, Mau (Prashant Singh's disability certificate was made from here, for which an OCT machine is necessary for eye examination) If there are signs of an eye expert and nodal officer, then this disability certificate will be valid everywhere except for government jobs. - Dr. Ghanshyam Yadav, Retired CMO, Gonda (Prashant Singh's disability certificate has only 3 signs, not 2) From the above facts, it is clear that the disability certificate of Ayodhya's GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh is fake. This is the same Prashant Kumar Singh who resigned from government service in Ayodhya on January 27 and withdrew it 4 days later. He cried in front of the media and stated the reason for his resignation as Swami Avimukteshwaranand's comment, in which he spoke against CM Yogi. Prashant was accused of the reason for his resignation was not to support CM Yogi, but to save himself from action regarding his fake disability certificate, because the investigation has been going on for 5 years and he is not cooperating with the investigation, hence he is avoiding going before the medical board for an eye examination. The board has called him 4 times so far. Whereas, Prashant Singh obtained government service from the disabled quota based on this very disability certificate. Is Prashant Singh's disability certificate fake? To answer this question, Dainik Bhaskar's team investigated, and one by one, all the layers began to unfold. Read the full revelation First, know what Prashant said when he resigned? I have resigned I couldn't tolerate it One should fulfill their duty to the one whose salt they eat The state whose bread I eat The state whose salary supports my family If the head of that state who has been constitutionally elected is subjected to unparliamentary words then I will certainly feel pain. Now, let's talk about Prashant Singh's disability certificate This certificate was issued by the CMO office in Mau, but no date is recorded on it. When Prashant requested a copy of the certificate from the CMO office in 2012 to apply for a government job, the date of issue of this certificate was recorded as October 27, 2009. On the certificate, Prashant's age is written as 31 years. In the place of illness, it is written - Macular Degeneration Left Eye and Loss of Vision Right Eye, meaning there is Macular Degeneration disease in the left eye and the vision in the right eye is weak. In the certificate, Prashant has been declared 40% disabled. It states Prashant has permanent disability. It is signed by Eye Surgeon YP Gupta. Elsewhere, above Prashant's photo, there are also his signatures with a seal. In place of the CMO, there are the signatures and seal of Nodal Officer Dr. Brij Kumar. At one place, there are the signatures of an Ortho Surgeon, but not of an ENT Surgeon and Physician. We reached Mau, 350 km from Lucknow. Here we met the in-charge CMO, Dr. Vakil Ali. We spoke to him on a hidden camera. He made several revelations during the conversation. He clearly stated - the certificate is fake. Why is it fake? He also explained the reason. Reporter: Is Prashant Singh's disability certificate fake...? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: This is completely fake because macular degeneration cannot happen This disease cannot occur at the age of 31 It cannot occur below 40 years of age Whatever it is, it will be after 40 Glasses will also not work in this and a person cannot read or write. Reporter: Has any such certificate been issued here before? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: No, it is not issued at all. Reporter: Is the doctor who issued it guilty or not? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: Definitely guilty. We wanted to understand how this disease occurs? For this, we asked the In-charge CMO to explain it completely. After this, Dr. Vakil Ali picked up a pen and paper and explained with a diagram why this certificate is fake. The doctor who wrote this disease was also a fool In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: This is the optic disc this is the optic nerve these are several layers of the retina there are about 10 layers of the retina then the lens is attached here this is the eye in this, the macular degeneration occurs in this disc where the optic nerve is the focal point on this is the macula this is sensitive Look, I'm telling you unofficially the doctor who wrote this disease if he hadn't written this he would have been saved he was also a fool just understand this, 'Vinash kale vipreet buddhi' (When destruction is near, one's intellect works against them). Reporter: Tell me... will this illness be proven in the medical board or will it be proven fake...? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: It will be proven fake... Reporter: Is this why Prashant Singh has not appeared before the medical board 4 times...? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: Yes... that's why he's not appearing... this is the reason it will be proven fake... Reporter: Finally, what do you think, will Prashant escape...? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: He won't escape... but it requires someone to fight... even the media gets managed in this... Reporter: If the investigation is done honestly, then...? In-charge CMO Dr. Vakil Ali: He's caught... Now the question before us was whether doctors can diagnose the disease macular degeneration, which is written in Prashant Singh's disability certificate, just like that, or if a machine is needed? Which machine is that? Is that machine available in the hospital from where Prashant's certificate was issued? To find an answer to this, we reached the ophthalmology department of the same district hospital in Mau, where Prashant's eyes were examined to issue this certificate. Dr. Y.P. Gupta, who issued the certificate here, has retired. In the ophthalmology department, we met eye surgeon Dr. L.S. Chaubey. Reporter: Sir, there is a disease called Macular Degeneration, at what age does it occur? Dr. Chaubey: Yes it's an age-related disease it occurs only after 60 years of age. Reporter: What are its symptoms? Dr. Chaubey: In this, vision will not come if the line is straight it will appear crooked it looks smaller or larger than the actual size. Reporter: Is this a progressive (worsening with age and not completely curable) disease? Dr. Chaubey: Yes it's a progressive disease. Reporter: Has any patient aged 30-35 years come? Dr. Chaubey: No... this disease does not occur at this age... Reporter: Which machine is here to diagnose this disease...? Dr. Chaubey: There is no machine here for this... we send them outside for diagnosis... Reporter: Do you also do this...? Dr. Chaubey: Yes... we also send them to BHU first... we don't want to take it upon ourselves... that's why we send them... Reporter: In Prashant Singh's case, the medical board called him 4 times for examination... he didn't come... what does that mean...? Dr. Chaubey: It means he is fake... Reporter: The doctor who made the certificate... must have taken some benefit...? Dr. Chaubey: Yes... absolutely must have... Everyone loves for their own self-interest... Without self-interest, does anyone do good for others...? After this, I spoke to 3 eye specialists and understood whether a person suffering from macular degeneration can live a normal life or not? Know the answers from all these doctors - This disease affects people over 60 years of age Dr. D.K. Sarraf, Senior Ophthalmologist at Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Hospital, Lucknow, said- This is an old age disease... It affects people over 60 years of age... For the diagnosis of this disease, fundus examination is done at a basic level... For advanced diagnosis, OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography) machine is used... . Black spots will appear, unable to read or write Dr. Pooja Mishra, Retina Specialist at Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Hospital in Lucknow, said - This disease is age-related... In this, base products accumulate on our macula, due to which light cannot pass through. In this, the patient sees black spots. There is no spectacle number in this, wearing any glasses does not affect the vision, in this, the person reading and writing will not be able to see properly, whatever they see... they will see black spots. This is a progressive disease, it increases with age. Dr. Kusum Kala, HOD of the Ophthalmology Department at Balrampur Hospital, Lucknow, said - This disease causes blurred vision, it occurs only after the age of 45, it is a progressive disease, it increases with age. If there is an objection to the certificate, then everyone's signatures will have to be brought To answer this, we spoke to Dr. Ghanshyam Yadav, retired CMO of Gonda. He said that if the signatures are of the highest officer, an expert, and the department where one has to work has accepted it, then it is fine, but if any objection arises, then it becomes necessary to get the signatures of all members of the medical board. Prashant Singh's certificate is absolutely wrong. Prashant's elder brother, Dr. Vishwajeet Singh, also says that it is inappropriate to issue a disability certificate even though 2 members of the medical board were absent. Prashant himself obstructed the investigation of the Disability Commissioner and Medical Board Prashant Singh's elder brother, Vishwajeet Singh, filed a complaint with the Mau CMO on August 16, 2021. After this, he also complained to the UP Disability Commissioner. In this, he demanded an investigation into Prashant's disability certificate. The Disability Commissioner's office instructed the GST Commissioner to investigate Prashant's disability certificate. After this, an investigation into the matter began on the instructions of the Director General of Health. This investigation is being conducted by the Azamgarh Divisional Medical Board. For the first time, on September 28, 2021, the board called Prashant Singh for an eye examination. After this, he was called again on October 7, 2021, but Prashant Singh did not go. For the third time, he was called on November 30, 2022, but Prashant Singh still did not go. Now, for the fourth time, he was called on January 31, 2026, but he did not go. Now the board is going to set a date and call him for the 5th time. The reality is that Prashant Singh himself has stalled the medical board's investigation. If he appears for the eye examination, it will be proven whether his disability certificate is fake or not. After getting answers to all four questions, we reached out to the 3 responsible individuals who were involved in the disability certificate scam- Dr. Brij Kumar: He signed and issued the certificate as a nodal officer in place of the CMO, even though he knew that the machine used to diagnose the disease mentioned in the certificate was not available at Mau District Hospital. He could have stopped the certificate if he wanted to. Not me, the one who made the certificate is guilty Dr. Brij Kumar is now posted as a senior consultant at Ayodhya Divisional Hospital. We asked him why he issued the certificate despite not having a machine to diagnose the disease he mentioned? To this, Dr. Brij Kumar said - The one who made the certificate is guilty. Dr. YP Gupta: He examined Prashant Singh's eyes and certified Prashant Singh as disabled by signing the disability certificate in 2 places. Whereas he is not a retina expert, and the disease mentioned can only be diagnosed by a retina expert. Responsible Eye Specialist Not Ready to Answer We reached the home of Dr. YP Gupta, the eye specialist who examined Prashant Singh's eyes and issued the certificate. After retirement, he lives in Anand Nagar Colony in Banaras. He has built a hospital here. The receptionist called Dr. Gupta. After receiving a response from the other end, we were told that Dr. Gupta has gone to Chandigarh, he is ill, he has cancer. He is undergoing chemo. A little later, Dr. Saurabh Gupta, Dr. Gupta's son, came out. We gave him the questions, for which we have not yet received answers. Prashant Kumar Singh: He obtained his disability certificate. Based on this, he secured a government job under the disability quota. When he obtained the certificate, Prashant was active in politics; he was close to Mukhtar Ansari and Amar Singh. Prashant Singh said - The matter is in court, I will not answer Now, we wanted answers to some questions from GST Deputy Commissioner Prashant Kumar Singh, the most important link in this case. For this, we reached his office in Ayodhya. From here, we learned that he had gone on a long leave. When we called him, he refused to answer any questions, saying the same thing in response to every question: "The matter is pending in the Divyang Nyayalaya (Court for Persons with Disabilities), I will not say anything."

stories.title: Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak performs Batuk Puja:Invites kids home for tika; had said, 'Pulling choti is a grave sin'
stories.summary: In UP, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak worshipped Brahmin Batuks amid the Shankaracharya controversy. He invited 101 Batuks to his Lucknow residence on Thursday morning. Along with wife Namrata Pathak, he applied tilak to all Batuks. He folded his hands in respect, worshipped them, and showered flowers. During this, the Batuks chanted Vedic mantras. Notably, in Hindu rituals, a batuk is a budding boy, mostly brahmins, who participates in religious ceremonies. He chants Vedic mantras and is considered pure and auspicious. Feeding or honouring batuks during rituals is believed to bring spiritual merit and divine blessings to devotees. Police had misbehaved with Batuks in Magh Mela Actually, on January 18, during Mauni Amavasya at the Prayagraj Magh Mela, police had grabbed and dragged Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's disciple by his hair and beat him. The matter escalated after the video surfaced in Dainik Bhaskar. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak remained silent on this entire matter for a month. 2 days ago, for the first time at a media event, he said, 'The choti (long hair on top of the head) should not have been pulled. Whoever is guilty, strict action should be taken against them. Pulling hair is a great crime. You will see, it will incur great sin.' However, he had not mentioned Shankaracharya's name. As such, this step by the Deputy CM is being seen as an attempt at damage control amid Brahmin resentment. Actually, the Brahmin community in UP is upset over the UGC and Avimukteshwaranand controversy. Pathak is a BJP Brahmin leader, but he was being targeted by the Brahmin community for maintaining silence on both issues so far. It is believed that this program was conducted to send a message to the Brahmin community. According to sources, Pathak undertook this exercise only after taking the central leadership into confidence. Know what happened on Mauni Amavasya On January 18, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was going to take a bath in a palanquin at Mauni Amavasya in the Prayagraj Magh Mela. The police stopped Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand's palanquin. The police asked him to walk to Sangam. The disciples of Shankaracharya did not agree and started moving forward with the palanquin. This led to pushing and shoving between the disciples and the police. Police had taken many disciples into custody. The police had also beaten a sadhu at the police post. This made Shankaracharya angry. He insisted on getting his disciples released. Officials tried to convince him, folded their hands, but he did not agree. After this, the police took many more supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Shankaracharya's palanquin was dragged 1 km away from Sangam. During this, the canopy of the palanquin also broke. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath. Shankaracharya remained on dharna outside his camp till January 28. Then returned to Varanasi. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya had tried damage control. In Prayagraj, he had said that I bow at the feet of revered Shankaracharya ji. I request him to take a bath. If any revered saint or Shankaracharya ji has been insulted, we will investigate and take action. However, Keshav had not gone to meet Shankaracharya. Images of clash between Shankaracharya's disciples and police- Exchange of allegations continues between Yogi and Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand First know 2 major statements of Yogi... 'Not everyone can become Shankaracharya' CM Yogi Adityanath spoke in the assembly on Friday, February 13 regarding the Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand controversy. Yogi said - Not everyone can write themselves as Shankaracharya. No one is above the law. Not even me. I believe every person in India should follow the law. If SP people want to worship him, let them worship. CM said - An issue that was not there in the Magh Mela was deliberately made into one. Will every person roam around the entire state becoming Chief Minister? Will someone roam around putting up a minister's board? Will someone roam around becoming SP's president? No... There is a system, there is a process. 'The same law applies to me as it does to any common person' Yogi said - This is the same system in India's Sanatan Dharma. In Sanatan Dharma, the position of Shankaracharya is considered supreme and sacred. Look at the system of the House, there is tradition here too. The House operates according to rules. On Mauni Amavasya in Magh Mela, 4.5 crore people came. A system was created for everyone. Law is equal for all. The same law applies to me as it does to any common person. No person can be above the law. It is my belief that every person in India should follow the law.

stories.title: Fake inspector’s father is a real cop:Conducting school admission test in Lucknow; found using CM advisor’s letterhead
stories.summary: Kanpur police caught a fake inspector. He was accused of conducting recruitment exams at a private school in Lucknow under the guise of a police uniform. He was extorting money from new candidates by luring them with police department jobs. Kanpur police is investigating how many children have been cheated so far. Only 3 boys have come forward till now. Several government documents were found from the fake inspector, including the letterhead of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's former advisor Avinash Awasthi and seal of Secretary Housing Development. A CBI ID card was also found. Regarding this, Sanjay told the police- When I went for raids with local police ID, people would ask where I was posted. But when I showed the CBI card, everyone would get scared. Police is also investigating where Sanjay got all these things prepared from. However, police has got leads about a cyber cafe in Lucknow, from where fake letterheads and documents were prepared. Now the question arose why Sanjay from Unnao decided to become a fake police inspector? In police custody, he revealed many pages of his fraudulent life. Read the report… Sanjay said - Saw father's influence as inspector Inspector Rahul Shukla of Kanpur Police is investigating this case. He said - During interrogation, Sanjay said that my father was an inspector in the police department. Father Ranjit Singh was posted at Unnao's Kali Mitti Police Training Center. The family lives in Dostinagar. In our house there are Papa, mother Surajkali, me and 2 brothers Jay and Ajay. I am married to Van Devi Singh. We have 2 daughters. Elder brother Jay runs a tent house in Unnao. Younger brother Ajay operates rental cars. At home we have i20, Scorpio and Ertiga cars. It should be noted that this i20 car had a fake number plate (UP32EG2250) meant for government vehicles. The car is registered in the name of Joint Commissioner of Income Tax, Lucknow. While its real registration number is UP35BK8203. Left studies in 2007, dream of becoming police inspector shattered Sanjay said - Papa retired in 2016. But as long as he was an inspector, according to Sanjay, many influential people would come home to get their work done. From the training center to the market, Papa was highly respected. I dropped out of studies in 2007. I studied up to BA second year from Bighapur college. After this, my dream of becoming a police inspector was shattered. I knew that I could not take the UP Police recruitment exam now, so I took a salesman job at Sony World showroom on 80 Feet Road. After that in 2013, I started working in tiffin service near Om Chauraha in Kakadeo. Our tiffins started going to the maternity hospital. In 2015, I started running a canteen at Om Sai Hostel in Kakadeo. I met Durgesh-Vijay in Lucknow, they gave me the uniform Sanjay further said - After doing this work till 2016, I got a dumper and a JCB machine financed. Then I started doing soil transportation work. In 2025, I suffered losses in this business, after which I sold the JCB and dumper. After doing so much business, I felt that I was not made for business. Then I went to Lucknow for some work where I met Durgesh Savita and Vijay Chauhan. Vijay was from Shuklaganj. At that time Durgesh was working in a private company. Vijay was working in a hotel. After becoming friends, both of them said that they help boys get jobs. They conduct workshops for this, and make thousands just by selling job application forms. Vijay and Durgesh had also shared stories about their connections in Lucknow administration. After this, Sanjay shared stories of his influence when his father was a police officer. Vijay and Durgesh asked - you must have good knowledge about the police department. Sanjay said - absolutely. It was decided here that you work with us. You stay in police uniform, so that the children who come have confidence that we are not doing anything wrong. Rented house in Lucknow, planning used to happen there Durgesh himself brought and gave the uniform to Sanjay. Provided ID card, realistic-looking pistol and holster. After this, these people started renting private college campuses during vacant times. Here they would call children and stage fake recruitment examinations. First they would take money in the name of forms and preparation, then take money as bribes for getting jobs. For properly dividing the money that was coming in from this fraud, they had rented a house near Amausi airport. Sanjay has admitted to cheating 3 people in front of the police by promising them jobs in the police department. Among them, 1 boy is from Kanpur City, while 2 boys are from Kanpur rural area. These boys were cheated of 7 to 8 lakh rupees. Inspector asked - Where all did you conduct raids? Sanjay remained silent Inspector asked - Where did you get the CBI ID card made? Sanjay said - I got the ID card made from a cyber cafe in Lucknow. On one card I kept my name as Rajesh Mishra, while on the other card I kept the identity of Vikram Goswami. The inspector asked - Why did you get a CBI ID card made? Sanjay said - With local police identification, people would immediately start inquiring. But after telling them CBI, no one would ask where I was posted. The inspector asked - Did you also conduct raids? Sanjay said - I conducted some raids along with Durgesh and Vijay. I would identify myself as a CBI officer. When asked where all the raids were conducted, Sanjay remained silent. He did not answer. Know what Sanjay's father told the police When Sanjay mentioned his retired inspector father after being arrested, he was also called to the police station. He said - I only knew about his business, I had no idea when he started committing fraud by pretending to be an inspector. The inspector asked - Did you ever see him in uniform at home? He said - No, never. Nor did he have any ID card. Fraudster Number 2. It was told about Durgesh that he is the PSO of Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya. Regarding this, Inspector Rahul Shukla says - This will only become clear after tracing Durgesh. Two teams of Kanpur Police have been tasked to catch him. ACP Anwarganj Abhishek Rahul says - Sanjay hasn't answered many questions. According to what Sanjay revealed, he started committing fraud after meeting Durgesh and Vijay. Now we are tracing Durgesh and Vijay to uncover this entire fraud racket. Now Know How Sanjay Was Caught Used to commit fraud in the name of transfer-posting DCP Central Atul Srivastava said - On Tuesday, Anwarganj police received information that a person roaming in police uniform was fake. Police reached on the information and arrested him. He was wearing the uniform of a UP Police inspector. When questioned, he turned out to be fake. When his car was searched, a fake pistol and ID card were recovered. He used to cheat people in the name of jobs and transfer-postings. He would conduct interviews at hotels and schools on his own. He would deceive people there. Two more people are involved in his gang. Information about both is being gathered. According to police, the fake inspector Sanjay mentioned the name of Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya's PSO, who is terminated. This is being verified.

stories.title: 4 killed as car falls into canal in Mathura:2 law students among deceased; bodies stuck in car, removed with crane
stories.summary: In Mathura late Wednesday night, a speeding car went out of control and fell into a canal. In the accident, 4 men including 2 law students died. All were going to Deeg in Rajasthan to attend a wedding. On the way, the driver couldn't see the turn and the car fell into a 6-meter deep canal. As soon as local people saw the car falling into the canal, they immediately engaged in rescue work. Upon receiving information, police reached the spot. The fire brigade team started the rescue operation. By then, local people had broken the car door and pulled out 2 boys. While two others remained trapped in the car. After this, a crane was called and the car was pulled out. Then the bodies of 2 other boys were removed from the car. The accident happened near Magorra police station area. 3 pictures of the accident Read full matter in detail Were going to attend wedding The deceased have been identified as Rahul (23 years), Amit (22 years), Mohit and another friend. Amit and Mohit were studying law, while Rahul worked as a tailor. The car is said to belong to Rahul Verma's advocate brother Sajjan Singh. According to eyewitnesses, late at night the four youths were going to Deeg via bypass route through Mahavan and Govardhan in a Franx car number UP85 CV 9856. Due to a turn on the way, the driver could not see the road ahead properly. Due to a sudden turn, the driver lost control and the car fell directly into the canal. Police and Fire Brigade Conducted Rescue As soon as people heard the sound of the car falling into the canal, locals reached the spot. Local residents immediately informed the police and began efforts to rescue the youths trapped in the car. Before police arrived, local people pulled out two youths from the car, but they had already died. After this, police and fire brigade team that reached the spot pulled out the car with the help of a crane. Two more youths were extracted from it, but they also could not be saved. After the accident, police sent the bodies of all four youths for post-mortem. The SP Rural said - all evidence will be collected and legal action will be taken. The identification of the fourth youth who died in the accident is being done.

stories.title: Rain wind increase cold, temperature drops:Banda coldest, weather to remain same for next 4 days
stories.summary: After rain in several districts of western UP on Wednesday, the weather has turned cold. Today Thursday morning, there is a feeling of chill from the cold wind. Temperature has dropped by 2 to 3 degrees. However, most districts in Purvanchal have not seen any significant impact from this change. The weather department has issued a green alert across the state for Thursday, meaning the weather will remain clear. IMD says the weather will remain clear for the next 4 days. Talking about Wednesday, Banda was the coldest at 8.2C. Heavy rain occurred in Mathura, Noida and Bulandshahr. Clouds remained in Meerut and Bareilly. Lucknow scientist Atul Singh said that western disturbance has become active in central Pakistan and surrounding Punjab region. Its effect has been seen in many districts of western UP. This is why light rain occurred. See pictures- Temperature will drop up to 3 degrees due to westerly winds According to the Meteorological Department, the weather in the state is now expected to clear. There is no possibility of rain for the next few days. Due to the effect of westerly winds, the minimum temperature may drop by 2 to 3 degrees Celsius, while no significant change is expected in the maximum temperature. Know the temperature- Wheat-Mustard crop damage will reduce yield Experts have advised farmers to remain alert. They have said that if there is rain with strong winds, wheat and mustard crops may fall, which can weaken the grains and affect the yield. The meteorological department has advised not to keep harvested crops in the open and to store them in a safe place. How has the weather been so far Mahesh Palawat, weather expert at Skymet Weather in Noida, says - UP experienced less cold this time compared to 2 years. Average maximum and minimum temperatures in December-January remained above normal. A 36 percent decrease was seen between January 1 and February 11. Extreme cold was not seen this time. Due to La Nina not being active, it could not get very cold. Mohammad Danish, scientist at Lucknow Meteorological Center, also says that this time the activity of western disturbances was also less during the winter season in the state. Due to this, rainfall during the cold season was also less than normal. BHU meteorologist Professor Manoj Srivastava says - Now winter is in its final phase. Temperature will gradually increase in the coming days. Spring season is currently ongoing. There won't be much change in weather for the next 2-3 weeks. During this time, there will be mild cold in the morning and night, while the afternoon sun will feel slightly intense. According to weather expert Mahesh Palawat, light drizzle may be seen in many districts of UP around February 18. This includes areas like Hathras, Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Banda, Lalitpur and Jhansi. Now read when intense heat will start and how high the temperature will reach 1- Summer begins from first week of March BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava says - the weather will start changing completely from the first week of March and the summer season will begin. Temperature will rise rapidly during both day and night. By the last week of March, maximum temperatures in many districts of UP could reach 35 to 38 degrees Celsius. 2- Mercury will reach 42 to 45 degrees in May-June Manoj Srivastava says - In April, temperatures are likely to remain around 40 degrees Celsius. In May-June, maximum temperatures in many districts could reach 42 to 45 degrees. This means that not only during the day, but even at night there will be less relief from heat and humidity will persist. However, this will largely depend on the El Nio conditions. If El Nio conditions persist or strengthen, the heat situation could become even more severe. 3- Heat wave will last longer Maximum and minimum temperatures will remain above normal during March to May across the country including UP. Only in March, both maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain above normal throughout the country. Additionally, the number of heat wave days will also be higher than normal. Heat wave days will remain normal only in northeastern India and peninsular states like Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. 4- Crops will be damaged by heat BHU's Agriculture Department Professor PK Singh says - March month could prove challenging for farmers. The rise in temperature will affect the Rabi crop. Especially wheat. Due to heat, the grains will not develop fully. This will result in lower yield. According to PK Singh, hot winds can also damage crops like mustard, chickpea and peas. Due to rising temperatures, the soil in fields dries up quickly. This increases irrigation costs. Crops face stress. 5- Early onset of summer heat, conditions will worsen further According to Dhruvsen Singh, Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Lucknow University, the heat has increased earlier than usual in 2026. Heat wave events may occur more frequently and for longer durations. Conditions could become more severe in urban areas due to the urban heat island effect. All these factors combined are continuously pushing the temperature upward.

stories.title: Brain-dead patient gives new life to 3 in Lucknow:Two regain eyesight; police create green corridor, transport liver 19 km in 18 minutes
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a 42-year-old brain-dead patient gave new life to three people, while two others regained their eyesight through corneal donation. He was admitted to Apex Trauma at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGI), where doctors declared him brain dead on Sunday, February 22. After counselling, the family agreed to donate his organs, and the process began immediately. Both kidneys were retrieved at SGPGI for transplant. King George's Medical University (KGMU) was informed about the liver, and police created a green corridor from SGPGI to KGMU. Escorting the ambulance with two vehicles, the 19-km distance was covered in 18 minutes. See 2 pictures People seen supporting the traffic Injured in an accident on February 7 Liver transplant facility available at KGMU Both kidneys were taken from the brain-dead patient at SGPGI, and kidney transplants were performed on needy patients here. However, liver transplant facility is currently not available at SGPGI. Whereas liver transplants are performed at KGMU. This was the reason why the liver was sent to KGMU by creating a green corridor. Along with this, both eyes were also sent. They will be kept in KGMU's eye bank. Women from Unnao and Mainpuri received kidneys Dr. Narayan Prasad, Head of the Nephrology Department at SGPGI, informed that both kidneys are being transplanted within the institute. Both recipients are women. One of them is a resident of Unnao and the other of Mainpuri. Both kidney transplants are ongoing. Both kidney transplants are expected to be completed by 10:30 PM. Meanwhile, the liver has been donated to a KGMU patient for liver transplant. He claimed that after about 20 years, SGPGI itself has found such a brain-dead patient whose organs can give new life to the needy. Before this, when I myself was a resident doctor here, such an opportunity arose. The good thing is that people are becoming aware of organ transplants.

stories.title: Uproar at Lucknow University, namaz offered on campus:Students protest over closure of Lal Baradari gate, heavy police deployed
stories.summary: Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, NSUI, and AISA protested against the closure of the door of Lal Baradari Mosque at Lucknow University. On Sunday afternoon, students first knocked down the barricades towards Lal Baradari. After this, they reached near the building, chanting slogans, and offered Namaz there. In the evening, they also had Iftar there. Students offering Namaz were surrounded by other students forming a human chain. This human chain was removed when they finished their prayers. During this, a heavy police force remained deployed there. Students say that the university administration sealed the door of this mosque and erected a wall there without any notice. They demanded the opening of the sealed door. See 3 pictures Whoever creates an obstruction will not be spared. Bhavna Mishra, Registrar of Lucknow University, stated that Lal Baradari is in a dilapidated condition. The construction superintendent was asked to get fencing done there. Meanwhile, Hasanganj police were also informed in advance and asked to deploy adequate police force. Work has been started on Sunday. Legal action will be taken against anyone who creates an obstruction in this. Registrar's Office had issued a letter A letter was sent by the Registrar to the Superintendent of Works of Nirman Bhawan on February 2. It had asked for the construction of fencing. Subsequently, on Sunday, the work of building the fencing began. Following this, students from groups like NSUI, Samajwadi Chhatrasabha, and AISA protested against the construction of the fencing. Read what the protesting students said This is not a lock on the door, but on faith Mahendra, vice-president of the Samajwadi Chhatrasabha, who is protesting, said- I am a Hindu and I am protesting in support of the mosque. Namaz has been offered here at Lucknow University for hundreds of years. Sealing this mosque during the month of Ramadan is extremely shameful. This is not a lock on the door, but a lock on faith. An attempt has been made to lock down religious values. This entire act is anti-constitutional. Article-25 grants religious freedom and allows us to perform religious acts according to our religion. It is shameful that in this India, we will be stopped from worshipping and offering prayers. 'BJP and RSS want to push LU into communalism' Student Prince Prakash said that BJP and RSS want to push Lucknow University into the fire of communalism. Ever since the new Vice Chancellor came here, there has been continuous controversy. After the arrival of the new VC, BJP programs are continuously being held here. During this, only people associated with RSS and BJP are allowed to enter. When Mohan Bhagwat came, all the university gates were closed. Let alone students, professors could not enter. More than 50 classes were suspended. Students cannot roam freely in their campus. They want to turn the university campus into a BJP office. Kamlesh Tiwari is the construction superintendent here, but he pays no attention to the basic facilities of the university. The drinking water is so bad that no one can drink it. The roofs of the university building are constantly breaking. The water is bad, there are no seats in the toilets, and no one pays attention to this. Countless students' memories are associated with Lal Baradari, and it is being forcibly dismantled. It is being forcibly broken down and rebuilt. 'The door was open in the morning, I offered prayers' Tauqeel Ghazi, who was sitting on the protest, said that the mosque has been closed. The mosque door was open in the morning, I offered prayers. When I came in the afternoon, the mosque door was found closed. Forces from three police stations were deployed here, but no one from the university administration came to meet us. This mosque is 200 years old, which does not come under the university, but under ASI. Locking it without any notice is condemnable. We will not leave until we get an answer and will offer all our prayers here. RSS-BJP people came here, after which it was sealed Ahmed Raza Khan alleged that prayers have been offered here for a long time. Recently, many prominent RSS-BJP figures have visited the university campus. After this, the decision was made to seal these premises. Today, police from several stations arrived at the spot, but no one from the university administration came. There is a conspiracy to incite religious frenzy here.

stories.title: Prime Minister reacts to ‘unexpected incident’ in Parliament:Says Congress cannot secure PM post by using women MPs and seat capture
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi broke his silence on the protest by Congress women MPs in the Lok Sabha 17 days ago. The PM said in Meerut on Sunday, "Before sitting on the chair, one has to win the hearts of the people." He alleged that one cannot become Prime Minister by putting women MPs forward and occupying the seat. PM Modi asked Congress, "Have you become so hollow that you are putting mothers and sisters forward for this?" The PM further said, "Congress has become a burden for the country and its politics has become disconnected from public sentiments." PM Modi said - Congress has become a burden for the country PM Modi said, Congress's unrestrained leaders are bent on destroying the country. If you want to sit on the Prime Minister's chair, you first have to win the hearts of the people. You cannot become Prime Minister by sending women MPs and occupying the seat. Have you become so hollow that you are putting mothers and sisters forward for this? PM said, Congress has become a burden for the country. I am satisfied that regarding the incident that happened in Delhi, all the allied parties of Congress showed the courage to criticize Congress extensively. For this, I publicly express my gratitude to these allies of the opposition. Congress commits sins, its allies have to suffer the consequences He said - I humbly want to request the country's media that please, when we criticize such actions, do not create headlines like 'Modi thrashed the opposition'. By saying 'opposition-opposition', you are saving Congress. The other allies sitting in the opposition have also understood that Congress commits sins, and they have to suffer the consequences. PM gave 3 big messages Om Birla had said - An unexpected incident could have happened with PM Modi Actually, on February 4, PM Modi was to respond to the Motion of Thanks on the President's address in the Lok Sabha. When the House proceedings began at 5 pm, women MPs from the opposition surrounded the chairs of the ruling leaders. This included PM Modi's chair. After the uproar escalated, the House proceedings were adjourned without the Prime Minister's speech. The next day, on February 5, the proceedings resumed. Speaker Om Birla explained the reason for adjourning the House and postponing the PM's speech a day earlier. He said, 'When the Leader of the House, PM Modi, had to respond to the President's address, opposition MPs could have caused an unexpected incident by reaching near the Prime Minister's seat.' Birla further said, 'If this incident had happened, the tradition of democracy would have been shattered. To avoid this, I urged the PM not to come to the House. The PM accepted my suggestion.' Birla called the women MPs going up to the PM's chair against decorum. He told the opposition MPs, 'If you bring posters, the House will not function. The way women members reached the PM's seat, the country saw it. This was not appropriate. It was also not in line with the dignity of the House.' What happened before the PM's speech? BJP MP Manoj Tiwari claimed that even after repeated requests from senior ministers, the women MPs did not return to their seats. They climbed onto the place where the Prime Minister sits. They created a lot of ruckus. They could have even attacked the Prime Minister. However, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi said on these allegations that it is completely false and wrong that the women were going to attack the PM. PM inaugurated the Rapid-Metro rail in Meerut Prime Minister Narendra Modi lashed out at Congress over their protest of stripping clothes at the AI Summit. Addressing a public meeting in Meerut on Sunday, he said - India hosted the world's largest AI conference. The whole country was filled with pride, but what did Congress and its ecosystem do? They turned a global event into an arena of dirty and naked politics. Congress leaders arrived in front of foreign guests by stripping their clothes.
