stories.title: Ashutosh Maharaj challenges Avimukteshwaranand to undergo medical test:Says, 'I will accept him as Shankaracharya', states he belongs in jail like Asaram
stories.summary: 'I challenge you (Shankaracharya). If you are pure, undergo a medical examination at a government medical college. I will then accept you as Shankaracharya. Also have your disciple Mukundanand medically examined. It will become clear whether you are truly celibate or not.' This is what Ashutosh Maharaj says after a POCSO court ordered an FIR to be registered against Shankaracharya. Following the order, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Maharaj, who is the complainant in the case. He stated, “These are Asaram’s babas; they belong in prison. Do not defame the seat of Jagadguru Shankaracharya.” Responding to the FIR registered against him, Maharaj said, 'Fine, let us assume that, according to them, I am a criminal. But will that conceal their crime? Will young disciples not receive justice because of me?' He further alleged, 'If they are fearless, why are attacks being orchestrated against me? Why were attempts made to snatch items from my car? Why did Avimukteshwaranand offer me ₹1 crore? We have conducted a sting operation against them.' ‘We have come to seek justice. We will not step back, even if we are killed. I have saved all ethe vidence on email. Even if they murder me, no one will be spared.’ Read the full interview Have you been a disciple of Avimukteshwaranand? We were never his disciples. Our guru has been a Sanatan Dharma teacher. During the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi campaign, we met many saints. Avimukteshwaranand was among those we were in contact with. He had given us a letter some time ago, and we raised our voice over it. At that time, we were unaware of any such alleged conduct. His disciple Mukundanand was close to us. A guru-brother’s disciple is like a nephew-disciple. That is how we were connected. When did you distance yourself from him? When we became aware of his actions, we went from door to door seeking justice for the young students (batuks). Justice has now been sought in the temple of justice — the court. How do you know about the alleged Sheesh Mahal and swimming pool in his ashram? The Sheesh Mahal is larger than a royal palace. The facilities in his room surpass those in the home of India’s Ambani. There are even facilities that should not exist in such a place. A swimming pool has been constructed. I was told that when he bathes there, female companions massage him. Who are these companions? A woman named Purnima calls him Swamishree. A former judge’s daughter informed us and sent some evidence. Sisters and disciples associated with the ashram told us that there are rooms where misconduct occurs and women are tortured. In my words, it is torture; in theirs, entertainment and revelry. What else do you know about the ashram? I sensed something was wrong. When rooms were locked, why were children inside? Why only two children daily? First, Mukundanand would enter, then the children. I stayed there several times. I saw children crying and heard sounds once or twice. Some disciples wondered if someone was being beaten. But no one could investigate because access to the upper level was restricted. The next day, some children came down with bloodstains on their dhotis from behind. At that time, no one spoke. Later, children who had escaped and reached our ashram told us what had happened. What is the ‘Pancham Tal’? Just as the Chief Minister has a ‘Pancham Tal’, they built one in their Vidyamath, a luxurious fifth-floor room where these alleged acts occurred. You plan a foot march to Varanasi. When will it begin? We will undertake a foot march to Varanasi with young disciples to expose these alleged misdeeds. I invite former UP Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav to join. The Deputy CM also used to call frequently; he should come as well. I am ready to reveal everything. Why are 21 cases registered against you? There are two types of history-sheeters, criminals and those with politically motivated cases. The cases against me were filed during the Samajwadi Party and BSP governments. None are personal. Regarding Mata Sheetla Temple, a government receiver has been appointed. If I intended to seize it, I would have done so. Many cases are false, and in most we have been acquitted. A list released with a police seal has itself led to a case at that police station. If genuine, why file a case? Why does Shankaracharya allege you are linked to cow slaughterers? Provide evidence. Allegations are common, even against Chief Ministers. Justice is decided by the court. The case against them was registered by the court, not a police station. Is the judge lying? He examined pen drives and CDs. Were you offered bribes? We were offered ₹50 lakh, then ₹1 crore. We conducted a sting operation. We are not for sale. Is a gangrape case registered against you? I underwent a medical examination and submitted it to the court. The case dates to the BSP government era. The High Court granted a stay. The complainant was an 80-year-old woman. I was very young then. Would I assault an elderly woman? When did the alleged exploitation occur? It is not appropriate to disclose children’s details. Section 22 prohibits revealing such information.

stories.title: Aparna-Prateek seen together for first time after divorce controversy:Celebrate daughter’s birthday in Lucknow; welcome guests together
stories.summary: Following a public divorce controversy in Lucknow, Aparna Yadav and her husband Prateek Yadav, have appeared together for the first time. The occasion was their daughter Prathama’s birthday celebration, where the couple jointly welcomed guests and posed for photographs. Several BJP leaders attended, including Neeraj Singh, son of Rajnath Singh. On 19 January, Prateek Yadav shocked many by announcing on social media that he intended to divorce Aparna. In his posts, he described her as selfish and accused her of damaging family relationships. However, just nine days later, he reversed his decision, stating that the couple had reconciled. Aparna is currently with the BJP and serves as Vice-Chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh State Women’s Commission. Divorce announcement Prateek (38), step-brother of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, made two Instagram posts within eight hours on 19 January declaring the end of his marriage. In the first, he wrote that he would divorce ‘this selfish woman’ as soon as possible, alleging she had ruined his family ties and cared only about fame and influence. He said his mental state was poor and accused her of being an “evil soul”. In the second post, he claimed that the person who had broken his relationships with his mother, father and brother cared only about fame. He described the situation as a story of broken trust built on lies and pretence. Prateek's Instagram posts... Political differences behind the rift According to family sources, tensions had existed for three years, since 2022, when Aparna left the Samajwadi Party and joined the BJP against Prateek’s wishes. On 5 February 2025, he had posted three critical messages about her on social media, later deleting them. In those posts, he alleged she had made his life “hell” and was motivated solely by money and power. Aparna broke her silence on 22 January. In a television interview, she said she was being targeted because of her political and social activism but remained strong. She alleged that some people were deliberately attempting to create rifts in relationships to exert mental pressure and push her out of public life. She described the matter as not merely personal but also political and social, suggesting attempts were being made to defame her. Reconciliation after 9 days Nine days after his announcement, Prateek posted a photograph with Aparna captioned: “All is Good. Champions are those who resolve their personal and professional problems. We are a family of champions.' In a video, he acknowledged a “fierce and dangerous dispute” on 19 January but stated they had resolved it together. He added that those unhappy with their reconciliation could “go to hell'. Marriage and family background Prateek and Aparna married on 4 December 2011 after a relationship that began in 2001 through email exchanges following a birthday party. Aparna, originally Aparna Bisht from Uttarakhand, adopted the name Aparna Bisht Yadav after marriage. She studied in Britain and is the daughter of a journalist who later became State Information Commissioner, and Ambi Bisht, a former property officer at the Lucknow Development Authority. Both parents are now retired. Prateek is the only son of Mulayam Singh Yadav’s second wife, Sadhana Gupta, a nurse. Mulayam Singh publicly acknowledged him as his son but named Akhilesh Yadav, his son from first wife Malti Devi, as political successor. The couple has two daughters. Their wedding in Saifai, Etawah, was a high-profile event attended by thousands, including Mulayam Singh Yadav and Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan. Aparna’s political journey Born on 1 January 1990, Aparna studied at Loreto Convent, Lucknow. She contested the 2017 Assembly elections on an SP ticket from Lucknow but lost to BJP’s Rita Bahuguna Joshi. When denied a ticket in 2022, she left SP and joined the BJP, becoming the first member of the Mulayam family to do so. Though she sought a BJP ticket from Sarojini Nagar, she did not receive one. In 2024–25, she was appointed Vice-Chairperson of the Women’s Commission. Known for her outspoken views, Aparna often diverged from the SP line, and Akhilesh Yadav did not publicly respond when she left the party.

stories.title: Government official assigned to fetch underwear:‘Royal’ protocol list in Prayagraj puts 50 officers on task
stories.summary: A ‘royal-style’ protocol prepared for a senior BSNL official’s proposed visit to Prayagraj has sparked widespread discussion. Around 50 officers were assigned duties, and a detailed chart was circulated outlining specific responsibilities for each of them. The list reportedly covered arrangements for everything from the officer’s breakfast and lunch to even personal items such as underwear. The protocol document soon went viral on social media, drawing sharp criticism and ridicule. BSNL director’s proposed Prayagraj visit sparks protocol controversy The proposed visit of BSNL Director (CFA, Consumer Fixed Access) Vivek Banjal to Prayagraj has triggered controversy after an elaborate protocol assigning duties to nearly 50 officers surfaced online. The visit was scheduled for February 25 and 26, during which the Director was to hold review meetings with officials, visit key BSNL facilities, and also travel to the Jain pilgrimage site in Kaushambi. A detailed protocol order was issued two days in advance by the Deputy General Manager (DGM) at the GM Office in the Prayagraj Business Area. It outlined comprehensive arrangements to ensure the visit was conducted smoothly. Duties assigned for every personal and official requirement To manage the Director’s visit, committees comprising around 50 officers and staff members were formed, with each group assigned specific responsibilities. The protocol covered arrangements for official meetings, logistics, hospitality, and personal convenience. One committee was tasked with preparing welcome kits containing items such as water bottles, chocolates, chips, fruit juice, glasses, and napkins. Another committee was assigned to arrange personal-use kits, which included towels, underwear, soap, shampoo, oil, slippers, and grooming items such as mirrors and combs. The protocol also ensured arrangements for daily essentials, including drinking water, refreshments, and other personal necessities during the Director’s stay. Official order directed staff to ensure successful visit The order stated that Director (CFA) Vivek Banjal’s visit to the Prayagraj Business Area was scheduled for February 25–26, alongside senior officials including the Chief General Manager of the UP (East) Circle and the Principal General Manager (CFA) of the UP (East) Circle. All officers and employees were instructed to actively participate and contribute to ensuring the successful completion of the visit. The order specifically mentioned that nominated committee members were responsible for completing the tasks assigned to them within the stipulated time. Protocol Withdrawn After Facing Public Criticism The protocol document went viral on social media, drawing criticism and sparking debate over the nature of the arrangements. Following widespread backlash and ridicule, the order was withdrawn the very next day. The incident has since raised questions about administrative practices and the extent of protocol arrangements for senior officials’ visits. The very next day after the protocol was issued, someone posted it on social media. Along with this, it was also criticized calling it a royal arrangement. Many users also made various comments about it. After this, an office order was suddenly issued by the DGM on Friday itself. It stated that the previously issued order regarding the proposed visit is cancelled with immediate effect. Also, any previously issued guidelines in this regard should be considered ineffective. Cancelled order states... It is hereby informed that the office order, which was issued regarding the proposed visit of Director (CFA) to Prayagraj BA, is cancelled with immediate effect. All concerned officers/employees are requested to take note of this cancellation. Act accordingly. Any instructions previously issued in relation to the above-mentioned order shall be considered invalid. PRO Ashish Gupta stated- An order was previously issued regarding the proposed visit. It was later cancelled. As such, the guidelines that were in place have automatically become ineffective.

stories.title: Will Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand face jail in sexual abuse case?:Under POCSO, child’s statement alone can lead to life imprisonment
stories.summary: The POCSO court of Prayagraj has ordered filing of FIR against Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati for sexual exploitation. The court gave this order based on allegations by 2 minor children. Now questions are being raised whether Shankaracharya really sexually exploited the children? What will happen after this POCSO court order? What legal options will Shankaracharya have? Will he be found guilty? If found guilty, what punishment will he get? Let's look at the answers to these questions... First, know why police had not registered the case? We spoke to Mukesh Sharma, a lawyer at Allahabad High Court's Lucknow bench. He says, police must have had some doubts about the allegations, that's why the case was not registered. The doubt was because the sexual exploitation of children was happening for a year, why didn't the victims come forward for so long? They came forward at a time when Shankaracharya was sitting on a protest against the administration. Another reason could be that the police may not have registered an FIR in such allegations considering Shankaracharya's stature. What options will Shankaracharya have if an FIR is filed? In response to this, Mukesh Sharma says, Shankaracharya can appeal against this FIR in the High Court, can demand its dismissal by calling it wrong. Even if a case is registered after this, he can get interim bail. After interim bail, the matter will be investigated, there will be no arrest. How important will the medical report be in POCSO? If an FIR is filed against Shankaracharya, the children will undergo medical examination. Ajit Yadav, a lawyer at Lucknow bench of Allahabad High Court says that in POCSO cases, while the minor's statement is sufficient, medical examination is considered the most crucial evidence. The medical examination will be based on the allegations made by both children. If such evidence is found in the medical examination, the case will proceed further. Based on that, the relevant sections under POCSO will be applied. Ajit Yadav says, this is a high-profile case, so investigating officers will tread very carefully. The children's allegations, dates, times, people involved, circumstances at that time - everything will matter. Investigation will follow FIR, then punishment will be discussed Action is expedited in cases related to sexual abuse of children under POCSO Act 2012. There is a provision to complete the hearing within 1 year from the date of cognizance. Within this one year, the investigating officer has to file a chargesheet within the first 2 to 3 months. Supreme Court lawyer Shashwat Anand says, after investigation of this case when the chargesheet is filed then arrest can happen, after this the trial will begin. Both parties will present their evidence. After a year, the court will be in a position to deliver judgment. There are several clauses in POCSO, depending on the level of offense, the court will pronounce judgment accordingly. In this case, Ashutosh Maharaj's lawyer is SK Manas. He says- Shankaracharya is considered a pillar of Sanatan culture and called God, if God himself has descended to crush the culture, imagine what could be the plight of Sanatan culture. The POCSO court has ordered the case citing 5-6 lines, which is significant in itself. CM Yogi has used the word Kalnemi for him, therefore this case is ordered to be filed not against Shankaracharya, but against Kalnemi. Clash with police in Prayagraj on February 18, sexual abuse complaint filed 6 days later On January 18, during Mauni Amavasya bath at the Prayagraj Magh Mela, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand had a confrontation with the fair administration. Shankaracharya sat on a dharna outside his camp. Exactly 6 days after this incident, on January 24, 2026, Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj arrived at Jhunsi police station in Prayagraj with two minor Batuks. He filed his complaint, but the police took no action. The next day, on January 25, a complaint was sent via email to the Prayagraj Police Commissioner and Police Superintendent Mela. On January 27, a complaint was sent by post to Mela SP. However, no FIR was registered. After this, on February 8, Ashutosh Maharaj went to court with both children. Ashutosh Maharaj's 2 complaints against Shankaracharya- First complaint: Minor children are kept in Avimukteshwaranand's camp and gurukul. They are made to do personal service, crowd gathering, programs and carrying palanquins. There is also suspicion of sexual exploitation of children. Children were made to work in large events like Magh Mela. This is a violation of child rights and labor laws. There are also concerns about illegal weapons in the camp. Investigation should be done into assets exceeding income and multiple bank accounts. The role of a person named Mukundanand should be investigated. Second complaint: Ashutosh Maharaj accused Avimukteshwaranand of creating fake letterheads and documents. Said that in the Magh Mela area, Avimukteshwaranand was claiming himself to be the Shankaracharya of Jyotishpeeth. He was sending letters to officials using letterheads and documents in the name of "Jyotishpeeth/Sri Shankaracharya Camp". These letterheads and letters are fake and misleading. They are being used to mislead the administration and general public. These letterheads bear the date January 24, 2026 (Magh Shukla Panchami). Letters were issued using this date in the name of "Sri Shankaracharya Camp". Their authenticity has been questioned. On February 10, the lawyer on behalf of Shankaracharya filed a reply stating - since they started raising their voice for the protection of Gomata (cow), the government and some people have not been liking it. By what right did Ashutosh Maharaj become the complainant? On February 13, Judge Vinod Kumar Chaurasia heard the case. Ashutosh Maharaj told the court that two disciples came to me and narrated their story of sexual harassment. We want a case to be registered against Shankaracharya. The court first asked Ashutosh how did you become their guardian/protector? Ashutosh Maharaj said - According to guru tradition, I have come for justice. The victims did not get justice anywhere, that's why these children came to me. The court was cleared. The statements of both children were recorded in front of the judge and lawyers from both sides. The children gave statements in court- During Mahakumbh 2025, Avimukteshwaranand committed misconduct with them. The other disciples used to say that this is guru seva. This will bring blessings. Now know what the court said? The court cited several Supreme Court judgments and said that it is not mandatory to file an FIR in every case. The magistrate has to decide at their discretion whether to direct an FIR or proceed as a complaint. If police investigation is necessary in the case, it would be appropriate to register an FIR and investigate. Court's observation- The case involves allegations of serious sexual offense. POCSO Act applies. Police investigation is necessary to gather evidence. It would not be appropriate to proceed with the case only as a private complaint. The court ordered that the concerned station in-charge should immediately file an FIR. Conduct independent and impartial investigation according to law. Provisions of POCSO Act should be followed. Protect the identity and dignity of victims. Investigation report should be submitted to court. Now the two cases where accused were both convicted and acquitted Case 1: Engineer who molested around 50 children sentenced On February 20, a husband and wife were sentenced in a Banda case. The Banda court gave death sentence to the husband-wife who sexually exploited around 50 children. They used to sexually abuse children and sell obscene videos-photos abroad through dark web. The husband Rambhavan was an engineer in irrigation department, while wife Durgavati was a housewife. CBI arrested Rambhavan on November 18, 2020. Both had sexually exploited more than 50 children. On the 88th day of arrest, CBI filed a 700-page chargesheet in Banda court. The chargesheet was based on medical reports and statements of children. Case 2: Driver spent 8 years in jail, later honorably acquitted On December 7, 2025, a special POCSO court in Mumbai acquitted a 56-year-old driver. The driver had spent 8 years in jail. He was accused of sexually harassing a 17-year-old disabled girl. The court while acquitting said - The victim's side could neither explain the basic facts of the incident, nor the girl's age, mental capacity, and there were discrepancies between medical reports and her statements. Special Judge ND Khose said - The evidence presented by the prosecution is weak. The accused has already spent 8 years in jail, therefore he is being acquitted. The accused's lawyers Vaishali Sawant and Kalam Sheikh told the court that there was an old dispute between the victim's family and the accused. Due to which he was falsely implicated.

stories.title: CRPF brother kills sister's boyfriend:Lures UPSC aspirant into car, assaults and shoots in remote area
stories.summary: In Itawa, the murder of UPSC aspirant Manish Yadav was solved by police within just 24 hours. The case stemmed from a love affair, as Manish was killed by the brother of his girlfriend, who is a CRPF personnel, along with his accomplices. Manish’s girlfriend is a trainee constable in the UP Police. According to police, Manish had left home in the morning to attend coaching classes. During this time, the accused CRPF jawan lured him into a car under the pretext of talking. He was brutally beaten inside the moving car. The perpetrators then took him to a secluded spot, shot him dead, and hid the body in the car overnight. The following night, they dismembered the body, wrapped it in a polythene bag, and dumped it near the railway tracks before fleeing. CCTV footage near the railway line captured the car. On questioning, the car owner revealed the full details of the murder. Police are conducting raids to arrest the main accused CRPF jawan and one of his accomplices, with three teams deployed by the SP. Now read why and how the murder happened… Manish, a resident of Bharathna village, left home around 7 a.m. on 18 February for coaching but did not return by night. His family filed a missing person report at Bharathna police station the same evening. On 19 February, around 10 p.m., his mutilated body was found wrapped in polythene near the Chitbhavan railway track in Ikdil police jurisdiction. His head was severed from the body, one leg was cut, jaw broken, and dozens of injury marks were visible. The body was completely bloodied. Following family pressure, the administration formed a forensic team of five doctors who conducted a second postmortem on Saturday. X-ray examinations revealed bullets lodged in Manish’s body, which were carefully removed, confirming that it was a premeditated murder. SSP Brijesh Kumar Srivastava said three police teams were formed for investigation. CCTV footage near the railway tracks showed a car used to transport the body. Police traced the car owner, Deepak, a resident of Keshopur Kala in Ikdil police area, and took him into custody. Had been in love with constable's sister for many years Interrogation revealed that Manish had a long-standing romantic relationship with trainee constable Akanksha Yadav, currently undergoing training in Rampur. The two had studied together since childhood. Akanksha’s brother, Abhishek Yadav, a CRPF jawan stationed in Jalandhar, disapproved of the relationship. He had spotted his sister with Manish and returned to the village on leave on 17 February. Abhishek, along with his friends Deepak and Vipin Yadav from Manikpur village, planned Manish’s murder. On the morning of 18 February, the trio arrived in Bharathna in Deepak’s car. As Manish walked to coaching, he was offered a lift. He was first beaten inside the moving car and later shot in a secluded spot in the evening. Body remained in car overnight Deepak confessed that after killing Manish, they hid the body in the car trunk overnight. To avoid detection, the body was dismembered, wrapped in polythene, and discarded near the Chitbhavan railway tracks late on Friday night before fleeing. SSP Srivastava confirmed that Deepak admitted the crime during interrogation. Police are actively searching for main accused Abhishek Yadav and another accomplice. Three teams comprising SOG, surveillance, and local police are involved in the hunt, with arrests expected soon Manish was the youngest in the family Manish was the youngest son in a family with one sister and two brothers. He and his elder brother Avnish were both preparing for civil services exams. Manish had completed a BSc in Agriculture and a BEd and had recently appeared for the Junior Assistant exam, whose results were pending. After the postmortem, when Manish’s body was returned home on Saturday, his father Rajveer Singh and brother Avnish were devastated. His last rites were performed later that evening.

stories.title: Questions raised over man who filed FIR against Shankaracharya:Rambhadracharya disciple linked to 21 cases
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand has alleged that Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj is a history-sheeter and his name is listed at number 34 on the wall of Kandhla police station in Shamli district. He claimed that Ashutosh Pandey’s name appears in the police register under history sheet number 76A. These allegations surfaced after Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj filed a complaint against the Shankaracharya. Acting on the complaint, a POCSO court in Prayagraj ordered the registration of a sexual harassment case against Swami Avimukteshwaranand, his disciple Mukundanand, and two to three unidentified persons. The controversy has raised questions about Ashutosh Maharaj’s background and the claims regarding his criminal record. Initiation into religious life and association with Rambhadracharya Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj is associated with the ancient Shakumbhari Siddhpeeth temple in Kandhla, Shamli district. His original name is Ashutosh Pandey. He took religious initiation from Jagadguru Rambhadracharya in 2022. He currently serves as chairman of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Mukti Nirman Trust and is also involved in managing temple activities. His uncle, Pradeep Pandey, is a priest at the temple. According to family members, Ashutosh Pandey was born into a Pandit family in Kandhla. His father, Rajendra Pandey, worked as a conductor on a private bus. He is the eldest among six siblings. He studied at a private school near his home and developed an interest in spirituality from a young age. After completing Class 12, he spent more time at the temple and became involved in religious activities. Claims of criminal record and police history sheet Amid the dispute, Yogiraj, a disciple of Swami Avimukteshwaranand, shared old newspaper clippings and a police document in an ashram WhatsApp group. The document, reportedly from Kandhla police station, mentions Ashutosh Pandey under history sheet number 76A. According to the document, multiple cases were registered against him in the past. These include cases under the Uttar Pradesh Cow Slaughter Act, Gangster Act, IT Act, and other criminal charges such as fraud, assault, rape, and criminal intimidation. The document also states that charge sheets were filed in several cases. However, there has been no official confirmation from police authorities regarding the current status of these cases or whether he is presently listed as a history-sheeter. Role in Krishna Janmabhoomi case and public activities Ashutosh Maharaj is also associated with the Krishna Janmabhoomi dispute and has written to the police and administration regarding related matters. He has been seen attending public and religious events and has shared photographs with political leaders. He remains active in religious and organisational work connected with temples and trusts. Dispute with Shankaracharya and court order The dispute began after disagreements between Swami Avimukteshwaranand and the administration during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. Several religious leaders reacted to the issue, with some supporting the Shankaracharya and others opposing him. Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj publicly opposed Swami Avimukteshwaranand and later filed a police complaint. He then approached the Additional District and Sessions Judge and POCSO Special Court in Prayagraj, alleging sexual harassment and other serious offences. On February 21, the POCSO court ordered the registration of an FIR against Swami Avimukteshwaranand, his disciple Mukundanand, and unidentified persons. The case has intensified tensions between the two sides. Police are expected to begin an investigation following the court’s order.

stories.title: Bullet tears through child's jaw in Bulandshahr:Father allegedly urged minor son to fire celebratory shots despite warnings
stories.summary: In Bulandshahr, a stray bullet during celebratory firing tore through an 8-year-old boy’s jaw. The child, Reyansh, was playing on a neighbour’s roof when the incident occurred. Upon being hit, the boy fell covered in blood. Children playing nearby informed his family, and his father immediately ran with him to the hospital. The incident took place around 5 p.m. on 19 February, and a video of the event has surfaced. It shows a minor, aged 16, firing a licensed revolver in the street. Police investigations revealed that the boy had been encouraged by his father, Vinod, who allegedly said: “Fire the gun. If anyone is hit, I’ll take care of it.” Reyansh is currently in critical condition at Fortis Hospital, Noida. He is in a coma and on ventilator support. Police have registered a case against the minor and his father, both of whom have fled the scene. Now the complete matter in detail... The incident took place about 1.5 km from the district headquarters, in the Nagar Kotwali area, Shekhsarai locality. Vinod, also known as Rinku Soni, was preparing for his daughter’s wedding on 20 February. On 19 February, the family held a rice-offering ceremony, with relatives dancing outside to the beat of drums. During this time, Vinod’s 16-year-old son took a licensed pistol indoors and fired a round. When family members scolded him, Vinod allegedly told him: “Krishna, fire the gun… I am telling you to fire. If anyone gets hit, I’ll handle it.” Despite family warnings about the narrow street and neighbours on rooftops, the boy began firing multiple rounds while walking through the street under his father’s encouragement. Around 5:30 p.m., during the celebratory firing, a bullet struck Reyansh, the 8-year-old son of neighbour Himanshu Soni. The bullet tore through his jaw and grazed his palate. Reyansh was playing on the roof when it happened, causing people nearby to scream. Hearing the commotion, the drumming outside stopped. Reyansh’s father carried him out of the house, bloodied and unconscious. Initially angry at Vinod and his son, Himanshu immediately ran towards the hospital upon seeing Reyansh’s condition. 4-hour operation, child on ventilator at Fortis Reyansh was first taken to a local hospital and then referred to Fortis Hospital in Noida. On Saturday, doctors operated on him for about four hours. Part of his skull had to be removed. He remains in a coma on ventilator support. Doctors have said the next 48 hours are critical, and his condition will be closely monitored until Monday. Police have registered a case based on a complaint by the boy’s father. CO City, Prakhar Pandey, said CCTV footage and other video evidence have been collected, and the licensed pistol has been seized. Both the minor and his father, Vinod, remain absconding. Police teams are conducting raids to locate them. Read what is shown in the video Two videos of the incident have emerged. In the first, Vinod’s wedding function is underway, with relatives dancing to drums outside. The minor son brings a licensed pistol and fires into the air. Despite relatives trying to stop him, Vinod encourages his son. The boy then fires multiple rounds while roaming the street. During this time, one bullet strikes Reyansh on the roof. His father, Himanshu, carries him out, initially scolding Vinod but then rushing to the hospital upon seeing Reyansh’s critical state. Taking advantage of the chaos, Vinod and his son flee. Another video shows Vinod himself also firing during the celebration. Reyansh is the only son of the family Himanshu said Reyansh is the only child in their family. He was standing on the roof when the bullet struck. Since the incident, Reyansh’s mother has been inconsolable. Doctors have described the next 48 hours as extremely critical. Himanshu pleaded, “God, please return my child safely to me.” The victim’s family has alleged that police initially allowed the accused to continue with the wedding arrangements. They have demanded the immediate cancellation of Vinod’s gun license and strict action against both father and son.

stories.title: 5 family members found dead in Kasganj:Husband, wife, and three children among the victims; house was closed for 3 days
stories.summary: On Saturday, five members of a family were found dead inside a locked house in Kasganj. The house had reportedly been shut for three days, and neighbors grew suspicious after noticing no activity. They informed the police, who arrived at the scene. The police broke open the lock and found the five bodies inside. Preliminary investigation suggests a possible case of mass suicide. The incident falls under the jurisdiction of the Amapur police station. The house belonged to Shyamveer Singh (50), a welder who lived behind Gupta Agency Petrol Pump. Along with him, his wife Sheela (48), daughter Akanksha (10), daughter Prachi (12), and son Greesh (8) were found dead. It is believed that Shyamveer may have administered some poisonous substance to his family before taking his own life. As news of the five deaths emerged, a crowd gathered at the site. Neighbors confirmed that the house had been closed for two to three days before they alerted the authorities. Police are investigating the exact cause of the deaths. Updates on the case are continuing. News is being continuously updated..

stories.title: PM Modi lays foundation stone for semiconductor unit in Noida:Yogi says Jewar transformed from lawlessness to industrial hub
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday laid the foundation stone of the India Chip semiconductor unit in Yamuna City, Greater Noida, and said the facility would strengthen India’s technological capabilities and create employment opportunities. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister said India was moving rapidly towards its goal of becoming a developed nation and had accelerated its pace at the start of 2026. He said the semiconductor unit would function as a technology powerhouse and help build a strong semiconductor ecosystem in the country. He added that the project would generate large-scale employment, especially for the youth of Uttar Pradesh, and promote the growth of design centres, research, and startups. The semiconductor unit is being set up by India Chip Private Limited, a joint venture between HCL and Foxconn, with an investment of ₹3,706.15 crore. The company has been allotted 48 acres of land in Sector 28 of Yamuna City. The project is part of the government’s efforts to strengthen domestic semiconductor manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports. First see 2 pictures... CM Yogi says region has undergone major transformation Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the region had witnessed lawlessness under previous governments, with incidents of firing, kidnapping, and disorder. He said people were afraid to step out after sunset. He added that the situation had changed significantly and Jewar was now emerging as a major industrial hub. CM Yogi said the Prime Minister’s vision had helped India emerge as a major technology and manufacturing centre. He added that Uttar Pradesh was becoming a preferred destination for investment due to improved infrastructure, better law and order, and business-friendly policies. Railways Minister calls it a historic milestone Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw described the foundation of the semiconductor unit as a historic step and said semiconductors were the backbone of modern technology. He said the presence of semiconductor manufacturing would enable multiple industries and strengthen India’s manufacturing capacity. He said India’s electronics manufacturing had grown rapidly over the past decade and the semiconductor unit would further boost domestic production. He added that global companies investing in India reflected growing confidence in the country’s technological strength and manufacturing potential.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Cong AI Summit protest triggers BJP nationwide protests BJP is staging protests across the country following disruptions by Youth Congress members at the India AI Impact Expo 2026. Meanwhile, Patiala House Court has sent all four arrested individuals to five days of police custody. 2. The complaint is filed by Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, a disciple of Jagadguru Ramabhadracharya, who produces two children before the court. Their statements are recorded in court in the presence of cameras. 3. University took 60% cut from fake degree racket in Kanpur; syndicate spread across 9 states A Kanpur-based syndicate issued B.Tech, B.Pharma and LLB marksheets and degrees without exams. During closed-door interrogation, mastermind and math teacher Shailendra revealed the racket operated on a 40% commission, while 60% of the earnings went to university clerks and employees. The network had spread across nine states, and he reportedly met presidents of four countries. 4. Red alert in Delhi over potential LeT attack A red alert has been issued for New Delhi’s Red Fort area on Saturday amid claims that a temple in Chandni Chowk could be targeted. Sources say Lashkar-e-Taiba may be planning an IED attack to avenge the February 6 mosque blast in Islamabad. 5. Bounty on Rahul Gandhi’s head: What is the legal punishment for public death threats? Raebareli MP Rahul Gandhi and 25 other MPs received threats of being shot at home. Congress leader Pawan Khera shared the video on X on February 19. Police detained the accused from Rajasthan. The report also questions development works in the Ghaziabad Development Authority area and plot allotments to the poor. 7. stories.title: Wedding dancer elopes with groom’s brother in Aligarh:Newlywed wife alleges blackmail; family fears safety
stories.summary: In Aligarh, a dancer who was invited to perform at a sister’s wedding allegedly ran away with the bride’s brother. The bride’s brother, Mohammad Bilal, had married just a month earlier. According to the family, after the dance programme ended around midnight, Bilal had gone to drop the dancer at her home. During their conversation on the way, Bilal developed a relationship with the dancer, identified as Soni alias Shabnam. Their closeness increased over time, and Bilal reportedly stopped speaking to his newlywed wife. The family claims Bilal and Soni were later seen at a hotel in Jaipur, and CCTV footage of the two together has surfaced. The bride and her family alleged that the dancer has a criminal background and had previously been jailed in a murder case. The incident falls under the Gandhi Park police station area. Now understand the entire matter in detail... Gulista Begum, a resident of Sarai Intezam Ali, said she married Mohammad Bilal on December 3, 2025. Two days later, on December 5, her sister-in-law’s wedding was scheduled. She said that on December 4, during the sangeet ceremony, Soni alias Shabnam, a resident of Neevari Mod in Aligarh, was invited to perform. During the programme, Soni allegedly obtained Bilal’s mobile number. Gulista alleged that conversations between Bilal and Soni began soon after. She said Bilal started arguing with her frequently. She later checked his phone and discovered he had been in regular contact with the dancer. Allegation of blackmail using objectionable video Gulista further alleged that a few days later, Soni called Bilal to her house and served him tea allegedly mixed with intoxicants. She claimed that Soni then recorded an objectionable video of him and used it to blackmail him. She also alleged that on January 9, 2026, Soni took Bilal’s thumb impression while he was intoxicated and prepared a fake marriage certificate. When the family objected, Soni allegedly demanded ₹10 lakh to leave Bilal, calling him a “golden egg-laying hen”. Bilal’s wife Gulista Begum narrated the entire incident to the media. Family alleges past criminal involvement Bilal’s father, Sadiq Ali, and sister-in-law Sonam alleged that Soni had previously trapped other young men. They claimed she was involved in the murder of a युवक in the Shahjamal area and had been jailed in connection with the case. The family said they fear for Bilal’s safety. Jaipur hotel video surfaces, police yet to receive complaint Family members said Bilal is currently missing. They claimed a video recorded on February 11 shows Bilal and Soni at a hotel in Jaipur. Gulista also alleged that Bilal had earlier attempted suicide and was under mental pressure. The Gandhi Park police station in-charge said no formal complaint has been received so far. He said police will contact the family based on the viral video, and appropriate investigation and action will be taken if a complaint is filed.

stories.title: '300 cops were deployed for Akhilesh security despite board exams':Following Ex-CM's remark, DSP says, 'He can tell where he was inconvenienced'
stories.summary: The matter of the security lapse of SP President Akhilesh Yadav in Fatehpur is gaining momentum. DSP City Pramod Shukla clarified the matter on Saturday. He said, Board exams are currently underway. Most of the force is deployed at examination centers. Despite this, 300 policemen were deployed for Akhilesh Yadav's security. If he saw less force anywhere, he himself can tell where he was jostled. Akhilesh Yadav had flared up at DSP Pramod Shukla on Friday. He had asked the DSP in front of his workers and journalists, he said, ‘Tell me how many policemen were deployed. There was no adequate police force anywhere in our security arrangements. We kept getting pushed.’ The SP chief also said that many FIRs are filed in Fatehpur. Palm warm, police soft. Will we also have to warm our palms? Ask the captain how much it will cost to warm the palm. See 2 visuals Samajwadi Party members alleging less force Akhilesh Yadav's statement regarding the security lapse caused a stir in political circles. Samajwadi Party members started accusing the administration of deploying less force. DSP City Pramod Shukla said, There were programs of the SP chief at 6 places in the district. For this, 300 policemen, including SHOs of 7 police stations, were deployed at all locations. The crowd of SP workers was large, yet policemen were deployed everywhere to prevent any disorder. Read in 5 points what Akhilesh said 1. Probe into Jairaj murder case Akhilesh Yadav said the killings in Fatehpur are not ordinary disputes but conspiracies. He said he is visiting the family of Fatehpur’s royal lineage member and assured that if his government is formed, the Jairaj Man Singh murder case will be investigated through proper legal procedure by senior officers, not junior officials. 2. Deputy CM should resign On the Shankaracharya controversy, he said those who lack proof of being a Yogi are demanding degrees from the revered Shankaracharya. He claimed the CM and Deputy CM are divided into factions and said if the Deputy CM supports Shankaracharya, he should resign. Without naming Brajesh Pathak, he added that even two Deputy CMs together cannot protect Shankaracharya’s honour. 3. Illegal activities in Gorakhpur Akhilesh said he had to change routes twice from Lalganj to Afoi due to incomplete Ganga bridges, causing delays. He alleged that in ten years the government failed to build proper bridges and roads, mandis are in poor condition, patients lack treatment in government hospitals, and illegal activities are ongoing in the CM’s Gorakhpur. He urged people to remove those who deceive them, saying SP will defeat them even through EVMs. 4. Alliance with Bahujan Samaj On a possible tie-up with Mayawati, he said the Samajwadi Party has already allied with the Bahujan Samaj and is working with backward classes, Muslims, and Dalits. 5. SP stands with the discontented He said SP has aligned with all those unhappy with the government, people who feel mistreated or humiliated, and stands with every individual and community affected by BJP policies.

stories.title: Prayagraj court orders POCSO FIR against Avimukteshwaranand:2 victims presented in court; seer denies charges, calls case fabricated
stories.summary: The Special POCSO Court in Prayagraj on Saturday directed the police to register an FIR against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati over allegations of sexual abuse of minor children. The order was passed by Special Judge (POCSO Act) Vinod Kumar Chaurasia after examining an investigation report submitted by the Prayagraj Police Commissioner. The court ordered the registration of a case against Avimukteshwaranand, his disciple Mukundanand, and two to three unidentified persons. The court had reserved its order on February 13 after hearing the matter. Two minors presented before court The complaint was filed by Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, a disciple of Jagadguru Ramabhadracharya. He presented two minor children before the court, where their statements were recorded. The complainant alleged that the abuse took place at a gurukul run under the Shankaracharya’s camp. Ashutosh Brahmachari said he approached the court after failing to get relief from the police. “We were approaching the police, but nobody listened to us. That is why we came to the court. Today, it feels that justice is still alive. The court has given us justice,” he said. He alleged that minor disciples were subjected to sexual abuse and said he would continue his efforts to seek justice. Complaint filed on February 8 The complainant had filed the case in the Special POCSO Court on February 8, alleging that minors were sexually abused under the guise of running a gurukul. Following the complaint, the court sought a report from the Prayagraj Police Commissioner before passing its order. Avimukteshwaranand’s counsel had submitted a reply in court on February 10, opposing the allegations. Shankaracharya denies charges, calls case false Responding to the court’s order, Avimukteshwaranand denied the allegations and termed the case fabricated. “A false case will not become true. This sexual abuse case will be proven false. It is a fabricated matter,” he said. He alleged that the complaint was filed at the behest of Jagadguru Ramabhadracharya through his disciple due to ongoing ideological differences. “We have differences with Ramabhadracharya. He has used his disciple to file a false case against us. We will cooperate with the legal process, and the truth will come out,” he said. He added that he had full faith in the judicial process and sought an early investigation to establish the facts. Court directs police to follow legal procedure The court’s order directs the Prayagraj police to register the FIR and proceed in accordance with the law. The case will now move into the investigation stage, during which police will record statements and collect evidence. The development comes amid ongoing tensions between the two religious figures, with both sides making serious allegations against each other. The police have not yet issued a detailed statement following the court’s order. The case was heard on February 13 by Special Judge (POCSO Act) Vinod Kumar Chaurasia in Prayagraj. Complainant Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj argued the matter himself in court. He told the judge that two disciples had approached him and narrated their experiences of sexual abuse. He urged the court to order the registration of an FIR against the Shankaracharya and initiate an investigation, saying he had faith only in the judiciary for justice. During the hearing, the Shankaracharya’s lawyer cross-examined the complainant and said the allegations were only claims at this stage. The defence sought some time to prepare the case. Ashutosh Brahmachari told the court that he had been receiving death threats and claimed that there were threats to blow up his car with a bomb. He said his life was in danger and requested the court to listen to the statements of the children who were allegedly abused. Courtroom cleared, children’s statements recorded Following this, the judge ordered the courtroom to be cleared. Only the lawyers from both sides were allowed to remain present. The two children were then brought into the courtroom, where they narrated their accounts of the alleged abuse before the judge. The statements were recorded inside the closed courtroom, and the entire process was documented on camera as part of the court proceedings. Ashutosh Brahmachari was seen leaving the courtroom in tears after the hearing, wiping his eyes as he came out.

stories.title: Quack doctor enters house and rapes woman:Locals in Kushinagar tie limbs and beat accused; video surfaces
stories.summary: A quack doctor accused of rape was severely beaten by locals in Kushinagar. He allegedly entered a woman’s house, molested her and raped her after threatening her. When the woman raised an alarm, nearby residents caught the accused. They beat him and tied his hands and legs with a saree, then made him lie on the road. The incident is from the Hanumanganj police station area. Police have arrested the accused. A video of the assault and his being tied up has also surfaced. Know the full matter... The victim said she has two children—aged 5 and 10—and her husband works in Hyderabad. On Thursday night she was sleeping with her children when, around 11 pm, a village quack doctor named Dinesh Maddheshia came to the back door and knocked. She said that as soon as she opened the door, he pushed her and forced his way inside. He then tried to assault her and allegedly threatened to kill her when she shouted. According to the woman, he raped her. She somehow pushed him away, ran, woke her children and called for help. Villagers caught and tied him up Hearing her cries, villagers rushed in and caught the accused. After beating him, they brought him to the road and tied him with a saree. The victim also slapped him several times. Village women also hit him. Within minutes a large crowd gathered. Someone informed the police. About an hour later police arrived, rescued the accused from the mob and took him into custody. People kept him lying on the ground for nearly an hour before police freed him. The accused has two wives, six children The victim said the accused had earlier entered her house several times with wrong intentions. A similar incident allegedly happened three to four years ago, but villagers had settled the matter then. According to locals, he has married twice. Both wives live with him and together they have six children. He runs a clinic in the village but has no medical degree. Station in-charge Sanjay Kumar said a case has been registered based on the woman’s complaint. She is being sent for medical examination. He added that there had been a dispute between the two sides earlier that was settled, but this time legal action is being taken.

stories.title: Prayagraj inspectors arrested for extorting ₹20 lakh:Accused allegedly threatened fake encounter and NSA charges
stories.summary: Two police inspectors posted in Prayagraj have been arrested for allegedly extorting ₹20 lakh from a textile businessman in Meerut by threatening to stage an encounter and impose the National Security Act (NSA). The accused had been absconding for the past 10 days. Meerut Police received information that the two inspectors would meet a lawyer in Prayagraj on Friday to file an appeal in the High Court to avoid arrest. Acting on the tip-off, a police team reached Prayagraj. On Friday evening, as soon as inspectors Lokendra Sahu and Mahesh Gangwar arrived at the lawyer’s chamber, police surrounded them. Both tried to flee but were chased and arrested. They were posted at Lohianagar police station at the time of the incident. Action was taken against them on the complaint of a businessman, Rasikh, who runs MSRS Textile in Meerut. Businessman alleges abduction and threats Rasikh, a resident of Islamabad Rickshaw Road in Meerut, said the incident took place on December 8. He was returning from his shop near Nauchandi when a car stopped on Azad Road. According to him, two inspectors were inside the vehicle. One of them got down and forced him into the car. He was allegedly told that he was involved in illegal funding and that NSA charges would be imposed on him. The businessman said the inspectors took him to Hapur and accused him of collecting hawala money. He alleged that he was threatened with an encounter and told he would be shot. ‘Tortured during journey, forced to arrange money’ Rasikh claimed he was tortured during the journey and his health deteriorated. On the way back from Hapur, he was allegedly taken to a forest area in Allipur where the inspectors made videos of him. He said the officers demanded ₹50 lakh for his release. When he said he could not arrange such a large amount immediately, the demand was reduced to ₹20 lakh. Rasikh called his brother-in-law Naeem, who arrived with ₹14 lakh in cash. The amount was handed over to the inspectors. Rasikh was then released with instructions to arrange the remaining ₹6 lakh. He said he arranged the remaining money the next day and handed it over at a location specified by the inspectors. Fresh demand and further threats According to the complaint, one of the inspectors later called him again and claimed that ₹13 lakh had been given instead of ₹14 lakh. He allegedly demanded another ₹1 lakh. Rasikh said he was called to Nauchandi Ground with ₹1 lakh. He reached the spot with his brother-in-law and handed over the money. He was allegedly warned that if he spoke to anyone, he would be implicated in the Delhi blast case and sent to jail for life. The businessman also alleged that the inspectors threatened to circulate a video in which he was made to “confess” to illegal funding. FIR registered after partial refund Fearing consequences, Rasikh remained silent for a few days. He later approached SP City Ayush Vikram Singh and narrated the entire incident. Senior officers verified the allegations. According to police sources, the inspectors were told to return the money and assured that action would be considered accordingly. Following this, ₹14 lakh was sent back to the businessman through an intermediary. After confirmation, an FIR was registered against both inspectors on February 6. Soon after the case was filed, the accused went absconding. A search operation was launched, leading to their arrest in Prayagraj on Friday. Further investigation is under way.

stories.title: Mayawati criticises Congress protest at AI summit:Jayant calls it height of indecency; BJP burns effigies in Lucknow, Varanasi
stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) workers staged protests in several cities of Uttar Pradesh on Friday and Saturday, condemning the Youth Congress demonstration held during the India AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi. Protests were reported from Lucknow, Varanasi, Kanpur and Agra, where BJP workers burned effigies of the Congress and raised slogans against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. In Lucknow, members of the BJP youth wing marched towards the Congress office from the VVIP Guest House area. Police stopped them by placing barricades on the road. Protesters raised slogans such as “Rahul Gandhi, come to your senses” and burned an effigy of the Congress leader. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers to maintain order. In Varanasi, BJP youth wing leaders gathered near the Circuit House and burned an effigy of Rahul Gandhi. Party leaders accused the Congress of damaging the country’s image through its protest at an international event. In Agra, BJP workers protested near the Congress office at St. John’s crossing. A confrontation broke out between protesters and the police when they attempted to move towards the Congress office. Police stopped them after efforts lasting about 30 minutes. Protesters raised slogans against Rahul Gandhi during the demonstration. Political reactions intensify The Youth Congress protest has drawn criticism from several political leaders. Bahujan Samaj Party president Mayawati said political protests should not harm the country’s international image. She said the manner of protest at a global summit attended by international delegates was inappropriate. Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary said the protest did not follow democratic norms and questioned its timing at an international event focused on technology and innovation. Former Union Minister Smriti Irani also criticised the protest and asked whether Congress leaders had endorsed the actions of Youth Congress workers. Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said the public would respond to the Congress through democratic means. Earlier, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had also criticised the protest and called it inappropriate. Youth Congress protest at summit The protests in Uttar Pradesh follow a demonstration by Youth Congress workers at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on February 20 during the India AI Impact Summit 2026. Some Youth Congress members removed their shirts and displayed white T-shirts bearing photographs of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and United States President Donald Trump. The T-shirts carried slogans referring to the India–US trade deal. Police detained several protesters at the venue. The summit, attended by representatives from more than 100 countries, focused on global cooperation and innovation in artificial intelligence. The Congress defended the protest, citing the democratic right to dissent, while the BJP accused the party of undermining India’s image at an international forum.

stories.title: German groom marries in Firozabad with Indian traditions:Unique ceremony blends cultures, saw ritual, and mehendi reflect love beyond borders
stories.summary: A wedding in Firozabad drew widespread attention as German groom Gustav arrived with an overseas procession and embraced traditional Indian customs. In a unique moment on stage, the bride and groom even cut wood with a saw, leaving guests pleasantly surprised. Gustav wore a sherwani and safa, looking completely Indian, while the bride, Khushi, looked elegant in a red outfit. The couple danced to Bollywood songs, often holding hands, as four translators accompanied the wedding party to help guests communicate. Khushi, a resident of Firozabad, married Gustav on Friday after a year-long relationship. Rituals such as varmala, seven pheras, and vidai were performed according to Hindu traditions, giving foreign guests a close and memorable experience of Indian culture. Know how their love story began The bride's aunt Jyoti said that Khushi and Gustav work in a German company. Khushi is posted in Jaipur, while Gustav works in Germany. A year ago, Gustav came to Jaipur for company work. During this time, he met Khushi. Khushi speaks German very well. This made things easier for Gustav in India. With Khushi's help, Gustav adapted to India. They gradually grew closer to each other. Things progressed, and they fell in love. Then the matter reached marriage. They said - Both got engaged at Green Park. During the 3-day program, Haldi and Mehendi ceremonies were held on Thursday, followed by a cocktail party on Friday, where Gustav had lots of fun. Our daughter knows the German language well. Food translators were arranged to avoid language problems for other guests. Family had shifted from Firozabad to Jaipur Jyoti said that Khushi's entire family had shifted from Firozabad to Jaipur many years ago. Khushi's father works in a private company there. Khushi also completed her education there. Khushi has done BTech and MBA. Started a new life holding hands Local people also attended the wedding in large numbers and blessed the bride and groom. Both families shared joy by embracing each other. Gustav and Khushi's couple started a new life holding hands. They gave the message that love has no boundaries, neither of language nor of country. Gustav said - People here are very friendly Gustav said that India is a large and diverse country. There are different types of people here. There are languages. There is culture. Every city has its own way and behaviour. Sometimes people seem very formal in front of foreigners, but most people, especially families, are very welcoming and heartfelt. This is what he liked best about India. He said - It's difficult to describe the experience of India and Indian people in words. Large countries and small cities like Piham or Shikohabad have less pollution and traffic. People are natural and friendly. The experience here was very lovely.

stories.title: What’s the punishment for public death threats?:Rahul, Shah Rukh among victims – which IPC category deals with such cases?
stories.summary: UP's Raebareli MP Rahul Gandhi, alongwith 25 MPs, received death threats of being shot at home. Congress leader Pawan Khera shared a related video on the social media platform X on February 19. However, police quickly detained the accused, who was from Rajasthan. In January 2026, Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan had also received similar threats. Akhil Bhartiya Hindu Mahasabha's Agra district president Meera Rathore had announced a reward of one lakh rupees for 'cutting his tongue'. What category of crime does giving death threats and announcing 'rewards' against someone fall under? Which sections of law apply in such situations? What are the punishment provisions? Read in Bhaskar Explainer... Question: Is giving threats to someone legally considered a crime? Answer: Former UP DGP Vikram Singh explains - threatening to kill someone or cause harm is a direct offense under Indian law. Under current law, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) categorizes this as criminal intimidation. According to Section 351 of BNS, if a person threatens another person with harm to their life, body, property, or reputation, with the intention to cause fear, create pressure, or force someone to do something, it will be considered a punishable offense. According to Vikram Singh, general threats can result in up to 2 years imprisonment or a fine, or both. If the threat involves murder, serious injury, arson, or major crimes, it can lead to up to 7 years imprisonment and a fine. Additionally, if the threat is anonymous, the punishment will increase by 2 more years. Question: Does this fall under the category of a non-bailable offense? Answer: In cases of death threats or threats of serious harm to someone, this offense can fall under the non-bailable category. However, it depends on the nature of the threat and under which sections the case has been registered. A general criminal threat case registered under Section 351 of BNS is usually bailable. It carries a provision of a maximum of 2 years' imprisonment. According to Vikram Singh, in the case of threats to Rahul Gandhi, it's not just about statements but falls under the category of serious criminal threats. Such public and explicit death threats are directly covered under Section 351 of BNS, 2023. This section provides for imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine. Question: Will the announcement of a reward also be counted as a threat and instigation? Answer: According to former DGP Vikram Singh, if someone publicly announces that 'a reward of 50 lakh rupees will be given for killing a particular person', this is not just a statement but is considered a serious criminal act. Such an announcement of reward becomes a crime on two levels: threat and instigation. According to former DGP Vikram Singh, announcing a reward directly falls under the category of criminal threat. Because it creates fear for life in the mind of the concerned person. This is considered an instigation for crime, as it motivates others to commit serious crimes like murder. In such cases, under Section 351 of BNS (Criminal Threat) and Section 61 of BNS (Instigation), the accused can be punished with imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine. Whether or not the murder or assault actually took place. Allahabad High Court Advocate Neeraj Pandey says - Under Section 351 of BNS, threatening to kill or cause serious harm is considered criminal. This section provides for imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine if found guilty. Question: Why punishment even when crime is not completed? Answer: The law believes that public announcement of rewards creates an atmosphere of fear in society and promotes crime. Therefore, merely making such an announcement is punishable, even if no person actually commits that crime. Question: Can an FIR be filed just based on a statement? Answer: Yes. According to lawyer Neeraj Pandey, an FIR can be registered merely based on a statement or threat. It doesn't require an actual incident or attack to occur. Under Indian law, criminal threats and incitement are considered complete offenses. Question: What do the SC guidelines say? Answer: The Supreme Court guidelines clearly state that the right to freedom of expression (Free Speech) is not unlimited. Where any statement leads to violence, threats, incitement, or creates an atmosphere of fear, that's where the limit of free speech is considered to end. The Supreme Court has clarified in several important judgments that while Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution gives citizens freedom of speech, reasonable restrictions can be imposed on this freedom under Article 19(2). Question: Are threats justified in the name of religious or political sentiments? Answer: According to lawyer Neeraj Pandey, if a person makes threats using religious or political sentiments, they can be charged under sections related to criminal intimidation, incitement, and disturbing public peace. In such cases, the court examines whether the statement has the effect of spreading fear and inciting violence, rather than the speaker's claimed emotions or intentions. The Supreme Court also states that the Constitution gives citizens the right to express their views, protest, and show dissent. However, this right exists only within the boundaries of law. As soon as any statement starts creating threats, violence, or fear for life, it goes beyond the scope of freedom of expression. Question: Does viral videos or statements make the crime more serious? Answer: Vikram Singh says - Absolutely, when a threatening statement or video goes viral, it makes the crime more serious. When someone issues death threats or provocative statements through public platforms, social media, or videos, their impact is not limited to just one person. It creates a situation of fear and unrest in society. In such cases, police do not limit themselves to just criminal threats. They can add strict sections related to incitement, disturbing public peace, and spreading terror. This directly results in the case becoming non-bailable. It becomes difficult for the accused to get relief. Question: Are there separate laws for threats against MPs or national leaders? Answer: According to former DGP Sulkhan Singh, the law is equal for everyone. The same punishment that applies to a common person in cases of threatening anyone will apply to all, whether they are MPs, leaders, or ordinary citizens. However, an important difference in the law comes in situations where a person threatens a public servant or a related person to force them to do something. Or tries to stop or influence legitimate work.

stories.title: SP leaders under house arrest in Varanasi:Delegates to visit Dalmandi on Akhilesh's instructions, entry prohibited
stories.summary: The residents of Dalmandi are facing significant distress following the recent demolition drive in the area. In response to the situation, a delegation from SP will meet with people to understand their pain and assess the impact of the action. Party’s National President, Akhilesh Yadav, has directed party leaders to visit Dalmandi and engage directly with those impacted. Leader of Opposition in Legislative Council, teacher MLC Lal Bihari Yadav has nominated 11 people on the direction of National President. Names of leaders included in the delegation have come forward. After this letter emerged, Varanasi police became active. Many SP leaders have been placed under house arrest since night. Police officials said that there is no permission to go to Dalmandi. No entry without permission SP delegation will meet affected families in Dalmandi today. Before this, police surveillance was placed at homes of many SP leaders in the city. They have been placed under house arrest. In this regard, Lanka police reached SP leader Satyaprakash Sonkar's house. When he asked the reason for this action, he got know that the delegation is going to Dalmandi. However, he cannot enter Dalmandi without permission. Therefore, security has been placed at his house. Satyaprakash Sonkar called it dictatorship saying that “Across the country we talk about the constitution and a person cannot even go anywhere to understand someone's pain and suffering. This is wrong”. Government better give us death than house arrest Lanka police also reached SP leader Aman Yadav's house late night and placed him under house arrest. He was also told that he cannot go to Dalmandi. Because no one is allowed to go inside there. On this Aman Yadav said “The government has put us under house arrest. Instead of house arrest, the government should give death sentence to socialists. What does the government think that we will get scared of this?'' He further added that Police keeps us under house arrest from time to time. Due to this, those of us who work will soon become unemployed. So is this also a government conspiracy? Because the company won't listen to all these excuses. This is the government's dictatorial attitude. SP government will not tolerate this and will continue to raise voice against oppression. Know who all are in SP's delegation list On the direction of National President Akhilesh Yadav, Leader of Opposition Lal Bihari Yadav has formed a delegation of 11 people under the leadership of former minister Surendra Patel to meet the victims in Dalmandi and understand their pain who will go to Dalmandi today. This includes former minister Surendra Patel, graduate MLC Ashutosh Sinha, district president Sujit Yadav, state president of women's assembly Ribu Srivastava, former candidate Ashfaq Ahmad W, former MLA Samad Ansari, former candidate Pooja Yadav, former metropolitan president Vishnu Sharma, former general secretary Lalu Yadav and Dilshad Ahmad Dillu. What is the Dalmandi project and how many people will be affected? The total budget for Dalmandi widening is ₹215 crore. Dalmandi is to be widened to a total of 17.05 meters. A total of 181 houses and 6 mosques are coming under this widening. Currently, PWD has demolished 20 houses. More than 40 houses have been registered. Currently, demolition work is ongoing on 30 houses. PWD has to complete the binding of Dalmandi and hand it over to the executing agency by June 2026. Millions of families will face livelihood crisis According to government figures, there are 1400 shops in Dalmandi. Additionally, according to locals, there are approximately 10,000 shops here. About 1 lakh people work in these shops. In such a situation, the demolition of Dalmandi will create a livelihood crisis for these one lakh people. The shopkeepers here say that the government should develop but what is the need to make it 17 meters wide. Take 10 feet but not more than that. 650-meter long road to be built for ₹215 crores The total length of Dalmandi road up to Chauk police station is 650 meters. The draft to make this road 17.5 meters wide has been passed. For this, a budget of ₹215 crores was approved on the last day of financial year 2024-25 and ₹2 crore have also been released. The PWD team has measured how wide the road is at different points, which houses are coming in the affected area, registry of 181 houses has begun after their measurement and demolition work has started. Additionally, there are 6 mosques in this area. PWD officials prepared the data. Based on this data, compensation was assessed, which is approximately ₹191 crore. So far, 40 houses have been registered. The demolition of houses is being carried out gradually. Road will be 60 feet wide According to PWD officials, the 650-meter Dal Mandi street from New Road to Chauk Police Station is to be widened to 60 feet. This will include a 30-foot road and 15-foot footpaths on both sides. Electricity, sewer, and water systems will be placed underground within this. The mess of wires here will be cleared.

stories.title: Clouds cover entire Purvanchal, rain likely:Day temperature reaches 32°C in UP, snowfall on mountains brings colder nights
stories.summary: The weather is set to turn bad again in Uttar Pradesh. Clouds have covered several districts of Purvanchal. Rain is likely here along with strong winds. The Meteorological Department says the impact of snowfall in the hills will be seen across the state. The sky will remain cloudy. During this period, winds may blow at a speed of 20 to 30 km per hour. Such weather conditions are expected to continue for the next four days. In the state on Saturday, except for a few districts, the weather remained clear since morning. Light fog was seen in five cities including Gorakhpur. The remaining districts witnessed bright sunshine. Strong winds created a slight chill in the air. In the past 24 hours, Sultanpur was the hottest, recording a maximum temperature of 32.2°C. Banda recorded the lowest minimum temperature at 8.4°C. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said- Currently there are no signs of any major weather system being active in UP. As such, after light rain, the weather is likely to be dry and clear. In the coming days, mild warmth may persist during the day, while night temperatures will continue to fluctuate slightly. Crops will be damaged by heat BHU's Agriculture Department Professor PK Singh says - March could prove to be a challenging month for farmers. The rise in temperature will affect the rabi crop. Especially wheat. Due to the heat, the grains will not develop fully. This will result in lower yield. According to PK Singh, crops like mustard, chickpeas, and peas can also be damaged by hot winds. Rising temperatures cause the soil in fields to dry quickly. This increases irrigation costs. Crops experience stress. How has the weather been so far? Now read when intense heat will start and how high the temperature will reach 1- Summer begins from 1st week of March BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava says, the weather will start changing completely from the first week of March, and the summer season will begin. The temperature will rise rapidly during both day and night. By the last week of March, the maximum temperature in many districts of UP could reach 35 to 38 degrees Celsius. 2- Mercury will reach 42 to 45 degrees in May-June Manoj Srivastava says - temperature is likely to remain around 40 degrees Celsius in April. In May-June, maximum temperature in many districts could reach 42 to 45 degrees. This means there will be less relief from heat, not only during the day but also at night, and humidity will persist. However, this will largely depend on the El Niño conditions. If El Niño conditions persist or strengthen, the heat situation could become even more serious. 3- Heat wave will last longer During March to May, maximum and minimum temperatures will remain above normal across the country, including UP. Only in March, both maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain above normal throughout the country. Additionally, the number of heat wave days will also be higher than normal. Heat wave days will remain normal only in northeastern India and peninsular states like Maharashtra, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh. 4- Crops will be damaged due to heat BHU's Agriculture Department Professor PK Singh says - March month could prove challenging for farmers. The rise in temperature will affect the Rabi crop. Especially wheat. Due to heat, grains will not develop fully. This will result in lower yield. According to PK Singh, hot winds can also damage crops like mustard, chickpeas, and peas. Due to rising temperatures, the soil in fields dries up quickly. This increases irrigation costs. Crops face stress. 5- Early rise in temperature, conditions will worsen further According to Dhruvsen Singh, Head of the Department of Earth Sciences at Lucknow University, temperatures have increased earlier than usual in 2026. Heat wave events may occur more frequently and for longer durations. Conditions could become more severe in urban areas due to the urban heat island effect. All these factors combined are continuously pushing temperatures upward.
