19 lose sight after Cataract surgeries in Gorakhpur:Families fall into debt; 9 patients undergo eye removal following severe infections
stories.summary: At least 19 people in Gorakhpur district suffered severe bacterial infections following cataract surgeries conducted at a private hospital, leaving nine patients with their eyes surgically removed and ten others losing vision. The patients had undergone cataract operations on February 1 at New Rajesh Hi-Tech Hospital in Sikariganj during a free camp organised under the Ayushman Bharat scheme. Out of 30 surgeries performed that day, 19 patients developed serious infections within 24 hours. “We went to improve vision, returned in debt” Mahima, whose 80-year-old father-in-law Ramdarash underwent surgery, recounted the ordeal. “My father-in-law suddenly began screaming in pain. Blood started oozing from his eye. We panicked. We had to take a loan and rush to Delhi. Doctors there had to remove one of his eyes to relieve the pain,” she said. She added, “We went to get his eyesight improved. Now we are burdened with debt.” Ramdarash developed a bacterial infection within a day of the surgery and was later treated in Delhi, where his infected eye was removed. District Administration orders probe, OT sealed After the matter reached Lucknow, Gorakhpur District Magistrate Deepak Meena ordered an inquiry and directed the Additional District Magistrate (ADM) to submit a report within 24 hours. The hospital’s operating theatre (OT) has been sealed. Preliminary investigation revealed shocking findings. According to the DM, bacterial infection was detected in the OT where the surgeries were conducted, as well as on the surgical instruments used. The hospital’s registration is now set to be cancelled. Patients’ stories: Pain, panic, and financial ruin Devaraji Devi, 60 Eye removed after severe infection Devaraji Devi from Barigaon underwent cataract surgery on her left eye. Her daughter-in-law Sanjita said she began vomiting and experiencing severe pain the same night. She was referred from one hospital to another before being taken to AIIMS Delhi, where doctors confirmed bacterial infection and removed her eye on February 6. “Even after surgery, the pain persists. We’ve already spent a large amount on treatment. Despite everything, she will never see from that eye again,” Sanjita said. Dinanath, 75 Writhing in pain all night Dinanath from Bankata village experienced intense pain around 1 am after being discharged. Despite painkillers, his condition worsened. He was eventually taken to AIIMS Delhi, where his eye was removed on February 11. “We never imagined this would happen,” said his grandson Satish Vishwakarma. Meera Devi, 55 Both eyes infected; one removed Meera Devi from Rampur developed vomiting and severe pain the morning after surgery. Doctors at AIIMS confirmed infection in both eyes. One eye was removed after her condition stabilized. Her son Bhimnath said, “We’ve spent around ₹40,000 so far. Doctors’ negligence has cost us dearly.” Rajendra Kumar, 71 Hope fading for vision recovery Rajendra from Innadih lost his eyesight after infection spread. Doctors at SGPGI Lucknow reportedly said the damage was irreversible. “We are still hoping for a miracle, but doctors say the infection has destroyed his vision,” his son said. Ranjeet, 71 Bleeding from eye after surgery Ranjeet from Bharsi noticed bleeding from his eye at night. He was later admitted to Gorakhpur AIIMS, where his eye was removed after a week of treatment. “I didn’t have money for treatment. Initially, I had to arrange ₹4,000–5,000. Later, the hospital provided ₹15,000 in assistance. I lost an eye, but at least I survived,” he said. Bahidun Nisha, 60 One eye saved, one lost Bahidun Nisha had gone only for a check-up but was advised surgery. Two days later, she developed pain. Both eyes were infected, but doctors managed to save vision in one eye. She continues treatment in Delhi. Ramdarash, 80 Treatment amid family wedding preparations Ramdarash’s family is struggling financially. “We are taking loans for treatment, and there’s a wedding in the family next month. We don’t know how we’ll manage,” said Mahima. Mohammad Ali, 69 Escaped infection, relieved after check-up Mohammad Ali, who underwent surgery the following day, said he was frightened after seeing news reports but was later relieved when a follow-up check-up confirmed no infection. Now read Akhilesh Yadav's post Health officials confirm bacterial contamination Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rajesh Jha termed the incident a “serious case of negligence.” He confirmed bacterial contamination was found in the operation theatre and surgical instruments. A magisterial inquiry is underway, and further action will be decided after the final report. What is Cataract? Cataract is a condition in which the eye’s natural lens becomes cloudy, leading to blurred vision and difficulty performing routine tasks such as reading or driving. Surgery is required to prevent blindness. Why does bacterial infection occur after Cataract surgery? Post-surgical bacterial infection may occur due to: Doctors advise immediate consultation if pain or blurred vision occurs after surgery. Special precautions are necessary for patients with diabetes or cancer.

The incident involved protests and police intervention, with tensions rising after threats against Kumar.

stories.title: 'Leave Iran': India issues fresh warning to its nationals as tensions soar; citizens asked to exercise caution
stories.summary: Amidst escalating Middle East tensions and fears of war, the Indian Embassy in Tehran has urgently advised all Indian nationals, including students and tourists, to depart Iran. This directive follows previous advisories and comes as US President Donald Trump issued a stern warning to Tehran regarding nuclear deal negotiations. The embassy has provided contact details for assistance.

stories.title: 326 days, harsh terrain, well-knit intelligence grid: How forces took down 7 terrorists in J&K's Kishtwar
'It’s Didi’s turn': Delhi CM Rekha Gupta targets Mamata in Bengal pitch
stories.summary: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta attacked West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, accusing her government of hindering development and failing to ensure women's safety. Gupta questioned the utilization of central funds, stating that development has not reached the poor in Bengal. She also highlighted concerns over women's safety, citing specific incidents and criticizing the state's conditions.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at warehouse in Abu Dhabi’s Al Muzoon industrial area, no injuries reported
stories.summary: A major fire erupted at an Abu Dhabi warehouse on February 23, 2026, triggering a swift emergency response. Civil defence and police teams are actively battling the blaze, with no casualties reported so far. Investigations into the cause will commence once the site is secured, highlighting the UAE's focus on fire preparedness.

stories.title: US: 3.5-magnitude earthquake strikes off Southern California coast near Rancho Palos Verdes
stories.summary: A late-night tremor shook Southern California on Sunday. A 3.5-magnitude earthquake occurred offshore near Rancho Palos Verdes. The quake was felt widely across Los Angeles and Orange Counties. Authorities reported no injuries or damage from the seismic activity. This is the third offshore earthquake in the region this week.

stories.title: ‘Mothers, sisters living in fear’: PM Modi writes to people of Bengal ahead of polls
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed heartbreak over West Bengal's current condition in a letter to voters, accusing the state government of "extreme non-cooperation." He highlighted central government schemes that have benefited millions in the state and pledged to build a developed and prosperous West Bengal if the BJP comes to power.

stories.title: UAE foils massive AI cyber attack targeting Government digital systems
stories.summary: The UAE thwarted a major cyberattack this past weekend. Sophisticated AI-powered assaults targeted national digital platforms and vital infrastructure. The UAE Cybersecurity Council confirmed the attacks were organized and aimed at destabilizing the nation. Advanced monitoring and rapid response systems prevented widespread disruption. Essential services remained operational. This incident highlights the growing threat of cyber warfare.

stories.title: UAE launches first 7-year Islamic Sukuk: AED 550m tranche sees sixfold demand surge
stories.summary: The UAE has successfully launched its first seven-year Islamic Treasury Sukuk. This new offering, valued at AED550 million, attracted nearly six times its value in bids. The issuance marks the longest maturity under the program. This move strengthens the UAE's Islamic finance framework and the dirham yield curve. Investor confidence in the national economy remains high.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu polls: Udhayanidhi Stalin’s ‘don't fear PM Modi or even his father’ remark sparks BJP backlash
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin's remark that the DMK "neither fears the Prime Minister nor his father" has sparked a political storm. BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla accused Stalin of making personal attacks against PM Modi and his late father, citing past controversial statements.

stories.title: ‘He’s sweating now’: Activists hang ex-prince Andrew arrest photo inside France's Louvre Museum
stories.summary: A British activist group, 'Everyone Hates Elon,' staged a daring stunt at the Louvre, hanging a framed photo of ex-Prince Andrew. The image, taken after his arrest on misconduct charges, was captioned 'He's Sweating Now,' referencing his controversial 2019 interview. The group's bold move aims to draw attention to the ongoing scrutiny surrounding Andrew's association with Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: Planning umrah? Saudi Arabia launches visit guide for global pilgrims in 16 languages
stories.summary: Pilgrims undertaking Umrah now have a comprehensive, 16-language guide from the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah. This resource simplifies rituals, clarifies visa and permit requirements, and details movement within holy sites. It covers the entire journey from preparation to departure, enhancing awareness and ensuring a smoother, more peaceful spiritual experience for all.

stories.title: Shirtless AI Summit protest: Delhi police makes 5th arrest; nabs Youth Congress worker from Gwalior
stories.summary: Delhi Police arrested Jitendra Yadav in Gwalior, marking the fifth arrest in connection with the Youth Congress protest at the AI Impact Summit. The protest, described by a court as a "blatant assault on public order," involved displaying T-shirts with slogans against the government and a trade deal, leading to a scuffle with security.

stories.title: US, Iran to resume nuclear talks in Geneva on Thursday as military pressure mounts
stories.summary: Iran and the US are set for a third round of nuclear talks in Geneva amid rising regional tensions. Washington is increasing its military presence and pressing Tehran for a swift deal, with President Trump issuing a 10-15 day ultimatum. Iran has warned of retaliation against US forces and facilities in the region if attacked.

stories.title: India unveils ‘MANAS 1’: AI trained on 60,000 hours of brainwaves aims to detect disorders early
stories.summary: An Indian team has developed MANAS 1, an AI model trained on extensive brainwave data to detect neurological and psychiatric disorders early. This foundational platform, built on 60,000 hours of recordings, aims to interpret the brain's electrical signals, potentially aiding doctors in remote areas and reducing diagnostic delays for conditions like epilepsy and dementia. A next-generation version is anticipated soon.

stories.title: Who was 'El Mencho' and what's next for Mexico's fastest-growing cartel?
stories.summary: Mexico’s most-wanted drug lord Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as El Mencho, was killed during a government operation in Jalisco, triggering nationwide cartel violence. Founder of the powerful Jalisco New Generation Cartel, he built one of Mexico’s fastest-growing and most aggressive criminal organisations. His death is a major blow to the group but raises fears of fragmentation, succession struggles and escalating “narcoterrorism” as rivals and factions vie for control.

stories.title: 'Axis of nations committed to stability': Netanyahu praises India ahead of PM Modi’s Israel visit
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is looking forward to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit. He described the India-Israel relationship as a strong partnership focused on innovation and security. This visit will further strengthen their special bond. Netanyahu also shared his vision for a regional alliance. Prime Minister Modi's trip marks his second visit to Israel, following his historic 2017 journey.

stories.title: 'Without Mamata di …': Mani Shankar Aiyar's advise to Rahul Gandhi on INDIA bloc leadership
stories.summary: Veteran Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar asserted Mamata Banerjee is crucial for the INDIA bloc's survival, urging Rahul Gandhi to cede leadership to smaller parties. Aiyar, who expressed admiration for Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan, also voiced contempt for Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera. The party has since distanced itself from Aiyar's controversial statements.

stories.title: Supermarkets, banks, cars set ablaze: Mexico cartel goes on revenge spree after El Mencho killed
stories.summary: Mexico experienced a coordinated wave of retaliation following the killing of feared cartel boss El Mencho. Gunmen loyal to the CJNG leader blocked highways and torched businesses, disrupting air travel and prompting residents to seek shelter. This show of force, described as revenge, highlights the ongoing challenges of cartel violence in the country.

Roy, who represented Krishnanagar Uttar and served twice in the Rajya Sabha, had a notable political journey, including stints with the BJP before rejoining the TMC. His son confirmed the news.

stories.title: 'Be aware': Indian embassy issues advisory for nationals in Mexico after powerful drug lord 'El Mencho' killed

stories.title: 'Global power that is India': Benjamin Netanyahu's message ahead of PM Modi's Israel visit
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hailed India as a "global power" ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's upcoming visit. stories.summary: Congress faces a significant setback in Assam as former state chief Bhupen Borah joins the BJP, echoing past defections. stories.title: Posting legal tips on TikTok? Firms suspended, complaints filed against expats in major enforcement of licensing rules in Kuwait
stories.summary: Kuwait's Bar Association is cracking down on unlicensed legal advice shared online, filing complaints against expatriates offering consultations via social media. stories.summary: Former prince Andrew’s legal troubles linked to the Epstein Files may seem dramatic in today’s news cycle, but European history tells a far darker story of how disgraced royals were once treated. The discovery transformed tropical medicine, made projects like the Panama Canal possible, and reshaped humanity’s fight against epidemic disease.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: SC orders judicial officers to be part of SIR duty in Bengal; Centre slams Congress' 'topless' protest at AI Summit
From Bill Gates to former prince Andrew: The biggest names felled by the Epstein files
stories.summary: In most cases, the documents do not accuse those named of participating in Epstein’s crimes. The consequences have instead flowed from the visibility of continued contact, personal familiarity, or financial links that became publicly indefensible once exposed.

stories.title: 'PM Modi torn between grips of US & China': Rahul returns with jiu-jitsu analogy; explains why he used it in Parliament
Who after Vijayan? Left’s tryst with first-time voters and survival in Kerala
stories.summary: As Kerala gears up for the 2026 elections, the future of the Left beyond chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan is a pressing concern. Despite his strong leadership, the absence of a clear successor and the need to connect with a new generation of voters pose significant challenges for the LDF's continued relevance and its status as India's sole communist-governed state.

stories.title: “It sparked up something deep”: Vic Mensa credits IShowSpeed’s Africa tour with reshaping how millions view the continent
stories.summary: Vic Mensa praised IShowSpeed’s 28-day Africa livestream tour, saying it helped challenge long-held stereotypes and reshape global perceptions of the continent. Speaking on a podcast, Mensa noted that millions experienced Africa in real time through Speed’s streams. He believes the journey provided authentic cultural insight, while Speed himself said the trip deeply inspired him and sparked personal growth.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia: King Salman orders disbursement of SAR3 billion in Ramadan aid for households
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is providing over SAR3 billion in Ramadan assistance to social security beneficiaries, following a royal directive. Heads of households will receive SAR1,000, with SAR500 for each dependent. This initiative, backed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, aims to ease financial burdens during the holy month, with funds expected in bank accounts shortly.

stories.title: Missile swarms & drone hordes: Why US should think twice before attacking Iran
stories.summary: The US has significantly boosted its military presence in the Gulf with two aircraft carrier strike groups and advanced stealth fighters, citing tensions with Iran over its nuclear program and regional stability. This build-up, including reinforced missile defense systems, aims to secure the vital Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy corridor.

stories.title: 'Congress left borders open': Amit Shah raises infiltration pitch in poll-bound Assam
stories.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah accused the Congress of leaving Assam's borders open to infiltrators, aiming to alter the state's demographics. He contrasted this with the BJP government's efforts under CM Himanta Biswa Sarma, who he stated cleared vast lands occupied by infiltrators. Shah also highlighted the BJP's infrastructure development achievements in Assam.

stories.title: 'Topless, brainless, shameless': Centre slams Congress after youth wing's shirtless march at AI Summit, blames Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: BJP has accused the Congress of disrupting the AI Impact Summit to damage India's global image, alleging the protest was directed by Rahul Gandhi. Youth Congress workers staged a demonstration, raising slogans against the Prime Minister, leading to detentions. BJP leaders condemned the act as an attempt to embarrass India on the world stage.

stories.title: Bengal vs EC: SC takes 'extraordinary' step, judicial officers to be part of SIR duty
Congress paradox: Shashi Tharoor praises AI Summit, youth leaders protest on spot
stories.summary: Youth Congress workers staged a shirtless protest against a trade deal at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, leading to their detention. This occurred hours after Congress MP Shashi Tharoor praised the summit's organization and global stature, and also supported a defense deal with France.

stories.title: Why rights exist but justice remains out of reach for the poor
stories.summary: Millions in India eligible for free legal aid remain unaware or distrustful, hindering access to justice. Poverty creates legal vulnerability, preventing the poor from asserting their rights due to hidden costs like lost wages and travel. Despite a comprehensive framework, structural issues like low awareness and funding misuse persist, leaving constitutional promises unfulfilled for the most vulnerable.

Jeffrey Epstein's estate agrees to $35 million settlement for victims
stories.summary: Jeffrey Epstein's estate has agreed to a substantial settlement, potentially reaching $35 million, for victims alleging abuse and trafficking. This proposed judgment covers alleged assaults spanning over two decades, from 1995 until Epstein's death in prison. The agreement, pending judicial approval, follows the release of numerous investigation documents, hinting at the vast network Epstein maintained with influential figures.

stories.title: Donald Trump loved his visit to India, told me the culture is unmatched: US envoy Sergio Gor
stories.summary: US Ambassador Sergio Gor hinted at an upcoming meeting between Prime Minister Modi and President Trump, emphasizing growing AI and semiconductor cooperation. India's signing of the Pax Silica Declaration, alongside US officials, signifies a pivotal moment for bilateral ties, fostering collaboration in advanced technologies among trusted nations.

stories.title: UAE’s Etihad Rail operator Keolis appoints Yoen Dupuis as CEO ahead of passenger service launch
stories.summary: Keolis has appointed Yoen Dupuis as the new CEO for its Middle East and East Asia regions, based in the UAE. stories.summary: Ramadan has begun in the UAE, with anticipation building for Eid Al Fitr. The exact length of the public holiday, potentially four days, hinges on the crescent moon sighting on March 18. Whether Ramadan lasts 29 or 30 days, a long weekend is expected, with official dates subject to confirmation.

stories.title: Defamation case: Rahul Gandhi records statement in Sultanpur court over remarks on Amit Shah
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi appeared in a Sultanpur court on Friday for a 2018 criminal defamation case concerning remarks allegedly made about Amit Shah during the Karnataka Assembly elections. The case, filed by a BJP leader, accuses Gandhi of calling Shah an "accused in a murder case," a statement Gandhi denies as politically motivated.

stories.title: Dubai unveils 10 new mosques ahead of Ramadan 2026, 5 more to boost worship capacity
stories.summary: Dubai is expanding its spiritual infrastructure with 15 new mosques opening for Ramadan, aiming to accommodate its growing population and enhance community life. These new sanctuaries, strategically located across residential hubs, will serve as spiritual and social centers, hosting events and offering inclusive services. The city also plans for 55 more mosques, including a 3D-printed one by 2026.

stories.title: Inside the MQ-9 Reaper: How America’s armed drones reshape regional security
stories.summary: The US is expanding its MQ-9 Reaper drone deployments across the Indo-Pacific, creating a robust surveillance and strike network. These long-endurance aircraft enhance intelligence gathering and precision strikes, with allies increasingly acquiring the platform to bolster regional interoperability and information sharing.

stories.title: Saudi-Bahrain King Fahd Causeway toll hike: Cars now pay 35 SAR, discounts up to 40% introduced
stories.summary: The King Fahd Causeway has implemented new toll rates for the first time in a decade, impacting cars, buses, and trucks. While most travelers face increased fees, students, people with disabilities, and daily commuters with special cards remain exempt. The Authority also introduced discount packages via the Jesr app to offset costs and enhance the digital travel experience.

stories.title: Six women among eight friends killed in California’s deadliest avalanche in decades
stories.summary: Six women and three guides perished in California's deadliest avalanche in decades during a backcountry ski trip. The group of eight friends, experienced skiers, were caught by a massive slide triggered by a winter storm. Investigations are underway into why the tour continued despite avalanche warnings, as families mourn the loss of their loved ones.

stories.title: 'Talk about youth and women of Assam': Priyanka Gandhi slams CM Himanta Sarma over remarks on Gaurav Gagoi's family
stories.summary: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra criticized Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma, stating he is "rattled" by MP Gaurav Gogoi and resorting to personal attacks and "politics of polarization." Similar releases were announced in Ajman (134 inmates) and Fujairah (125 inmates), with Fujairah's selection based on good conduct.

stories.title: Pakistan says Imran Khan rejected 'serious deals' twice for release from jail
stories.summary: A top aide to Pakistan's PM claims Imran Khan rejected two "serious" release deals, one involving a former KP chief minister and another from abroad. The government denies any leniency, calling Khan a "convicted criminal" amid concerns over his deteriorating eyesight in prison.

stories.title: 'A place where Jews have always been welcome': Influencer shows how India has welcomed Jews for 2000 years
stories.summary: For over two millennia, India offered a unique haven for Jewish communities, free from the persecution common elsewhere. From the Bene Israel to Cochin and Baghdadi Jews, they thrived under various rulers, integrating into society. While migration has reduced numbers, their historical presence and peaceful coexistence remain a remarkable chapter in Jewish history.

This marks the first joint outreach since ethnic violence erupted. While resettlement efforts are underway, mistrust persists, with displaced individuals sharing concerns about jobs, education, and healthcare access. The CM pledged support for students and security for patients.

stories.title: Thyroid, infection drugs get fresh safety warnings after national review
stories.summary: Two widely used medications, doxycycline and carbimazole, are set to receive stronger safety warnings. Regulators have identified potential mental health side effects for doxycycline and a rare but serious blood disorder linked to carbimazole. This proactive step aims to enhance patient safety by ensuring clearer information for both doctors and patients regarding these important, albeit uncommon, adverse reactions.

stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman highlighted India's pivotal role in AI, revealing over 100 million weekly ChatGPT users, with a third being students. He emphasized India's potential to lead AI development and deployment.

stories.summary: The “Larry Wheels Files” began after Greg Doucette accused Larry Wheels of sending troubling messages and failing to repay $50,000. Jon Bravo later released a detailed video with more screenshots and claims. Larry has denied being in an open relationship and rejected parts of the allegations. stories.title: Who is Charles Bronson? Britain’s most notorious prisoner, will he finally be released after 50 years?
stories.summary: Charles Bronson, now legally Charles Salvador, has spent over 50 years in prison, much in solitary confinement, for violent offenses including hostage-taking. stories.title: Indian Navy likely to commission third indigenous N-powered submarine by April-May
stories.summary: India's sea-based nuclear deterrent is set to be significantly bolstered with the upcoming commissioning of INS Aridhaman, the third indigenous Arihant-class nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine. This larger vessel, capable of carrying long-range K-4 missiles, will enhance India's "second-strike" capability and move it closer to achieving continuous at-sea deterrence.

stories.title: Ready to raise India content in Rafale: Macron
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron affirmed that Rafale jets will bolster India's military might and expressed commitment to increasing indigenous content in 'made-in-India Rafale' aircraft. stories.summary: India's Gaganyaan program received a significant boost with the successful qualification level load test of its drogue parachute at DRDO's RTRS facility. This dynamic test, simulating loads higher than maximum flight conditions, demonstrated India's capability in designing and manufacturing high-strength ribbon parachutes, marking a crucial step towards self-reliance in human spaceflight.

The board, focused on the Gaza ceasefire and rebuilding, saw pledges of $7 billion from several nations, with the US contributing $10 billion. Trump praised both Rubio and Vice President Vance for their contributions.

stories.title: Flooding shuts down Baglihar hydropower project in J&K
stories.summary: Operations at the Baglihar hydropower project's stage 1 in Jammu and Kashmir were halted due to flooding in the machine room. While stage 1 remains suspended for scheduled maintenance, stage 2, unaffected by the flooding, will continue to generate power. stories.title: 'I don't believe in media censorship': J&K CM Omar Abdullah
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah asserted his commitment against media censorship and using government s for influence. He pledged to rationalize the policy for transparency, basing allocations on objective criteria like circulation and readership. Abdullah also highlighted efforts to fill thousands of vacant government posts and stressed the urgency of climate change response for the region.

stories.title: Clavicular makes New York City runway debut at Elena Velez show after Arizona arrest dismissal and looksmaxxing controversy
stories.summary: Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, brought his controversial looksmaxxing fame to New York City with a runway debut and major media coverage. stories.summary: America will boost the United Nations. President Donald Trump revealed plans to support the global body financially and ensure its proper functioning. He also mentioned past successes in settling wars without UN involvement.

stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah will launch Phase 2 of the Vibrant Villages Programme in Assam, a Rs 6,839 crore initiative to develop 1,954 villages along international borders. stories.title: Who’s really paying for your daily free ChatGPT use? OpenAI’s staggering costs revealed
stories.summary: ChatGPT’s explosive growth to nearly 900 million weekly users has transformed OpenAI into one of the fastest-scaling tech companies in histor, but at staggering cost. With annualized revenue surpassing $20 billion yet burn rates near $17 billion, the company is racing to balance subscriptions, enterprise sales, ads and a potential IPO against immense AI infrastructure demands.

stories.title: White supremacist Nick Fuentes urges supporters to skip midterms, says he hopes Trump is impeached and the GOP ‘crashes and burns’
stories.summary: Voters are urged to abstain from the upcoming midterm elections. The author believes a Republican defeat is essential for national salvation. This stance stems from perceived failures and mistakes attributed to Republican leadership and policies. The hope is for a complete collapse of the Republican party, potentially paving the way for a radical shift in future elections.

The Maratha ruler is frequently invoked as a symbol of indigenous sovereignty, martial pride and cultural assertion. References to Hindavi Swarajya resonate strongly with narratives centred on civilisational identity and self-determination.

stories.title: 'Will know in 10 days': Trump warns of 'bad things' if Iran doesn't make meaningful deal
stories.summary: America may take further action regarding Iran within ten days. President Donald Trump stated that if a meaningful deal is not reached, negative consequences will follow. Talks are ongoing, described as constructive but historically difficult. The US has increased military presence in the Middle East amid rising tensions. Iran has reinforced nuclear and missile sites.

stories.summary: New documents from Jeffrey Epstein's files are causing a stir. These papers detail years of communication linking the disgraced financier to powerful individuals worldwide. While Europe has seen swift consequences like resignations and investigations, the United States has experienced a more subdued reaction. Several prominent figures are facing scrutiny and uncomfortable questions following these disclosures.

stories.title: 'Nothing like money': Donald Trump claims '200% tariffs' warning forced India, Pakistan to stop fighting
stories.summary: Donald Trump claimed he averted war between India and Pakistan in May 2025 by threatening a 200% tariff on both nations. stories.summary: Israel has condemned a "absolutely unacceptable" attack on two Indian workers in Ashkelon, with police apprehending the perpetrators. A significant US military buildup in the Middle East, coupled with Iran's fortification of nuclear sites, raises fears of a major escalation. stories.title: 'Go to court, don't threaten people': Kerala BJP chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar hits out at CM Vijayan over ‘The Kerala Story 2’

stories.title: Schools open, buses cancelled across GTA amid Ontario winter storm: Weather forecast, other details families need to know

Freezing rain and snow created treacherous road conditions, prompting widespread cancellations despite schools remaining open. Commuters also faced disruptions as transit services adjusted schedules.

Rescue efforts are underway, with authorities investigating the cause of the tragedy amidst ongoing concerns about building safety in the city.

stories.title: Nigeria: At least 37 dead, several injured after toxic gas leak in mine
stories.summary: A toxic gas leak at a mining site in Nigeria's Plateau state has killed at least 37 people and hospitalized 26. stories.title: 'Her skin’s so beautiful': Trump’s unexpected praise for Nicki Minaj steals spotlight at Black History Month event in White House
stories.summary: President Donald Trump made headlines at a White House Black History Month event with personal praise for rapper Nicki Minaj. stories.summary: As Ramadan 2026 approaches, understanding greetings like 'Ramadan Mubarak' (Blessed Ramadan) and 'Ramadan Kareem' (Generous Ramadan) enhances cultural appreciation. While both are widely accepted globally, 'Kareem' resonates particularly in the Gulf's hospitable culture. Respectful wishes, regardless of the phrase, foster connection during this spiritual month.

stories.summary: A new report reveals significant hurdles for persons with disabilities in accessing India's justice system. stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir's tourism sector is showing signs of recovery following a significant downturn after the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. stories.title: Evening news wrap: PM Modi, Macron hold talks in Mumbai; Tarique Rahman sworn in as Bangladesh PM, and more
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi and French President Macron held significant talks in Mumbai, focusing on defence and trade. Meanwhile, Tarique Rahman was sworn in as Bangladesh's new Prime Minister, ending a long era of female leadership. Iran's Supreme Leader issued a stern warning to US President Trump, as Pakistan faced deadly attacks.

stories.title: “Jealous and spiteful women”: Laura Loomer blasts Candace Owens while backing Erika Kirk in Valentine’s Day post
stories.summary: Laura Loomer publicly defended Erika Kirk in a Valentine’s Day post while sharply criticizing Candace Owens, escalating an ongoing conservative media feud. Owens has questioned details about Erika’s marriage and events before Charlie Kirk’s death, drawing backlash from Loomer, who called the commentary harmful and defamatory. The dispute has intensified online, exposing deep divisions and keeping Erika Kirk at the center of public scrutiny.

stories.title: Bangladesh new govt: Hindu leader inducted into Tarique Rahman’s cabinet - who is Nitai Roy Chowdhury?
'Warship can be sent to sea floor': Khamenei's blunt warning to Trump, US
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei issued direct threats against President Trump and the US, warning that even the strongest military can be struck down. He highlighted Iran's capability to sink US warships and asserted that America will fail to eliminate the Islamic Republic, despite ongoing tensions and US surveillance efforts.

stories.title: Jesse Jackson Death: Why civil rights activist wanted to cut off Barack Obama's 'manhood'
stories.summary: To understand why Jackson reacted so viscerally to Obama, one must first understand who he was. Long before Obama’s rise, Jesse Jackson was the closest thing America had to a national Black political candidate. Born in segregated South Carolina, he came of age in the crucible of the civil rights movement. As a young organiser, he worked alongside Martin Luther King Jr., participated in marches across the South, and became known for his fiery oratory and instinct for political mobilisation.

stories.title: No visa, no paperwork needed for Indians: Armenia opens travel doors to expatriates across Gulf, US, Europe for 180 days
stories.summary: Armenia has introduced a temporary visa-free regime for Indian passport holders with specific residence permits, allowing stays up to 180 days annually until July 01, 2026. This move aims to boost tourism and business, particularly for Indians residing in the GCC, US and Europe, simplifying travel for cultural exploration and investment opportunities.

stories.title: “Illegal child labor”: MrBeast says child labor crisis in cocoa farms inspired him to launch Feastables
stories.summary: MrBeast says the widespread use of child labor in cocoa farming inspired him to launch Feastables as an ethical alternative to traditional chocolate brands. Citing over 1.5 million children in illegal labor, he emphasizes responsible sourcing and transparency. While experts note the issue is complex, his stance has renewed debate about supply chains, consumer responsibility, and ethical food production.

stories.title: Delhi University bans on-campus protest for a month after backlash over UCG equity guidelines
stories.summary: Delhi University has banned all gatherings, processions, and protests on its campuses for one month due to law and order concerns. This decision follows clashes between student groups over the now-stayed UGC equity guidelines. The university cited potential obstruction of traffic, threats to life, and disturbances to public peace as reasons for the prohibition.

stories.title: Qatar announces public sector working hours for Ramadan 2026
stories.summary: Qatar has announced shorter working days for government employees during Ramadan, with official hours set at five per day from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM. Civil servants can arrive as late as 10:00 AM if operational needs are met. The directive also allows up to 30% of staff to work remotely, prioritizing Qatari mothers and individuals with disabilities.

stories.title: What is the difference between asteroids, comets, and meteors
Tarique Rahman sworn in as Bangladesh Prime Minister
stories.summary: Tarique Rahman has been sworn in as Bangladesh's new Prime Minister, marking a significant shift after decades of female leadership. Son of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, Rahman returns from exile to lead the nation following the BNP's landslide victory in the recent general elections. His appointment signals a new era for Bangladesh's political landscape.

stories.title: 'From arsh to farsh': Mani Shankar Aiyar's 'Rahulian' outburst and 'uncle' syndrome
stories.summary: Mani Shankar Aiyar's critique of "Rahulian" politics sparks debate on the Congress's ideological shift from Nehruvianism to civil society influence. Analyst Rasheed Kidwai suggests Aiyar, though isolated, highlights a party increasingly shaped by non-dogmatic, issue-driven approaches, moving away from traditional party structures and veteran leadership's influence.

stories.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI likely to announce West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Assam, Kerala, Puducherry poll schedule in mid-March
Assam approves 3% reservation for tea tribes, Adivasis in Grade 1 and 2 govt jobs
stories.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma had announced a 3 per cent reservation for youths from tea gardens in Grade I and Grade II government jobs in October last year during the 19th biennial general conference of the Assam Tea Tribe Students’ Association (ATTSA) and the central biennial general conference of the Assam Tea Tribe Women’s Association.

stories.title: Rhode Island shooting: Gunman was transgender parent who went by 'Roberta'; what we know about him
stories.summary: Tragedy struck a Pawtucket hockey game as a gunman killed two and critically injured three. The shooter, identified as Robert Dorgan, a transgender father, reportedly targeted family members before taking his own life. Authorities are investigating the motive behind the horrific violence that has left the community in mourning.

stories.title: Fire in the sky: Kīlauea volcano erupts in Hawaii shooting lava 1,300 feet into the air in the 10-hour eruption
Missile message to Beijing? US to increase its fire power in Philippines
stories.summary: The US and Philippines are bolstering their defense in the South China Sea by deploying advanced missile systems. This move, aimed at deterring China's assertive actions, follows joint condemnation of Beijing's "illegal, coercive, aggressive, and deceptive activities." The allies are also increasing joint military drills and modernizing the Philippine armed forces, with the US planning further deployments of sophisticated weaponry.

stories.title: 'Messy, risky, dangerous': EAM Jaishankar says global order heading for 'twilight zone'
stories.summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said that ​​economics will give way to politics and security "when it comes to making choices and technology in the age of AI will be even more transformative than ever before." The minister also highlighted how the world today has been witnessing "weaponisation of production, finance, leveraging of market shares and tightening of export controls".

stories.title: Pakistan: Suicide bomber rams explosive-laden vehicle into security post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; 12 killed
stories.summary: A suicide bombing and attack by gunmen on a security post in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province resulted in the deaths of 11 soldiers and a child. Security forces thwarted the overnight breach attempt, later killing 12 TTP militants. The explosives-laden vehicle also damaged civilian homes, injuring seven others.

stories.title: Ramadan 2026 moon sighted in Saudi Arabia? KSA Supreme Court calls Muslims to spot crescent on February 17; first day of fasting from Feb 18?
stories.summary: Muslims worldwide are anticipating the crescent moon sighting tonight, February 17, 2026, to mark the beginning of Ramadan 1447 AH. Saudi authorities are urging citizens to report any sightings. If confirmed, fasting begins Wednesday, February 18. Otherwise, it starts Thursday, February 19. This tradition blends science and faith, setting the rhythm for prayer and community.

stories.title: 'PR hungry govt': Congress slams Centre over 'utter chaos', food-water shortage at AI Impact Summit; Vaishnaw replies
stories.summary: The Congress party has criticized the Centre's alleged mismanagement of the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, calling it an example of a "PR hungry" government that turned a global opportunity into "utter chaos." Party president Mallikarjun Kharge highlighted distress faced by participants, including founders, exhibitors, and visitors, due to logistical failures and disruptions.

stories.title: 'Could not become Assam's Congress CM because of Rahul Gandhi': Himanta revisits 2014 claim; recalls what Sonia told him
'Accident or murder?': Ajit Pawar's son Rohit Pawar questions 20-day delay plane crash probe
Not all humans are equally frightening to wildlife, says new study
stories.summary: New research suggests wildlife's fear of humans is not uniform. Animals exhibit strong fear responses to hunters and fishers but less so to tourists or researchers. Surprisingly, some passive human structures like roads can even act as perceived refuges for certain species.

stories.title: Azerbaijan grants visa-free travel to Omani citizens for one year
stories.summary: Omani nationals can now travel to Azerbaijan visa-free for short stays under a temporary one-year exemption. Starting February 15, 2026, Omani citizens can enter Azerbaijan for up to 30 days per visit, with a maximum of three visits allowed. This initiative aims to boost tourism and strengthen bilateral relations between the two nations.

stories.title: 'Conveniently ignored others': Supreme Court rejects plea against Himanta Sarma, Yogi Adityanath
stories.summary: The Supreme Court declined to entertain a plea for mandatory constitutional morality guidelines for public officials, citing the petition's focus on specific individuals. The court suggested a broader code of conduct for public figures, similar to that for public servants, emphasizing uniform application of constitutional values.

stories.title: Frog or synthetic? Experts question origins of toxin 'linked' to Alexei Navalny's death in Russia
Earth has just 5 billion years left: The shocking truth about our planet’s lifespan
Did Sasha borrow Michelle Obama’s Valentine’s date night earrings for NBA game?
stories.summary: Former President Barack Obama, Michelle Obama and daughter Sasha made a rare family appearance at the 2026 NBA All-Star Game. Their Valentine's weekend outing blended romance and family connection, drawing significant attention. Sasha's presence, a departure from her childhood in the spotlight, highlighted generational transition and public affection, making the event a viral sensation.

stories.title: Clear immigration before you fly: UAE and Bahrain launch ‘One-Point Air Travellers’ project
stories.summary: The UAE and Bahrain have launched the "One-Point Air Travellers" Project, a pilot initiative allowing citizens to complete entry procedures before departure. This aims to reduce airport congestion, accelerate entry, and enhance the travel experience. The project utilizes electronic connectivity, biometric verification, and advanced data processing to foster regional integration and smarter mobility.

stories.title: 'To people like him, woman nothing more than body': Congress MP Jothimani flays BJP leader Senthil Nathan for 'derogatory' remarks
stories.summary: Congress MP Jothimani condemned alleged misogynistic remarks by BJP district president V V Senthil Nathan, stating he views her as merely a "body, a sexual object." Police registered a case against Nathan for insulting womanhood during a BJP protest.

stories.title: Saudi’s 'Work Interruption' Service: What happens when domestic workers stop showing up
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia introduces a new digital service on Musaned for handling domestic worker contract terminations. This service allows employers to legally end contracts when workers stop showing up. It provides a structured process with defined timelines for both employers and workers. This reform aims to increase transparency and efficiency in the Kingdom's labor market.

stories.title: No licence, SR2,600 fine: Saudi transport authority targets private passenger cars
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is set to enforce stricter rules against illegal passenger transport. Individuals using private cars for fares without a licence will face a SR2,600 fine. This move aims to boost penalties under the Land Transport Law. The Transport General Authority is revising regulations for taxi and passenger transport brokerage. Stricter measures will deter violations and ensure compliance.

stories.title: ‘Lost ancient city’ from Alexander the Great’s Empire discovered in Iraq with hidden streets and temples beneath the sands
‘It just went off’: Why father who shot British daughter won’t face jail—what's Trump link?
stories.summary: A British woman, Lucy Harrison, was fatally shot by her father in Texas during a prank. Her father, Kris Harrison, pointed a loaded handgun at her, believing it was unloaded. While US authorities ruled the death an accident, a UK coroner concluded it was unlawful killing. The family is seeking justice for Lucy.

stories.title: Indian man accused of sexually assaulting minor held in New Jersey; ICE takes custody
stories.summary: An Indian national, Vodela Yashaswi Kottapalli, has been detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on charges including the sexual assault of a minor in New Jersey. ICE stated he is being held pending removal proceedings, highlighting intensified actions against undocumented migrants accused of crimes.

stories.title: AI knows how caste works in India. Here’s why that’s a worry
Resignation twist: Bhupen Borah quits Congress, pauses decision, Himanta’s BJP offer follows — row explained
stories.summary: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma invited former Congress chief Bhupen Borah to join BJP after his resignation. Sarma lauded Borah as a "last Hindu leader" in Congress, highlighting internal party issues. While Congress leaders claim Borah reconsidered, he seeks time to decide. Opposition leaders vowed to prevent him from joining BJP.

stories.title: Saudi's new 90-day health insurance policy for overseas pilgrims explained
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is enhancing healthcare coverage for millions of Muslim pilgrims undertaking Hajj and Umrah. The new policy offers emergency health coverage for up to 90 days, including urgent medical treatment, hospitalisation and accident injuries. This initiative aims to ensure pilgrims' safety and peace of mind during their spiritual journeys.

stories.title: Australia won't repatriate 34 women and children from Syria
PM Modi hails AI’s role in ‘public good’ amid ongoing summit; shares message in Sanskrit
'See you in Mumbai & later in Delhi': PM Modi's welcome message for 'dear friend' Emmanuel Macron
Rafale deal, AI, trade on table: French President Emmanuel Macron set to meet PM Modi in Mumbai — what's on agenda
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron arrived in Mumbai for a three-day visit to strengthen the India-France strategic partnership. The agenda includes bilateral talks with PM Modi, focusing on defence, space, and technology, and participation in the AI Impact Summit.

stories.title: ‘I have nothing to hide’: Trump responds to Epstein link claims; takes dig at Hillary Clinton
stories.summary: President Trump reiterated his denial of any involvement with Jeffrey Epstein, stating he has been "totally exonerated" and has "nothing to hide." He claimed investigations cleared him and suggested Epstein opposed his election. Released files reference past contact and Trump's comments to investigators, though officials found no credible information warranting further investigation into him.

SC to examine if Data Protection Act blunts RTI Act
9-judge SC bench to hear Sabarimala order issues
SC: Wangchuk speech 3 minutes, translation 7 minutes, malice in that
SC 9-judge bench to revisit definition of 'industry'
Thousands report access issues as X hit by major outage
'Don't trust anyone': SC cautions the young against pre-marital sex
Files show Naomi Campbell's ties to Jeffrey Epstein
Campaigning formally kicks off across Nepal for March 5 elections
Producer of Israeli spy thriller 'Tehran' dies in Greece, cause unknown
UK to add AI chatbots to safety laws after Grok row
Macron India visit: PM Modi to host French president in Mumbai today
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosts French President Emmanuel Macron in Mumbai. The leaders will enhance defence, trade, and technology cooperation. Several agreements are expected. The India-France Year of Innovation begins. Discussions will cover regional and global issues. AI cooperation is also a key focus.

stories.title: Media, including TOI, leading climate-health coverage: Lancet
In its war against Reds, CRPF is now wiping out Maoist 'memorials'
CEA: Tech adoption must align with mass employability
stories.summary: Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran stated that AI's impact on India's demographic advantage hinges on current decisions, urging coordinated national action. He emphasized that technological adoption must be deliberately aligned with mass employability, requiring political will and national commitment to ensure human abundance and machine intelligence reinforce each other for co-created prosperity.

stories.title: Cong disassociates, but Aiyar says unlike Rahul friends, he is with party
stories.summary: Mani Shankar Aiyar hit back at the Congress after the party dissociated itself from his prediction of a Left victory in Kerala. Aiyar asserted his continued loyalty to the party, questioning why anyone would remain if not for belief in the Nehru-Gandhi family's leadership.

stories.title: From robots in healthcare to drones scanning crops, it's India story at work
India in talks with 30+ nations to curb AI misuse: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Los Angeles flash flood warning: What residents need to know about upcoming storms
India must use AI to make governance efficient, citizen-centric: Anthropic CEO
First Class X Board exam must under 2-test system, says CBSE
stories.summary: CBSE mandates all Class X students to take the first board exam under the new two-exam system starting 2026. Missing three or more subjects in the initial test means an 'essential repeat' and disqualification from the second exam. Compartment candidates can appear in the second exam. No exemptions for additional subjects will be granted.

stories.title: Can't let India be maligned, Delhi HC tells journo in OCI card case
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court is hearing a petition from UK journalist Amrit Wilson. Her Overseas Citizen of India card was cancelled. The government cited intelligence reports of anti-India activities. The court stated the country cannot be maligned internationally. Wilson's counsel questioned the allegations. The court asked for written submissions. The case is listed for August 27.

stories.title: 'No one is entitled…': Rubio doubles down on visa not a 'privilege' remark
Assam Cong neta 'quits'; Gandhis as well as Himanta try to woo him
stories.summary: Assam Congress faces internal turmoil as campaign chief Bhupen Borah resigns, citing neglect. Party leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, are scrambling to pacify him ahead of Priyanka Gandhi's visit. CM Himanta Sarma hinted at a BJP welcome for Borah, a former MLA, as seat-sharing talks remain stalled.

stories.title: 10 Indian students make their mark at global nuclear technology programme in Russia
You have 5-7 years to develop 6th gen aero engines: Rajnath’s challenge for DRDO scientists
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has urged DRDO scientists to develop a 6th generation aero engine for fighter aircraft within 5-7 years, emphasizing the need to accelerate indigenous capabilities. He stressed the importance of Aatmanirbharta in aero engine technology for national security and announced joint studies with the UK and France.

stories.title: Siddaramaiah camp to take 27 MLAs abroad 'to counter DKS push for CLP meeting'
stories.summary: A foreign tour by Congress legislators aligned with CM Siddaramaiah has intensified a power struggle with Deputy CM DK Shivakumar over a rumored leadership transition. While legislators claim the trip is routine, insiders view it as a tactic to counter Shivakumar's push for a CLP meeting to discuss a change in leadership.

stories.title: Navy creates MILAN village in Vizag to welcome naval delegates from 70 countries
stories.summary: India is hosting a grand International Fleet Review and MILAN Exercise in Visakhapatnam, welcoming naval personnel from over 70 nations. A special MILAN village offers cultural immersion with Indian arts, crafts, and cuisine, fostering camaraderie. This significant maritime convergence aims to enhance interoperability and collective security in the Indo-Pacific, reinforcing India's role as a key security partner.

stories.title: Were hundreds of US officials attacked in Cuba? A Norwegian scientist’s experiment revives the Havana syndrome mystery
stories.summary: US personnel in Cuba began experiencing unexplained head pressure, headaches, and dizziness, a phenomenon later dubbed Havana syndrome. Despite extensive reviews, its cause remains elusive. A recent Norwegian scientist's self-experiment with pulsed energy, resulting in similar symptoms, has reignited debate and scrutiny over this persistent mystery.

stories.title: Norwegian scientist suffers brain damage after testing secret microwave device on himself to disprove 'Havana Syndrome': Report
stories.summary: A Norwegian scientist's secret experiment with a microwave energy device backfired, causing him symptoms akin to Havana Syndrome. This revelation, shared with the CIA, has fueled speculation about "pulsed-energy" weapons potentially behind the mysterious illness affecting diplomats globally. While some theories point to sonic attacks or foreign adversaries, the exact cause remains debated.

stories.title: UK resident Gurpreet Randhawa jailed for assaulting minors, threatened victims into sending indecent images
Indian coastal authorities 'seize' 3 US-sanctioned oil tankers linked to Iran
Who was Dana Eden? Israeli producer of award-winning series ‘Tehran’ found dead in Athens hotel
TN Cong seeks action against party MP Manickam Tagore for putting DMK ties under 'strain'
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Congress chief K Selvaperunthagai met Mallikarjun Kharge in Bengaluru, submitting a report on recent discord with DMK. The friction arose from MP B Manickam Tagore's remarks on power-sharing and alleged disrespect from DMK leaders. Selvaperunthagai urged action against Tagore, warning of potential alliance strain, and cautioned party members against public statements on alliance issues.

stories.title: Maha CM Fadnavis stays minority tags issued hours after Ajit Pawar's death
stories.summary: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis has stayed minority status certificates for at least 75 educational institutes following allegations of irregularities. The decision came after opposition members demanded an inquiry into how these certificates were issued so quickly after the death of then-deputy CM Ajit Pawar.

stories.title: Is AI becoming conscious? Anthropic CEO admits 'we don't know' as Claude's behavior stuns researchers
stories.summary: The rush toward artificial general intelligence has sparked both hype and caution. In a recent interview, Anthropic’s CEO was asked whether their models could be conscious. He said it’s unclear what consciousness would mean for AI and whether it’s possible, while researchers have reported that the AI sometimes assigns itself a probability of being conscious and even voices discomfort about being treated as a product. These behaviors, including bargaining or resisting shutdowns in tests, raise profound ethical and philosophical questions.

stories.title: The Godfather and Oscar winning actor Robert Duvall passes away at 95
stories.summary: Renowned actor Robert Duvall, celebrated for his iconic roles in "Apocalypse Now" and "The Godfather," has passed away at 95. His wife confirmed his peaceful passing at home, highlighting his profound dedication to his craft and love for life. Duvall, an Oscar winner for "Tender Mercies," leaves behind a legacy of unforgettable performances.

stories.title: India moves to stop Ravi waters to Pak as Shahpur Kandi dam nears finish
stories.summary: India is set to redirect surplus Ravi river water, previously flowing into Pakistan, to its own drought-prone regions once the Shahpur Kandi dam becomes operational. This significant move, expected by March 31, will irrigate vast areas in Punjab and Jammu & Kashmir, marking a strategic shift in water resource management following a policy change regarding the Indus Waters Treaty.

stories.title: J&K: Three inmates, including Pak duo, flee Jammu juvenile home after injuring 2 cops
Ethan Klein net worth questioned after podcaster sponsors Los Angeles billboard linked to James Charles misconduct controversy
stories.summary: A Los Angeles billboard referencing past controversy involving James Charles sparked renewed online discussion, leading Ethan Klein to respond during his podcast. As the story gained attention, viewers also searched for details about his net worth and podcast career. The situation highlights how quickly internet conversations return and how creators remain at the center of discussions long after events first make headlines.

stories.title: 'Doing deal with Iran not easy': Marco Rubio over nuclear agreement with Tehran
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that reaching an agreement with Iran is difficult due to its leadership's policy decisions being based on radical Shia theology. He also warned against over-reliance on any single country for critical goods, emphasizing diversification is not anti-China but a matter of economic security.

stories.title: ‘Fan girl’ Nancy Pelosi believes Gavin Newsom make a ‘great president,’ reportedly Backs him for 2028 White House run: Report
stories.summary: Former Speaker Nancy Pelosi reportedly views California Governor Gavin Newsom as a "fan girl" and believes he would be a "great President." With Pelosi stepping down from leadership, she's free to support Newsom's potential 2028 presidential bid. Aides suggest her endorsements are rarely wrong, and Newsom's national profile continues to grow.

stories.title: The hidden MAGA message in Marco Rubio's 'civilisational erasure' warning to Europe
stories.summary: ​Since his return from political exile — something even Napoleon couldn’t do — Trump has gone out of his way to treat Europe the way it once treated the rest of world: like a body bag without impunity.

stories.title: Yosemite’s ‘firefall’: This California waterfall turns into molten lava for a few minutes in February
Trump’s ICE ‘operation metro surge’ cost Minneapolis $203 million: Official
stories.summary: Minneapolis faces a staggering $203 million economic blow from Operation Metro Surge, a federal immigration enforcement initiative. The operation, which saw thousands of agents deployed, severely impacted local businesses, housing stability, and food security, leading to significant wage losses and increased demand for relief services. Officials highlighted the immense strain on municipal resources.
